module

public import KimiK3.Model
public import Mathlib.Data.Fin.VecNotation
public import TorchLean.NN.Softmax
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Algebra
public import TorchLean.Tensor.LinearAlgebra.Real
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Operations
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Reduce.Real
public import Mathlib.Geometry.Convex.ConvexSpace.Defs
public import Mathlib.Data.EReal.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Group.MinMax

/-!
# EAGLE-3 draft model and speculative sampling

Read three depth features from the target model, fuse them with a token embedding, and run
the draft transition. A separate finite-distribution calculation proves that accepted
proposal mass plus corrected rejection mass equals the target distribution. This probability
identity does not verify a deployed sampler's random-number generator or cache restoration.

Reference: Kimi K3 technical report, Section 2.5 and Sections 3--4, pp. 10--14.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace KimiK3

open TorchLean
open Tensor
open scoped BigOperators

namespace Draft

namespace Features

/-- Read the first, fourth, and final AttnRes block outputs named by the K3 report. The hypothesis
rules out applying the EAGLE-3 head before four block outputs exist. -/
def ofBlockState {hiddenDim : Nat} (state : AttnRes.BlockState ℝ hiddenDim)
    (hFour : 4 ≤ state.blockOutputs.length) : Tensor ℝ [3, hiddenDim] :=
  let outputs := state.blockOutputs
  have hFourOutputs : 4 ≤ outputs.length := by simpa [outputs] using hFour
  have hNonempty : outputs ≠ [] := List.ne_nil_of_length_pos (by omega)
  Tensor.dim ![outputs.get ⟨0, by omega⟩,
    outputs.get ⟨3, by omega⟩, outputs.getLast hNonempty]

end Features

namespace LanguageModel

/-- Extract the EAGLE-3 feature triplet for one token after a target-model forward pass.
Features come from that token's retained AttnRes state. -/
noncomputable def eagleFeaturesAt {cfg : TextConfig} {decayRank sequenceLength : Nat}
    (model : LanguageModel ℝ cfg decayRank)
    (embeddings : Tensor ℝ [sequenceLength, cfg.hiddenDim])
    (position : Fin sequenceLength)
    (hFour : 4 ≤ (model.forwardDepthStates embeddings position).blockOutputs.length) :
    Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim] :=
  Features.ofBlockState (model.forwardDepthStates embeddings position) hFour

end LanguageModel

namespace FeatureFusion

variable {hiddenDim : Nat}

/-- Multiplying a real vector by an all-zero square matrix gives the zero vector. -/
@[simp]
private theorem vecMatMul_fill_zero (values : Tensor ℝ [hiddenDim]) :
    Tensor.vecmat values (Tensor.zeros [hiddenDim, hiddenDim]) =
      Tensor.zeros [hiddenDim] := by
  apply Tensor.ext_vector
  intro column
  simp [Tensor.vecmat, Tensor.getScalar_contract_vecMat_eq_sum, Tensor.get2]

/-- Multiplying a real row vector by the identity matrix returns that vector. -/
@[simp]
private theorem vecMatMul_identity (values : Tensor ℝ [hiddenDim]) :
    Tensor.vecmat values (Tensor.identity hiddenDim) = values := by
  apply Tensor.ext_vector
  intro column
  simp [Tensor.vecmat, Tensor.getScalar_contract_vecMat_eq_sum, Tensor.get2_identity]

variable {α : Type} [Storage α] [Context α]

/-- Concatenate-and-project written as a sum of three matrix products. -/
def forward (fusion : Tensor α [3, hiddenDim, hiddenDim]) (features : Tensor α [3, hiddenDim]) :
    Tensor α [hiddenDim] :=
  Tensor.vecmat (features.unstack 0) (fusion.unstack 0) +
    Tensor.vecmat (features.unstack 1) (fusion.unstack 1) +
    Tensor.vecmat (features.unstack 2) (fusion.unstack 2)

/-- With the report's `[0 0 I]` initialization, fusion returns the high-level feature. -/
theorem initial_fusion_eq_high (features : Tensor ℝ [3, hiddenDim])
    (fusion : Tensor ℝ [3, hiddenDim, hiddenDim])
    (hLow : (Tensor.unstack fusion 0) = Tensor.zeros [hiddenDim, hiddenDim])
    (hMiddle : (Tensor.unstack fusion 1) = Tensor.zeros [hiddenDim, hiddenDim])
    (hHigh : (Tensor.unstack fusion 2) = Tensor.identity hiddenDim) :
    FeatureFusion.forward fusion features = (Tensor.unstack features 2) := by
  rw [forward, hLow, hMiddle, hHigh]
  rw [vecMatMul_fill_zero, vecMatMul_fill_zero, vecMatMul_identity]
  simp

end FeatureFusion

/-- One-layer MTP/EAGLE-3 draft head. Its two input matrices represent the bias-free linear map
applied to the concatenation of the current token embedding and fused target feature. The decoder
layer has the same KDA-or-MLA and channel-mixer structure as a backbone layer. -/
structure Model (cfg : TextConfig) (decayRank : Nat) where
  /-- Three-source feature-fusion projection. -/
  featureFusion : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim, cfg.hiddenDim]
  /-- Token embedding table shared with the draft input path. -/
  tokenEmbedding : Tensor ℝ [cfg.vocabSize, cfg.hiddenDim]
  /-- Projection applied to the current token embedding. -/
  tokenInputWeight : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim, cfg.hiddenDim]
  /-- Projection applied to the fused target-model feature. -/
  featureInputWeight : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim, cfg.hiddenDim]
  /-- Single causal decoder layer used by the draft model. -/
  decoderLayer : BackboneLayer ℝ cfg decayRank
  /-- Query used to read the draft layer's final AttnRes depth state. -/
  finalQuery : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim]
  /-- RMS-normalization scale before the vocabulary projection. -/
  finalNormScale : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim]
  /-- Projection from hidden states to draft-token logits. -/
  vocabularyHead : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim, cfg.vocabSize]
  vocabSize_pos : 0 < cfg.vocabSize
  activeExperts_le : cfg.activeExperts ≤ cfg.numRoutedExperts

namespace Model

variable {cfg : TextConfig} {decayRank : Nat}

/-- Form a draft decoder input from a token embedding and one already fused feature. The feature is
the target model's three-level fusion at the first training-time-test step and the preceding draft
hidden state at every later step. -/
noncomputable def inputFromFeature (model : Model cfg decayRank) (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize)
    (feature : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim]) : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim] :=
  Tensor.vecmat (Tensor.unstack model.tokenEmbedding token) model.tokenInputWeight +
    Tensor.vecmat feature model.featureInputWeight

/-- Form the first draft input by fusing the low-, middle-, and high-level target features. -/
noncomputable def input (model : Model cfg decayRank) (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize)
    (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim] :=
  model.inputFromFeature token (FeatureFusion.forward model.featureFusion features)

/-- Causal KDA or MLA state retained by the single draft decoder layer. -/
abbrev CausalState (model : Model cfg decayRank) :=
  model.decoderLayer.sequence.CausalState

/-- Empty causal state at the beginning of a draft window. -/
noncomputable def initialState (model : Model cfg decayRank) : model.CausalState :=
  model.decoderLayer.sequence.initialState

/-- Advance the draft decoder from one fused feature, returning the sequence-mixer state for the
next draft position and the normalized hidden state. -/
noncomputable def stepHiddenFromFeature (model : Model cfg decayRank) (state : model.CausalState)
    (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize) (feature : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    model.CausalState × Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim] :=
  let depthState := BackboneLayer.initialDepthState (model.inputFromFeature token feature)
  let result := model.decoderLayer.forwardToken model.activeExperts_le state depthState
  (result.1, RMSNorm.scale (result.2.retrieve model.finalQuery) model.finalNormScale)

/-- Advance the first draft position from target-model features. Later training-time-test positions
use `stepHiddenFromFeature` with the preceding draft hidden state. -/
noncomputable def stepHidden (model : Model cfg decayRank) (state : model.CausalState)
    (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    model.CausalState × Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim] :=
  model.stepHiddenFromFeature state token (FeatureFusion.forward model.featureFusion features)

/-- Run the first draft position from an empty causal state. -/
noncomputable def forwardHidden (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim] :=
  (model.stepHidden model.initialState token features).2

/-- Advance one causal draft position and return its next-token logits. -/
noncomputable def stepLogits (model : Model cfg decayRank) (state : model.CausalState)
    (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    model.CausalState × Tensor ℝ [cfg.vocabSize] :=
  let result := model.stepHidden state token features
  (result.1, Tensor.vecmat result.2 model.vocabularyHead)

/-- Advance one continuation position using the preceding draft hidden state as the feature
input. -/
noncomputable def stepLogitsFromFeature (model : Model cfg decayRank) (state : model.CausalState)
    (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize) (feature : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    model.CausalState ×
      (Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim] × Tensor ℝ [cfg.vocabSize]) :=
  let result := model.stepHiddenFromFeature state token feature
  (result.1, result.2, Tensor.vecmat result.2 model.vocabularyHead)

/-- Draft next-token logits. -/
noncomputable def logits (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    Tensor ℝ [cfg.vocabSize] :=
  (model.stepLogits model.initialState token features).2

/-- With the report's `[0 0 I]` initialization, the EAGLE-3 fused input equals the pretrained MTP
input built from the high-level feature alone. This is why the draft head can start from the MTP
layer. -/
theorem input_at_eagle_initialization (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim])
    (hLow : (Tensor.unstack model.featureFusion 0) =
      Tensor.zeros [cfg.hiddenDim, cfg.hiddenDim])
    (hMiddle : (Tensor.unstack model.featureFusion 1) =
      Tensor.zeros [cfg.hiddenDim, cfg.hiddenDim])
    (hHigh : (Tensor.unstack model.featureFusion 2) = Tensor.identity cfg.hiddenDim) :
    model.input token features =
      Tensor.vecmat (Tensor.unstack model.tokenEmbedding token) model.tokenInputWeight +
        Tensor.vecmat (Tensor.unstack features 2) model.featureInputWeight := by
  rw [input, inputFromFeature,
    FeatureFusion.initial_fusion_eq_high features model.featureFusion hLow hMiddle hHigh]

end Model

/-- A probability vector over the finite vocabulary, as a point of Mathlib's standard simplex. -/
abbrev Distribution (vocabSize : Nat) := Convexity.StdSimplex ℝ (Fin vocabSize)

namespace Distribution

/-- Interpret a nonempty vocabulary-logit vector as a probability distribution through TorchLean's
stable softmax specification. Positivity and normalization come from TorchLean's softmax
theorems, not from new assumptions. -/
noncomputable def ofLogits {vocabSize : Nat} (hVocab : 0 < vocabSize)
    (logits : Tensor ℝ [vocabSize]) : Distribution vocabSize := by
  cases vocabSize with
  | zero => omega
  | succ n =>
      let probabilities := Softmax.vec logits
      exact {
        weights := Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm (Tensor.getScalar probabilities)
        nonneg := fun token => by
          simpa using le_of_lt (Softmax.vec_pos logits token)
        total := by
          simpa [Finsupp.sum_fintype, probabilities, Tensor.sum_eq_coord_sum,
            Fintype.sum_prod_type, Tensor.getScalar_eq_apply] using Softmax.sum_vec logits }

end Distribution

/-- Target-model distribution at one sequence position, computed from the logits of the complete
K3 language backbone. -/
noncomputable def targetDistributionAt {cfg : TextConfig} {decayRank sequenceLength : Nat}
    (model : LanguageModel ℝ cfg decayRank)
    (embeddings : Tensor ℝ [sequenceLength, cfg.hiddenDim])
    (position : Fin sequenceLength) : Distribution cfg.vocabSize :=
  Distribution.ofLogits model.vocabSize_pos (Tensor.unstack (model.logits embeddings) position)

namespace Model

/-- Next-token distribution emitted by the EAGLE-3 draft head. -/
noncomputable def distribution (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    Distribution cfg.vocabSize :=
  Distribution.ofLogits model.vocabSize_pos (model.logits token features)

/-- Advance one causal draft position and return the normalized distribution used by lossless
speculative sampling. -/
noncomputable def stepDistribution (model : Model cfg decayRank) (state : model.CausalState)
    (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    model.CausalState × Distribution cfg.vocabSize :=
  let result := model.stepLogits state token features
  (result.1, Distribution.ofLogits model.vocabSize_pos result.2)

/-- Advance a continuation position and expose both the hidden feature fed into the next step and
the normalized token distribution. -/
noncomputable def stepDistributionFromFeature (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (state : model.CausalState) (token : Fin cfg.vocabSize)
    (feature : Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    model.CausalState ×
      (Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim] × Distribution cfg.vocabSize) :=
  let result := model.stepLogitsFromFeature state token feature
  (result.1, result.2.1, Distribution.ofLogits model.vocabSize_pos result.2.2)

end Model

/-- Lossless speculative-sampling acceptance rate `Σ_x min(p(x), q(x))`. -/
noncomputable def acceptanceRate {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) : ℝ :=
  ∑ token, min (target.weights token) (draft.weights token)

/-- Total-variation distance between target and draft next-token distributions. -/
noncomputable def totalVariation {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) : ℝ :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ∑ token, |target.weights token - draft.weights token|

/-- Swapping target and draft does not change speculative acceptance. -/
theorem acceptanceRate_comm {vocabSize : Nat} (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) :
    acceptanceRate target draft = acceptanceRate draft target := by
  simp only [acceptanceRate, min_comm]

/-- Total variation is nonnegative. -/
theorem totalVariation_nonneg {vocabSize : Nat} (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) :
    0 ≤ totalVariation target draft :=
  mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => abs_nonneg _)

/-- Acceptance rates lie in `[0, 1]`. -/
theorem acceptanceRate_mem_unitInterval {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) :
    0 ≤ acceptanceRate target draft ∧ acceptanceRate target draft ≤ 1 := by
  constructor
  · exact Finset.sum_nonneg (fun token _ =>
      le_min (target.nonneg token) (draft.nonneg token))
  · calc
      acceptanceRate target draft
          ≤ ∑ token, target.weights token :=
            Finset.sum_le_sum (fun token _ => min_le_left _ _)
      _ = 1 := target.total_of_fintype

/-- Speculative acceptance equals one minus the total-variation distance, so the Eq. 16 loss
`-log(acceptance)` depends on target and draft only through that distance. -/
theorem acceptanceRate_eq_one_sub_totalVariation {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) :
    acceptanceRate target draft = 1 - totalVariation target draft := by
  have htarget : ∑ token, target.weights token = 1 := by
    exact target.total_of_fintype
  have hdraft : ∑ token, draft.weights token = 1 := by
    exact draft.total_of_fintype
  have hpointwise : ∀ token : Fin vocabSize,
      min (target.weights token) (draft.weights token) =
        (target.weights token + draft.weights token - |target.weights token - draft.weights token|) / 2 := by
    intro token
    by_cases h : target.weights token ≤ draft.weights token
    · rw [min_eq_left h, abs_of_nonpos (sub_nonpos.mpr h)]
      ring_nf
    · have h' : draft.weights token ≤ target.weights token := le_of_not_ge h
      rw [min_eq_right h', abs_of_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr h')]
      ring_nf
  rw [acceptanceRate, totalVariation]
  simp_rw [hpointwise]
  rw [← Finset.sum_div]
  rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib,
    htarget, hdraft]
  ring_nf

/-- Speculative acceptance is perfect exactly when the draft and target distributions agree. -/
theorem acceptanceRate_eq_one_iff {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) :
    acceptanceRate target draft = 1 ↔ target = draft := by
  constructor
  · intro hAcceptance
    have hIdentity := acceptanceRate_eq_one_sub_totalVariation target draft
    rw [hAcceptance] at hIdentity
    have hVariation : totalVariation target draft = 0 := by linarith
    have hSum : ∑ token, |target.weights token - draft.weights token| = 0 := by
      rw [totalVariation] at hVariation
      linarith
    apply Convexity.StdSimplex.ext
    apply Finsupp.ext
    intro token
    have hCoordinate :
        |target.weights token - draft.weights token| = 0 :=
      (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg fun _ _ => abs_nonneg _).mp hSum token
        (Finset.mem_univ token)
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp (abs_eq_zero.mp hCoordinate)
  · rintro rfl
    rw [acceptanceRate]
    simp only [min_self]
    exact target.total_of_fintype

/-- Rejection probability: the target mass not shared with the draft. -/
noncomputable def residualMass {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) : ℝ :=
  1 - acceptanceRate target draft

/-- Unnormalized correction mass for one token after speculative rejection. -/
noncomputable def residualNumerator {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) (token : Fin vocabSize) : ℝ :=
  max 0 (target.weights token - draft.weights token)

/-- The positive part of `target - draft` is the target mass not covered by acceptance. -/
theorem residualNumerator_eq_sub_min {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) (token : Fin vocabSize) :
    residualNumerator target draft token =
      target.weights token - min (target.weights token) (draft.weights token) := by
  simpa only [residualNumerator, sub_self] using
    (max_sub_sub_left (target.weights token) (target.weights token) (draft.weights token))

/-- Correction numerators sum to the rejection probability. -/
theorem sum_residualNumerator {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) :
    ∑ token, residualNumerator target draft token = residualMass target draft := by
  have htarget : ∑ token, target.weights token = 1 := by
    exact target.total_of_fintype
  simp_rw [residualNumerator_eq_sub_min]
  rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, htarget]
  rfl

/-- Distribution sampled after a rejection, defined when target and draft differ (acceptance below
one). Its density is the normalized positive part of `target - draft`. -/
noncomputable def correctionDistribution {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize)
    (hReject : acceptanceRate target draft < 1) : Distribution vocabSize := by
  have hMass : 0 < residualMass target draft := by
    simpa [residualMass] using sub_pos.mpr hReject
  exact {
    weights := Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm
      (fun token => residualNumerator target draft token / residualMass target draft)
    nonneg := fun token => by
      simpa [residualNumerator] using
        div_nonneg (le_max_left 0 (target.weights token - draft.weights token)) hMass.le
    total := by
      simpa [Finsupp.sum_fintype, ← Finset.sum_div, sum_residualNumerator] using
        div_self (ne_of_gt hMass) }

/-- One-token speculative sampling is lossless. For every token, the mass accepted from the draft
plus the mass drawn from the rejection correction equals the target-model mass. -/
theorem accepted_add_corrected_eq_target {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize)
    (hReject : acceptanceRate target draft < 1) (token : Fin vocabSize) :
    min (target.weights token) (draft.weights token) +
        residualMass target draft *
          (correctionDistribution target draft hReject).weights token =
      target.weights token := by
  have hMass : residualMass target draft ≠ 0 := by
    apply ne_of_gt
    simpa [residualMass] using sub_pos.mpr hReject
  rw [correctionDistribution]
  change min (target.weights token) (draft.weights token) +
      residualMass target draft *
        (residualNumerator target draft token / residualMass target draft) =
    target.weights token
  rw [mul_div_cancel₀ _ hMass]
  rw [residualNumerator_eq_sub_min]
  ring

namespace Model

/-- State of EAGLE-3 training-time testing after target features have been fused once. The second
component is the draft hidden feature consumed by the following step. -/
abbrev TrainingTimeTestState (model : Model cfg decayRank) :=
  model.CausalState × Tensor ℝ [cfg.hiddenDim]

/-- Initial training-time-test state: an empty draft cache and the fused target-model feature. -/
noncomputable def initialTrainingTimeTestState (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) : model.TrainingTimeTestState :=
  (model.initialState, FeatureFusion.forward model.featureFusion features)

/-- One EAGLE-3 training-time-test transition. It consumes the current token and
feature, then stores its own hidden output as the feature for the next transition. No fresh
target-model feature is requested after initialization. -/
noncomputable def trainingTimeTestStep (model : Model cfg decayRank) :
    model.TrainingTimeTestState → Fin cfg.vocabSize →
      model.TrainingTimeTestState × Distribution cfg.vocabSize :=
  fun state token =>
    let result := model.stepDistributionFromFeature state.1 token state.2
    ((result.1, result.2.1), result.2.2)

/-- Run EAGLE-3 training-time testing over shifted training tokens, starting from the fused
target-model features. Kimi K3 supplies seven tokens. -/
noncomputable def trainingTimeTest (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (tokens : List (Fin cfg.vocabSize)) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    model.TrainingTimeTestState × List (Distribution cfg.vocabSize) :=
  CausalScan.run model.trainingTimeTestStep
    (model.initialTrainingTimeTestState features) tokens

/-- Training-time testing emits one draft distribution for every shifted training token. -/
theorem trainingTimeTest_length (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (tokens : List (Fin cfg.vocabSize)) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    (model.trainingTimeTest tokens features).2.length = tokens.length :=
  CausalScan.outputs_length model.trainingTimeTestStep
    (model.initialTrainingTimeTestState features) tokens

/-- Splitting a training-time-test token sequence into chunks does not change its final state or
draft distributions, so the seven reported steps can be replayed incrementally. -/
theorem trainingTimeTest_append (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (initialTokens remainingTokens : List (Fin cfg.vocabSize))
    (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    model.trainingTimeTest (initialTokens ++ remainingTokens) features =
      let first := model.trainingTimeTest initialTokens features
      let second := CausalScan.run model.trainingTimeTestStep first.1 remainingTokens
      (second.1, first.2 ++ second.2) := by
  exact CausalScan.run_append model.trainingTimeTestStep
    (model.initialTrainingTimeTestState features) initialTokens remainingTokens

/-- The seven draft distributions used by K3 fine-tuning. Indexing by `Fin 7` puts the reported
training-time-test depth into the type. -/
noncomputable def sevenStepDistributions (model : Model cfg decayRank)
    (tokens : Fin 7 → Fin cfg.vocabSize) (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) :
    Fin 7 → Distribution cfg.vocabSize := by
  let outputs := (model.trainingTimeTest (List.ofFn tokens) features).2
  have hLength : outputs.length = 7 := by
    rw [model.trainingTimeTest_length]
    simp
  exact fun step => outputs.get ⟨step.val, by rw [hLength]; exact step.isLt⟩

end Model

/-- Likelihood-based draft loss in Eq. 16.

The codomain is `EReal` because disjoint target and draft distributions have zero acceptance and
so infinite negative-log loss.  Lean's convention `Real.log 0 = 0` would hide that case.
-/
noncomputable def likelihoodLoss {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) : EReal :=
  if acceptanceRate target draft = 0 then ⊤
  else ((-Real.log (acceptanceRate target draft) : ℝ) : EReal)

/-- Likelihood loss is infinite exactly when the acceptance rate is zero. -/
theorem likelihoodLoss_eq_top_iff {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize) :
    likelihoodLoss target draft = ⊤ ↔ acceptanceRate target draft = 0 := by
  simp [likelihoodLoss]

/-- At positive acceptance, the extended loss agrees with the ordinary real negative log. -/
theorem likelihoodLoss_eq_neg_log_of_pos {vocabSize : Nat}
    (target draft : Distribution vocabSize)
    (hAcceptance : 0 < acceptanceRate target draft) :
    likelihoodLoss target draft =
      ((-Real.log (acceptanceRate target draft) : ℝ) : EReal) := by
  simp [likelihoodLoss, ne_of_gt hAcceptance]

namespace Model

/-- Kimi K3's seven-step EAGLE-3 objective against a frozen target language model. Each target
distribution comes from the target model at the corresponding training position, and each draft
distribution comes from the recurrent training-time-test pass. As in Eq. 16 of the report, there
is no auxiliary ground-truth cross-entropy term. -/
noncomputable def sevenStepLikelihoodLoss {targetDecayRank draftDecayRank sequenceLength : Nat}
    (target : LanguageModel ℝ cfg targetDecayRank) (draft : Model cfg draftDecayRank)
    (embeddings : Tensor ℝ [sequenceLength, cfg.hiddenDim])
    (positions : Fin 7 → Fin sequenceLength) (tokens : Fin 7 → Fin cfg.vocabSize)
    (features : Tensor ℝ [3, cfg.hiddenDim]) : EReal :=
  ∑ step : Fin 7,
    likelihoodLoss (targetDistributionAt target embeddings (positions step))
      (draft.sevenStepDistributions tokens features step)

end Model

end Draft

end KimiK3

module

public import TorchLean.NN.Optimizer.Muon
public import TorchLean.Tensor.OfFn

/-!
# Per-head Muon

Split a projection's output columns into head blocks, apply a supplied orthogonalizer to each
block, and reassemble the original layout. Split and merge laws prove this is a reversible
reindexing. Properties of the orthogonalized blocks come from the supplied orthogonalizer's
contract, so no particular iterative algorithm is proved correct here.

Reference: Kimi K3 technical report, Section 2.5 and Sections 3--4, pp. 10--14.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace KimiK3

open TorchLean
open Tensor

namespace PerHeadMuon

open TorchLean.Muon

/-- One momentum matrix for every attention head. -/
abbrev HeadMatrices (α : Type) [Storage α] (heads rows columns : Nat) :=
  Fin heads → MatrixTensor α rows columns

/-- Partition a projection matrix along its output-head axis.

For a matrix of shape `rows × (heads * columns)`, output column `(head, column)` belongs to the
`head`-th `rows × columns` block. Per-Head Muon uses this layout to treat the Q, K, and V momentum
buffers head by head.
-/
def split {α : Type} [Storage α] {heads rows columns : Nat}
    (momentum : MatrixTensor α rows (heads * columns)) :
    HeadMatrices α heads rows columns :=
  fun head => Tensor.matrix fun row column =>
    get2 momentum row (finProdFinEquiv (head, column))

/-- Reassemble per-head matrices into the original projection layout. -/
def merge {α : Type} [Storage α] {heads rows columns : Nat}
    (blocks : HeadMatrices α heads rows columns) :
    MatrixTensor α rows (heads * columns) :=
  Tensor.matrix fun row outputColumn =>
    let headColumn := finProdFinEquiv.symm outputColumn
    get2 (blocks headColumn.1) row headColumn.2

/-- Splitting and reassembling a projection momentum matrix preserves every entry. -/
theorem merge_split {α : Type} [Storage α] {heads rows columns : Nat}
    (momentum : MatrixTensor α rows (heads * columns)) :
    merge (split momentum) = momentum := by
  apply Tensor.Rep.ext
  rintro ⟨row, column, ⟨⟩⟩
  have h : get2 (merge (split momentum)) row column = get2 momentum row column := by
    simp only [merge, split, Tensor.matrix, Tensor.get2, Tensor.unstack_dim, Tensor.getScalar_ofFn,
      Prod.mk.eta, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
  simpa only [Tensor.get2_eq_apply] using h

/-- Reassembling and splitting an indexed head family returns the same family. -/
theorem split_merge {α : Type} [Storage α] {heads rows columns : Nat}
    (blocks : HeadMatrices α heads rows columns) :
    split (merge blocks) = blocks := by
  funext head
  apply Tensor.Rep.ext
  rintro ⟨row, column, ⟨⟩⟩
  have h : get2 (split (merge blocks) head) row column = get2 (blocks head) row column := by
    simp only [merge, split, Tensor.matrix, Tensor.get2, Tensor.unstack_dim, Tensor.getScalar_ofFn,
      Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
  simpa only [Tensor.get2_eq_apply] using h

/-- Orthogonalize every output-head block independently and restore the projection layout. -/
def orthogonalize {α : Type} [Storage α] {heads rows columns : Nat}
    (orthogonalizer : Orthogonalizer α [rows, columns])
    (momentum : MatrixTensor α rows (heads * columns)) :
    MatrixTensor α rows (heads * columns) :=
  merge fun head => orthogonalizer.apply (split momentum head)

/-- Splitting a Per-Head Muon direction recovers the independently orthogonalized head blocks. -/
theorem split_orthogonalize {α : Type} [Storage α] {heads rows columns : Nat}
    (orthogonalizer : Orthogonalizer α [rows, columns])
    (momentum : MatrixTensor α rows (heads * columns)) :
    split (orthogonalize orthogonalizer momentum) =
      fun head => orthogonalizer.apply (split momentum head) := by
  exact split_merge _

/-- With an exact orthogonalizer, every head block of the reassembled update has orthonormal
columns. -/
theorem orthogonalize_hasExactColumnGram {α : Type} [Storage α] [Context α]
    {heads rows columns : Nat}
    (orthogonalizer : Orthogonalizer α [rows, columns])
    (hExact : ∀ buffer : MatrixTensor α rows columns,
      ExactOrthogonalizesBuffer orthogonalizer buffer)
    (momentum : MatrixTensor α rows (heads * columns)) :
    ∀ head, HasExactColumnGram (split (orthogonalize orthogonalizer momentum) head) := by
  intro head
  rw [split_orthogonalize]
  exact hExact (split momentum head)

/-- An approximate orthogonalizer's Gram-residual bound carries over to every reassembled head. -/
theorem orthogonalize_hasApproxColumnGram {α : Type} [Storage α] [Context α]
    {heads rows columns : Nat} (epsilon : α)
    (orthogonalizer : Orthogonalizer α [rows, columns])
    (hApprox : ∀ buffer : MatrixTensor α rows columns,
      ApproxOrthogonalizesBuffer epsilon orthogonalizer buffer)
    (momentum : MatrixTensor α rows (heads * columns)) :
    ∀ head, HasApproxColumnGram epsilon
      (split (orthogonalize orthogonalizer momentum) head) := by
  intro head
  rw [split_orthogonalize]
  exact hApprox (split momentum head)

end PerHeadMuon

end KimiK3

/-!
# Masked next-token pretraining

Average the next-token loss over a nonempty set of supervised positions. Text targets can be
selected even when the input includes visual embeddings or padding. This file also states a
logit-gradient formula and proves its values on supervised and masked rows.

Reference: Kimi K3 technical report, Section 2.5 and Sections 3--4, pp. 10--14.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace KimiK3

open TorchLean
open Tensor
open scoped BigOperators

namespace Pretraining

/-- Negative log-likelihood of one target token, evaluated from unnormalized vocabulary logits. -/
noncomputable def tokenLoss {vocabSize : Nat}
    (logits : Tensor ℝ [vocabSize]) (target : Fin vocabSize) : ℝ :=
  -Tensor.getScalar (Tensor.logSoftmax logits ⟨0, Nat.one_pos⟩) target

/-- Mean next-token loss over the positions selected by `supervised`.

The model may receive both text and visual embeddings, but its targets are vocabulary tokens.
Visual input positions, padding, and input-only protocol tokens are left out of `supervised`, so
their entries in `targets` never reach the loss.
-/
noncomputable def nextTokenLoss {sequenceLength vocabSize : Nat}
    (logits : Tensor ℝ [sequenceLength, vocabSize])
    (targets : Fin sequenceLength → Fin vocabSize)
    (supervised : Finset (Fin sequenceLength)) (_hSupervised : supervised.Nonempty) : ℝ :=
  (∑ position ∈ supervised, tokenLoss (Tensor.unstack logits position) (targets position)) /
    supervised.card

/-- Closed-form logit-gradient formula for the masked next-token objective.

Rows omitted from `supervised` have zero gradient. A supervised row uses the standard
`softmax(logits) - oneHot(target)` derivative, divided by the number of supervised positions.

No theorem here proves that this is the derivative or VJP of `nextTokenLoss`.
-/
noncomputable def logitGradientFormula {sequenceLength vocabSize : Nat}
    (logits : Tensor ℝ [sequenceLength, vocabSize])
    (targets : Fin sequenceLength → Fin vocabSize)
    (supervised : Finset (Fin sequenceLength)) (_hSupervised : supervised.Nonempty) :
    Tensor ℝ [sequenceLength, vocabSize] :=
  Tensor.dim fun position =>
    if position ∈ supervised then
      Tensor.scale
        (Tensor.crossEntropyBackward .logits (Tensor.unstack logits position)
          (Tensor.oneHot vocabSize (targets position)) ⟨0, Nat.one_pos⟩ false)
        (1 / supervised.card)
    else
      Tensor.zeros [vocabSize]

/-- On every supervised position, the formula uses TorchLean's stable
cross-entropy-on-logits derivative, with the outer mean reduction applied. -/
theorem logitGradientFormula_at_supervised {sequenceLength vocabSize : Nat}
    (logits : Tensor ℝ [sequenceLength, vocabSize])
    (targets : Fin sequenceLength → Fin vocabSize)
    (supervised : Finset (Fin sequenceLength)) (hSupervised : supervised.Nonempty)
    (position : Fin sequenceLength) (hPosition : position ∈ supervised) :
    Tensor.unstack (logitGradientFormula logits targets supervised hSupervised) position =
      Tensor.scale
        (Tensor.crossEntropyBackward .logits (Tensor.unstack logits position)
          (Tensor.oneHot vocabSize (targets position)) ⟨0, Nat.one_pos⟩ false)
        (1 / supervised.card) := by
  simp only [logitGradientFormula, Tensor.unstack_dim, ite_eq_left hPosition]

/-- At every masked position the formula is zero. -/
theorem logitGradientFormula_at_masked {sequenceLength vocabSize : Nat}
    (logits : Tensor ℝ [sequenceLength, vocabSize])
    (targets : Fin sequenceLength → Fin vocabSize)
    (supervised : Finset (Fin sequenceLength)) (hSupervised : supervised.Nonempty)
    (position : Fin sequenceLength) (hPosition : position ∉ supervised) :
    Tensor.unstack (logitGradientFormula logits targets supervised hSupervised) position =
      Tensor.zeros [vocabSize] := by
  simp only [logitGradientFormula, Tensor.unstack_dim, ite_eq_right hPosition]

end Pretraining

namespace LanguageModel

/-- Evaluate the masked next-token objective on the logits of the complete language backbone, so
the pretraining loss belongs to a concrete model. -/
noncomputable def pretrainingLoss {cfg : TextConfig} {decayRank sequenceLength : Nat}
    (model : LanguageModel ℝ cfg decayRank)
    (embeddings : Tensor ℝ [sequenceLength, cfg.hiddenDim])
    (targets : Fin sequenceLength → Fin cfg.vocabSize)
    (supervised : Finset (Fin sequenceLength)) (hSupervised : supervised.Nonempty) : ℝ :=
  Pretraining.nextTokenLoss (model.logits embeddings) targets supervised hSupervised

end LanguageModel

end KimiK3

/-!
# MoonViT-V2 specification

Kimi K3 uses one vision encoder for images and videos. This file follows the released
`modeling_kimi_k3.py` (Hugging Face `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, revision `f831ab6`) rather than the
report's prose. Section 2.4 of the report says attention is factorized into intra-frame spatial and
inter-frame temporal passes. The released `MoonViTEncoderLayer` has one attention module, and it
attends jointly over all `t * h * w` patch tokens of a media item. The code is what runs, so the
code is what we specify.

One media item is a grid of `t × h × w` flattened patches with `t ≤ 4`. The released tower then
1. projects each patch with a bias-free `14 × 14` stride-`14` convolution, i.e. a linear map;
2. adds a learned `64 × 64` position table, bilinearly resized to `h × w`, and, when `t > 1`, a
   fixed sine-cosine frame embedding (`Learnable2DInterpPosEmbDivided_fixed`);
3. runs 27 pre-norm blocks. Each block applies RMSNorm, one packed `wqkv` projection, 2-D rotary
   position embedding on queries and keys (`Rope2DPosEmbRepeated`), non-causal scaled dot-product
   attention over the whole item, the output projection `wo`, and a residual; then RMSNorm, a
   bias-free MLP with the tanh GELU, and a residual (`MoonViTEncoderLayer`);
4. applies a final RMSNorm (`MoonViT3dEncoder.final_layernorm`);
5. averages the `t` frames and groups each `2 × 2` patch block into one token (`tpool_patch_merger`);
6. projects with two bias-free linear maps around the exact erf GELU, then RMSNorm with
   `ε = 10⁻⁵` (`PatchMergerMLPV2`).

Different media items never attend to each other (`cu_seqlens`), so a video longer than four frames
is a list of separate items, each pooled on its own. `forwardChunks` states this for a video cut
into equal chunks.

The input is an already extracted grid of flattened patches. Pixel decoding, resizing and patch
extraction belong to the data pipeline, outside the model equation.

Reference: Kimi Team, "Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence", 2026, Section 2.4, pp. 9--10,
https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653, and the released code above. Dimensions are recorded in
`KimiK3.paperConfig`.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace KimiK3

open TorchLean
open FloatLib.Numerics (MathFunctions)
open Tensor

namespace MoonViT

/-! ## Constants of the released vision tower -/

/-- Rows of the learned position table (`init_pos_emb_height`). -/
def positionRows : Nat := 64

/-- Columns of the learned position table (`init_pos_emb_width`). -/
def positionColumns : Nat := 64

/-- Frames per media item (`init_pos_emb_time`). The position embedding asserts `t ≤ 4`. -/
def maxFrames : Nat := 4

/-- Base of the sine-cosine frame embedding and of the 2-D rotary embedding. -/
def positionBase : Nat := 10000

/-- `nn.RMSNorm(hidden_dim)` inside the encoder leaves `eps` unset. PyTorch then uses the float32
machine epsilon `2⁻²³` for float32, bfloat16 and float16 inputs (`aten/src/ATen/native/
layer_norm.cpp`, `rms_norm_composite`, and the fused CUDA kernel in `layer_norm_kernel.cu`). -/
def encoderNormEpsilon {α : Type} [RatCast α] : α :=
  Rat.cast (1 / 8388608 : Rat)

/-! ## Patch grids, position tables, and rotary tables -/

/-- A video/image patch grid with axes `(frame, row, column, feature)`. -/
abbrev Grid (α : Type) [Storage α] (frames rows columns features : Nat) :=
  Tensor α [frames, rows, columns, features]

section Tables

variable {α : Type} [Storage α] [Context α]

/-- Weight of source coordinate `a` in output coordinate `i` for PyTorch's
`F.interpolate(mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)` along one axis of length `source`, resized to
`target`.

PyTorch reads the source coordinate `(i + 1/2) * source / target - 1/2`, clamped below at `0`,
interpolates between its floor and the next index, and repeats the last index at the border.
Here the source coordinate is `numerator / denominator`, and natural subtraction performs the
clamp. -/
def interpolationWeight (source target i a : Nat) : α :=
  let numerator := (2 * i + 1) * source - target
  let denominator := 2 * target
  let lower := numerator / denominator
  let upper := if lower + 1 < source then lower + 1 else lower
  let fraction : α := ((numerator % denominator : Nat) : α) / ((denominator : Nat) : α)
  (if a = lower then 1 - fraction else 0) + (if a = upper then fraction else 0)

/-- One-axis bilinear resize matrix, from `source` positions to `target` positions. -/
def interpolationMatrix (source target : Nat) : Tensor α [target, source] :=
  Tensor.dim fun i => Tensor.dim fun a => Tensor.scalar (interpolationWeight source target i a)

/-- Bilinear resize of a `sourceRows × sourceColumns` table to `rows × columns`.

Bilinear interpolation is separable: the row matrix acts on the first axis and the column matrix on
the second. This is what `get_rope_shape` computes with `F.interpolate` after moving the feature axis
to the front. -/
def resizeTable {sourceRows sourceColumns rows columns width : Nat}
    (rowWeights : Tensor α [rows, sourceRows])
    (columnWeights : Tensor α [columns, sourceColumns])
    (table : Tensor α [sourceRows, sourceColumns, width]) :
    Tensor α [rows, columns, width] :=
  have hFlat : Shape.size [sourceRows, sourceColumns, width] =
      Shape.size [sourceRows, sourceColumns * width] := by
    simp [Shape.size]
  have hUnflat : Shape.size [rows, sourceColumns * width] =
      Shape.size [rows, sourceColumns, width] := by
    simp [Shape.size]
  let alongRows : Tensor α [rows, sourceColumns, width] :=
    Tensor.reshape (Tensor.matmul rowWeights (Tensor.reshape table _ hFlat)) _ hUnflat
  Tensor.dim fun row => Tensor.matmul columnWeights (Tensor.unstack alongRows row)

/-- Frequency `1 / base ^ (index / half)` of the sine-cosine frame embedding. -/
def frameFrequency (width index : Nat) : α :=
  1 / (positionBase : α) ^ ((index : α) / ((width / 2 : Nat) : α))

/-- The fixed buffer `time_weight`: `get_1d_sincos_pos_embed(width, maxFrames)`.

Frame `f` stores `sin (f * ω_k)` in its first `width / 2` coordinates and `cos (f * ω_k)` in the
rest. -/
def frameTable (width : Nat) : Tensor α [maxFrames, width] :=
  Tensor.dim fun frame => Tensor.dim fun k => Tensor.scalar <|
    if k.val < width / 2 then
      MathFunctions.sin ((frame.val : α) * frameFrequency width k.val)
    else
      MathFunctions.cos ((frame.val : α) * frameFrequency width (k.val - width / 2))

/-- Frame embedding added to a `frames`-frame item: nothing for one frame, otherwise the first
`frames` rows of `frameTable`. The released code takes `time_weight[0:t]` only when `t > 1`. -/
def frameEmbedding (frames width : Nat) (hFrames : frames ≤ maxFrames) :
    Tensor α [frames, width] :=
  if frames = 1 then
    Tensor.full [frames, width] 0
  else
    Tensor.dim fun frame =>
      Tensor.unstack (frameTable width) ⟨frame.val, lt_of_lt_of_le frame.isLt hFrames⟩

/-- Rotary angle of head coordinate `coordinate` at patch position `(row, column)`.

`Rope2DPosEmbRepeated` stores `headDim / 2` complex rotations per position. Rotation `j` acts on
the coordinate pair `(2j, 2j + 1)`. Even rotations follow the column, odd rotations the row, and
both use the frequency `base ^ (-4i / headDim)` with `i = j / 2`. Frames share their rotations
(`repeat(t, 1)`). -/
def ropeAngle (headDim row column coordinate : Nat) : α :=
  let rotation := coordinate / 2
  let position : Nat := if rotation % 2 = 0 then column else row
  (position : α) / (positionBase : α) ^ (((4 * (rotation / 2) : Nat) : α) / (headDim : α))

/-- Per-token rotary table `f (angle)` for a `frames × rows × columns` item, laid out over all
heads. Token `p` sits at row `(p % (rows * columns)) / columns` and column `p % columns`. The
released code tabulates these angles for rows and columns up to `512` and asserts that bound. -/
def ropeTable (f : α → α) (frames rows columns heads headDim : Nat) :
    Tensor α [frames * rows * columns, heads * headDim] :=
  Tensor.dim fun token => Tensor.dim fun k => Tensor.scalar <|
    f (ropeAngle headDim ((token.val % (rows * columns)) / columns) (token.val % columns)
      (k.val % headDim))

/-- Fixed matrix sending each coordinate pair `(x₀, x₁)` to `(-x₁, x₀)`. -/
def pairRotation (width : Nat) : Tensor α [width, width] :=
  Tensor.dim fun m => Tensor.dim fun k => Tensor.scalar <|
    if k.val % 2 = 0 ∧ m.val = k.val + 1 then -1
    else if m.val % 2 = 0 ∧ k.val = m.val + 1 then 1
    else 0

/-- Rotary embedding `x ⊙ cos + (x R) ⊙ sin`.

On every pair this is the complex product `(x₀ + i x₁) * (cos θ + i sin θ)` computed by
`apply_rope` (see `applyRope_even` and `applyRope_odd`). -/
def applyRope {tokens width : Nat} (cosTable sinTable input : Tensor α [tokens, width]) :
    Tensor α [tokens, width] :=
  Tensor.zipWith (· + ·) (Tensor.zipWith (· * ·) input cosTable)
    (Tensor.zipWith (· * ·) (Tensor.matmul input (pairRotation width)) sinTable)

/-- Patch embedding with its resize matrices and frame rows supplied: the projected patches, plus
the resized learned table at every frame, plus the frame row at every patch. -/
def embedPatches {frames rows columns patchFeatures sourceRows sourceColumns hidden : Nat}
    (patchWeight : Tensor α [patchFeatures, hidden])
    (positionWeight : Tensor α [sourceRows, sourceColumns, hidden])
    (rowWeights : Tensor α [rows, sourceRows])
    (columnWeights : Tensor α [columns, sourceColumns])
    (frameRows : Tensor α [frames, hidden])
    (patches : Grid α frames rows columns patchFeatures) :
    Grid α frames rows columns hidden :=
  let projected := einsum patches, patchWeight
    "frame row column pixel, pixel feature -> frame row column feature"
  let spatial := Tensor.repeatLeading frames (resizeTable rowWeights columnWeights positionWeight)
  let temporal := Tensor.dim fun frame =>
    Tensor.repeatLeading rows (Tensor.repeatLeading columns (Tensor.unstack frameRows frame))
  projected + spatial + temporal

/-- RMSNorm of every row with a supplied epsilon. -/
def normRows {rowCount width : Nat} (hWidth : 0 < width) (epsilon : α)
    (input : Tensor α [rowCount, width]) (gamma : Tensor α [width]) :
    Tensor α [rowCount, width] :=
  Tensor.mapLeading [rowCount] (RMSNorm.scalePositive hWidth · gamma epsilon) input

end Tables

/-! ## What the tables compute -/

section TableTheorems

/-- At an even head coordinate, `x R` reads minus the partner coordinate. -/
theorem get2_matMul_pairRotation_even {tokens width : Nat} (x : Tensor ℝ [tokens, width])
    (token : Fin tokens) (j : Nat) (hj : 2 * j + 1 < width) :
    Tensor.get2 (Tensor.matmul x (pairRotation width)) token ⟨2 * j, by omega⟩ =
      -Tensor.get2 x token ⟨2 * j + 1, hj⟩ := by
  rw [Tensor.get2_matmul_eq_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single ⟨2 * j + 1, hj⟩]
  · simp [pairRotation]
  · intro m _ hm
    have hm' : m.val ≠ 2 * j + 1 := fun h => hm (Fin.ext h)
    simp only [pairRotation, Tensor.get2_dim]
    split_ifs with h₁ h₂ <;> first | omega | simp
  · simp

/-- At an odd head coordinate, `x R` reads the partner coordinate. -/
theorem get2_matMul_pairRotation_odd {tokens width : Nat} (x : Tensor ℝ [tokens, width])
    (token : Fin tokens) (j : Nat) (hj : 2 * j + 1 < width) :
    Tensor.get2 (Tensor.matmul x (pairRotation width)) token ⟨2 * j + 1, hj⟩ =
      Tensor.get2 x token ⟨2 * j, by omega⟩ := by
  rw [Tensor.get2_matmul_eq_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single ⟨2 * j, by omega⟩]
  · simp [pairRotation]
  · intro m _ hm
    have hm' : m.val ≠ 2 * j := fun h => hm (Fin.ext h)
    simp only [pairRotation, Tensor.get2_dim]
    split_ifs with h₁ h₂ <;> first | omega | simp
  · simp

/-- First coordinate of a rotated pair: the real part of `(x₀ + i x₁)(cos θ + i sin θ)`. -/
theorem applyRope_even {tokens width : Nat} (cosTable sinTable x : Tensor ℝ [tokens, width])
    (token : Fin tokens) (j : Nat) (hj : 2 * j + 1 < width) :
    Tensor.get2 (applyRope cosTable sinTable x) token ⟨2 * j, by omega⟩ =
      Tensor.get2 x token ⟨2 * j, by omega⟩ * Tensor.get2 cosTable token ⟨2 * j, by omega⟩ -
        Tensor.get2 x token ⟨2 * j + 1, hj⟩ * Tensor.get2 sinTable token ⟨2 * j, by omega⟩ := by
  rw [applyRope, Tensor.get2_zipWith, Tensor.get2_zipWith, Tensor.get2_zipWith,
    get2_matMul_pairRotation_even x token j hj]
  ring

/-- Second coordinate of a rotated pair: the imaginary part of `(x₀ + i x₁)(cos θ + i sin θ)`. -/
theorem applyRope_odd {tokens width : Nat} (cosTable sinTable x : Tensor ℝ [tokens, width])
    (token : Fin tokens) (j : Nat) (hj : 2 * j + 1 < width) :
    Tensor.get2 (applyRope cosTable sinTable x) token ⟨2 * j + 1, hj⟩ =
      Tensor.get2 x token ⟨2 * j + 1, hj⟩ * Tensor.get2 cosTable token ⟨2 * j + 1, hj⟩ +
        Tensor.get2 x token ⟨2 * j, by omega⟩ * Tensor.get2 sinTable token ⟨2 * j + 1, hj⟩ := by
  rw [applyRope, Tensor.get2_zipWith, Tensor.get2_zipWith, Tensor.get2_zipWith,
    get2_matMul_pairRotation_odd x token j hj]

/-- Both coordinates of a pair inside one head share their rotary angle. -/
theorem ropeAngle_pair (headDim row column j : Nat) (hEven : 2 ∣ headDim) :
    (ropeAngle headDim row column ((2 * j) % headDim) : ℝ) =
      ropeAngle headDim row column ((2 * j + 1) % headDim) := by
  have hPair : (2 * j) % headDim / 2 = (2 * j + 1) % headDim / 2 := by
    obtain ⟨half, rfl⟩ := hEven
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos half with h | h
    · subst h
      simp only [Nat.mul_zero, Nat.mod_zero]
      omega
    · have hLow : j % half < half := Nat.mod_lt j h
      have hSplit : 2 * j + 1 = (2 * (j % half) + 1) + 2 * half * (j / half) := by
        have := Nat.mod_add_div j half
        rw [Nat.mul_assoc]
        omega
      have hOdd : (2 * j + 1) % (2 * half) = 2 * (j % half) + 1 := by
        rw [hSplit, Nat.add_mul_mod_self_left, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by omega)]
      rw [Nat.mul_mod_mul_left 2 j half, hOdd]
      omega
  simp only [ropeAngle, hPair]

/-- The patch at row `0`, column `0` is not rotated. -/
@[simp] theorem ropeAngle_origin (headDim coordinate : Nat) :
    (ropeAngle headDim 0 0 coordinate : ℝ) = 0 := by
  simp [ropeAngle]

/-- A single frame receives no frame embedding, as in the released `if t == 1` branch. -/
theorem frameEmbedding_one {α : Type} [Storage α] [Context α] (width : Nat)
    (hFrames : 1 ≤ maxFrames) :
    (frameEmbedding 1 width hFrames : Tensor α [1, width]) = Tensor.full [1, width] 0 := by
  simp [frameEmbedding]

/-- Resizing an axis to its own length is the identity. This is why the released code may skip
`F.interpolate` when the patch grid is already `64 × 64`. -/
theorem interpolationWeight_self (n i a : Nat) (hi : i < n) :
    (interpolationWeight n n i a : ℝ) = if a = i then 1 else 0 := by
  have hn : 0 < 2 * n := by omega
  have hNumerator : (2 * i + 1) * n - n = 2 * n * i := by
    rw [Nat.add_mul, one_mul, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    ring
  have hLower : 2 * n * i / (2 * n) = i := Nat.mul_div_cancel_left i hn
  have hRemainder : 2 * n * i % (2 * n) = 0 := Nat.mul_mod_right (2 * n) i
  simp only [interpolationWeight, hNumerator, hLower, hRemainder]
  split_ifs <;> simp_all

/-- Entries of the resize matrix for an axis kept at its own length. -/
theorem get2_interpolationMatrix_self (n : Nat) (i a : Fin n) :
    Tensor.get2 (interpolationMatrix n n : Tensor ℝ [n, n]) i a = if a = i then 1 else 0 := by
  simp only [interpolationMatrix, Tensor.get2_dim]
  rw [interpolationWeight_self n i a i.isLt]
  simp [Fin.ext_iff]

end TableTheorems

/-! ## Encoder blocks -/

/-- Bias-free two-layer MLP (`MLP2` with `linear_bias = false`). -/
structure MLP (α : Type) [Storage α] (inputDim hiddenDim outputDim : Nat) where
  /-- `fc0.weight`, transposed. -/
  inputWeight : Tensor α [inputDim, hiddenDim]
  /-- `fc1.weight`, transposed. -/
  outputWeight : Tensor α [hiddenDim, outputDim]

/-- Parameters of one `MoonViTEncoderLayer`: the six released tensors of a block. -/
structure Block (α : Type) [Storage α] (heads hiddenDim headDim intermediateDim : Nat) where
  /-- `norm0.weight`, the RMSNorm scale before attention. -/
  attentionNormScale : Tensor α [hiddenDim]
  /-- `wqkv.weight`, transposed. Output columns are `(q | k | v)`, each laid out head-major. -/
  qkvWeight : Tensor α [hiddenDim, 3 * (heads * headDim)]
  /-- `wo.weight`, transposed. -/
  outputWeight : Tensor α [heads * headDim, hiddenDim]
  /-- `norm1.weight`, the RMSNorm scale before the MLP. -/
  feedForwardNormScale : Tensor α [hiddenDim]
  /-- `mlp.fc0.weight` and `mlp.fc1.weight`. -/
  feedForward : MLP α hiddenDim intermediateDim hiddenDim

namespace Block

variable {α : Type} [Storage α] [Context α]
variable {heads hiddenDim headDim intermediateDim tokens : Nat}

/-- Split the packed projection `x · wqkv` into queries, keys and values, as
`view(..., 3, heads, headDim)` followed by `unbind(dim=-3)`. -/
def splitQKV (packed : Tensor α [tokens, 3 * (heads * headDim)]) :
    Tensor α [3, tokens, heads * headDim] :=
  have hSize : Shape.size [tokens, 3 * (heads * headDim)] =
      Shape.size [tokens, 3, heads * headDim] := by
    simp [Shape.size]
  let tokenMajor := Tensor.reshape packed [tokens, 3, heads * headDim] hSize
  tokenMajor.permute (Shape.adjacentSwap _ 0) [3, tokens, heads * headDim]

/-- Self-attention of one media item: packed projection, 2-D RoPE on queries and keys, non-causal
scaled dot-product attention in every head, and the output projection. -/
def attention (block : Block α heads hiddenDim headDim intermediateDim)
    (cosTable sinTable : Tensor α [tokens, heads * headDim])
    (input : Tensor α [tokens, hiddenDim]) (_hTokens : tokens ≠ 0) :
    Tensor α [tokens, hiddenDim] :=
  let packed := splitQKV (Tensor.matmul input block.qkvWeight)
  let query := applyRope cosTable sinTable (Tensor.unstack packed 0)
  let key := applyRope cosTable sinTable (Tensor.unstack packed 1)
  let value := Tensor.unstack packed 2
  let queryHeads := MultiHeadAttention.splitHeads query heads headDim rfl
  let keyHeads := MultiHeadAttention.splitHeads key heads headDim rfl
  let valueHeads := MultiHeadAttention.splitHeads value heads headDim rfl
  let scale := 1 / (if headDim = 0 then 1 else Context.sqrtNat headDim)
  let attended := Tensor.attention (batch := [heads]) queryHeads keyHeads valueHeads scale
  Tensor.matmul (MultiHeadAttention.combineHeads attended) block.outputWeight

/-- Bias-free MLP with PyTorch's tanh GELU (`PytorchGELUTanh`). -/
def feedForwardPass (feedForward : MLP α hiddenDim intermediateDim hiddenDim)
    (input : Tensor α [tokens, hiddenDim]) : Tensor α [tokens, hiddenDim] :=
  Tensor.matmul (Tensor.map Activation.geluTanh (Tensor.matmul input feedForward.inputWeight))
    feedForward.outputWeight

/-- `MoonViTEncoderLayer.forward`: two pre-norm residual branches. -/
def forward (block : Block α heads hiddenDim headDim intermediateDim)
    (epsilon : α) (cosTable sinTable : Tensor α [tokens, heads * headDim])
    (input : Tensor α [tokens, hiddenDim]) (hTokens : tokens ≠ 0) (hHidden : 0 < hiddenDim) :
    Tensor α [tokens, hiddenDim] :=
  let attended := Tensor.zipWith (· + ·) input
    (block.attention cosTable sinTable (normRows hHidden epsilon input block.attentionNormScale)
      hTokens)
  Tensor.zipWith (· + ·) attended
    (feedForwardPass block.feedForward
      (normRows hHidden epsilon attended block.feedForwardNormScale))

end Block

/-- `PatchMergerMLPV2`: two bias-free linear maps around the exact GELU, then RMSNorm. -/
structure Projector (α : Type) [Storage α] (mergedDim textDim : Nat) where
  /-- `mm_projector.proj.0.weight`, transposed. -/
  firstWeight : Tensor α [mergedDim, mergedDim]
  /-- `mm_projector.proj.2.weight`, transposed. -/
  secondWeight : Tensor α [mergedDim, textDim]
  /-- `mm_projector.post_norm.weight`. -/
  outputNormScale : Tensor α [textDim]

/-- Parameters of MoonViT-V2 and its projector: the released vision tensors. -/
structure Model (α : Type) [Storage α] (cfg : VisionConfig) (patchFeatures : Nat) where
  /-- `patch_embed.proj.weight` flattened over `(channel, y, x)` and transposed. -/
  patchWeight : Tensor α [patchFeatures, cfg.hiddenDim]
  /-- `patch_embed.pos_emb.weight`. -/
  positionWeight : Tensor α [positionRows, positionColumns, cfg.hiddenDim]
  /-- Ordered encoder blocks. -/
  blocks : List (Block α cfg.numHeads cfg.hiddenDim
    (cfg.qkvHiddenDim / cfg.numHeads) cfg.intermediateDim)
  /-- The parameter list contains exactly the configured number of blocks. -/
  blocks_length : blocks.length = cfg.numLayers
  /-- `encoder.final_layernorm.weight`. -/
  finalNormScale : Tensor α [cfg.hiddenDim]
  /-- Projector into the language width. -/
  projector : Projector α (cfg.mergeHeight * cfg.mergeWidth * cfg.hiddenDim) cfg.textHiddenDim

namespace Model

variable {α : Type} [Storage α] [Context α]
variable {cfg : VisionConfig}
variable {patchFeatures frames rows columns : Nat}

/-- Patch projection plus the resized position table and the frame embedding
(`MoonVision3dPatchEmbed.forward`). -/
def embed (model : Model α cfg patchFeatures)
    (patches : Grid α frames rows columns patchFeatures) (hFrames : frames ≤ maxFrames) :
    Grid α frames rows columns cfg.hiddenDim :=
  embedPatches model.patchWeight model.positionWeight
    (interpolationMatrix positionRows rows) (interpolationMatrix positionColumns columns)
    (frameEmbedding frames cfg.hiddenDim hFrames) patches

/-- Run all configured blocks over one item's token sequence, then the final RMSNorm. -/
def encode (model : Model α cfg patchFeatures) {tokens : Nat}
    (cosTable sinTable : Tensor α [tokens, cfg.numHeads * (cfg.qkvHiddenDim / cfg.numHeads)])
    (input : Tensor α [tokens, cfg.hiddenDim])
    (hTokens : tokens ≠ 0) (hHidden : 0 < cfg.hiddenDim) :
    Tensor α [tokens, cfg.hiddenDim] :=
  let hidden := model.blocks.foldl
    (fun hidden block => block.forward encoderNormEpsilon cosTable sinTable hidden hTokens hHidden)
    input
  normRows hHidden encoderNormEpsilon hidden model.finalNormScale

/-- With zero configured blocks, the encoder is only its final RMSNorm. -/
theorem encode_of_numLayers_eq_zero (model : Model α cfg patchFeatures) {tokens : Nat}
    (cosTable sinTable : Tensor α [tokens, cfg.numHeads * (cfg.qkvHiddenDim / cfg.numHeads)])
    (input : Tensor α [tokens, cfg.hiddenDim])
    (hTokens : tokens ≠ 0) (hHidden : 0 < cfg.hiddenDim) (hLayers : cfg.numLayers = 0) :
    model.encode cosTable sinTable input hTokens hHidden =
      normRows hHidden encoderNormEpsilon input model.finalNormScale := by
  have hLength : model.blocks.length = 0 := by simpa [hLayers] using model.blocks_length
  have hBlocks : model.blocks = [] := List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp hLength
  simp [encode, hBlocks]

omit [Context α] in
/-- A positive configured depth forces the model to contain at least one MoonViT block. -/
theorem blocks_ne_nil (model : Model α cfg patchFeatures)
    (hLayers : 0 < cfg.numLayers) : model.blocks ≠ [] := by
  intro hBlocks
  have hLength := model.blocks_length
  simp [hBlocks] at hLength
  omega

/--
Temporal pooling, pixel-shuffle merge, and projection into the language width
(`tpool_patch_merger` followed by `PatchMergerMLPV2`). The output sequence has one token for each
merged spatial location, and the frame axis is pooled away.
-/
def mergeAndProject [Erf α] (model : Model α cfg patchFeatures)
    (grid : Grid α frames (rows * cfg.mergeHeight) (columns * cfg.mergeWidth) cfg.hiddenDim)
    (_hFrames : 0 < frames)
    (hText : 0 < cfg.textHiddenDim) :
    Tensor α [rows * columns, cfg.textHiddenDim] :=
  let pooled : Tensor α [rows * cfg.mergeHeight, columns * cfg.mergeWidth, cfg.hiddenDim] :=
    Tensor.mean grid [⟨0, by simp⟩] false
  let interleavedShape : Shape :=
    [rows, cfg.mergeHeight, columns, cfg.mergeWidth, cfg.hiddenDim]
  let groupedShape : Shape :=
    [rows, columns, cfg.mergeHeight, cfg.mergeWidth, cfg.hiddenDim]
  let mergedDim := cfg.mergeHeight * cfg.mergeWidth * cfg.hiddenDim
  let mergedShape : Shape := [rows * columns, mergedDim]
  have hInterleaved :
      Shape.size [rows * cfg.mergeHeight, columns * cfg.mergeWidth, cfg.hiddenDim] =
        Shape.size interleavedShape := by
    simp [interleavedShape, Shape.size, Nat.mul_assoc]
  have hMerged : Shape.size groupedShape = Shape.size mergedShape := by
    simp [groupedShape, mergedShape, mergedDim, Shape.size, Nat.mul_assoc]
  let interleaved := Tensor.reshape pooled _ hInterleaved
  let grouped := interleaved.permute (Shape.adjacentSwap interleavedShape 1) groupedShape (by
    rw [Shape.permute_adjacentSwap])
  let merged := Tensor.reshape grouped _ hMerged
  let hidden := Tensor.gelu (Tensor.matmul merged model.projector.firstWeight)
  let projected := Tensor.matmul hidden model.projector.secondWeight
  RMSNorm.rows hText projected model.projector.outputNormScale

/-- Complete reference path for one media item: from flattened patches of at most four frames to
language-width visual tokens. -/
def forward [Erf α] (model : Model α cfg patchFeatures)
    (patches : Grid α frames (rows * cfg.mergeHeight) (columns * cfg.mergeWidth) patchFeatures)
    (hFrames : 0 < frames) (hMaxFrames : frames ≤ maxFrames)
    (hSpatial : 0 < (rows * cfg.mergeHeight) * (columns * cfg.mergeWidth))
    (hHidden : 0 < cfg.hiddenDim) (hText : 0 < cfg.textHiddenDim) :
    Tensor α [rows * columns, cfg.textHiddenDim] :=
  let height := rows * cfg.mergeHeight
  let width := columns * cfg.mergeWidth
  let tokens := frames * height * width
  have hGridTokens : Shape.size [frames, height, width, cfg.hiddenDim] =
      Shape.size [tokens, cfg.hiddenDim] := by
    simp [tokens, Shape.size, Nat.mul_assoc]
  have hTokens : tokens ≠ 0 := by
    have hPositive : 0 < frames * (height * width) := Nat.mul_pos hFrames hSpatial
    simpa [tokens, height, width, Nat.mul_assoc] using Nat.ne_of_gt hPositive
  let heads := cfg.numHeads
  let headDim := cfg.qkvHiddenDim / cfg.numHeads
  let sequence := Tensor.reshape (model.embed patches hMaxFrames) _ hGridTokens
  let encoded := model.encode
    (ropeTable MathFunctions.cos frames height width heads headDim)
    (ropeTable MathFunctions.sin frames height width heads headDim)
    sequence hTokens hHidden
  model.mergeAndProject (Tensor.reshape encoded _ hGridTokens.symm) hFrames hText

/-- A video given as `chunks` items of `frames` frames each. Items never attend to each other, so
each chunk is encoded and pooled on its own. Its visual tokens form one row of the result. -/
def forwardChunks [Erf α] (model : Model α cfg patchFeatures) {chunks : Nat}
    (video : Tensor α
      [chunks, frames, rows * cfg.mergeHeight, columns * cfg.mergeWidth, patchFeatures])
    (hFrames : 0 < frames) (hMaxFrames : frames ≤ maxFrames)
    (hSpatial : 0 < (rows * cfg.mergeHeight) * (columns * cfg.mergeWidth))
    (hHidden : 0 < cfg.hiddenDim) (hText : 0 < cfg.textHiddenDim) :
    Tensor α [chunks, rows * columns, cfg.textHiddenDim] :=
  Tensor.dim fun chunk =>
    model.forward (Tensor.unstack video chunk) hFrames hMaxFrames hSpatial hHidden hText

/-- Each chunk's tokens depend only on that chunk. -/
@[simp] theorem get_forwardChunks [Erf α] (model : Model α cfg patchFeatures) {chunks : Nat}
    (video : Tensor α
      [chunks, frames, rows * cfg.mergeHeight, columns * cfg.mergeWidth, patchFeatures])
    (hFrames : 0 < frames) (hMaxFrames : frames ≤ maxFrames)
    (hSpatial : 0 < (rows * cfg.mergeHeight) * (columns * cfg.mergeWidth))
    (hHidden : 0 < cfg.hiddenDim) (hText : 0 < cfg.textHiddenDim) (chunk : Fin chunks) :
    Tensor.unstack (model.forwardChunks video hFrames hMaxFrames hSpatial hHidden hText) chunk =
      model.forward (Tensor.unstack video chunk) hFrames hMaxFrames hSpatial hHidden hText := by
  simp [forwardChunks]

end Model

module

public import Nemotron.Architecture.Schedule
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Shape
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega

/-!
# Shapes, projection partitions, and cache payloads

Table 1 (report p. 4) and the released BF16 config give the dimensions below. For the Mamba
input projection partition, see `NemotronHMamba2Mixer.__init__`, lines 384–421 of:
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c8b25ab3af135bcfd9496eff3ef507303da17f15/src/transformers/models/nemotron_h/modeling_nemotron_h.py

Payload counts cover one main-model sequence, not all the memory a serving system uses. They
leave out convolution history, scales, allocator padding, batch size, MTP caches, and rollback or
prefix snapshots. §4.5 (pp. 44–46) compares FP32 SSM storage to FP8 KV storage. An FP32 cache
(the BF16 config's default) and the deployed quantized model's FP16 stochastic cache are
different operating points, not conflicting claims about one configuration.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.Architecture

open TorchLean

/-- A recurrent layer stores one matrix per head, independent of sequence length. -/
def ssmShape (heads headDim stateDim : Nat) : Shape := [heads, headDim, stateDim]

/-- One attention layer stores keys and values for every preceding token. -/
def kvShape (tokens kvHeads headDim : Nat) : Shape := [2, kvHeads, tokens, headDim]

/-- SSM payload bytes for the recurrent blocks of an arbitrary hybrid schedule. -/
def ssmBytes (schedule : List BlockKind) (heads headDim stateDim bytesPerScalar : Nat) : Nat :=
  schedule.count .mamba * (ssmShape heads headDim stateDim).size * bytesPerScalar

/-- KV payload bytes for the attention blocks of an arbitrary hybrid schedule. -/
def kvBytes (schedule : List BlockKind) (tokens kvHeads headDim bytesPerScalar : Nat) : Nat :=
  schedule.count .attention * (kvShape tokens kvHeads headDim).size * bytesPerScalar

/-- Each head contributes one headDim-by-stateDim matrix. -/
theorem ssmShape_size (heads headDim stateDim : Nat) :
    (ssmShape heads headDim stateDim).size = heads * headDim * stateDim := by
  simp [ssmShape, Shape.size, Nat.mul_assoc]

/-- Keys and values give the leading factor of two. -/
theorem kvShape_size (tokens kvHeads headDim : Nat) :
    (kvShape tokens kvHeads headDim).size = 2 * kvHeads * tokens * headDim := by
  simp [kvShape, Shape.size, Nat.mul_assoc]

/-- KV bytes add over a split of the token count. -/
theorem kvBytes_add_tokens (schedule : List BlockKind)
    (tokens more kvHeads headDim bytesPerScalar : Nat) :
    kvBytes schedule (tokens + more) kvHeads headDim bytesPerScalar =
      kvBytes schedule tokens kvHeads headDim bytesPerScalar +
        kvBytes schedule more kvHeads headDim bytesPerScalar := by
  simp only [kvBytes, kvShape_size]
  ring

/-- SSM bytes add over concatenated stacks, whatever their layer order. -/
theorem ssmBytes_append (left right : List BlockKind)
    (heads headDim stateDim bytesPerScalar : Nat) :
    ssmBytes (left ++ right) heads headDim stateDim bytesPerScalar =
      ssmBytes left heads headDim stateDim bytesPerScalar +
        ssmBytes right heads headDim stateDim bytesPerScalar := by
  simp [ssmBytes, List.count_append, Nat.add_mul]

/-- Channels convolved together: expanded values, grouped B, and grouped C. -/
def mambaConvChannels (heads headDim groups stateDim : Nat) : Nat :=
  heads * headDim + 2 * groups * stateDim

/-- Input projection width: a gate, the convolved channels, and one time step per head. -/
def mambaInputWidth (heads headDim groups stateDim : Nat) : Nat :=
  heads * headDim + mambaConvChannels heads headDim groups stateDim + heads

/-- Splitting as the source does, `[gate, x, B, C, dt]`, leaves no remainder. -/
theorem mambaInputWidth_partition (heads headDim groups stateDim : Nat) :
    mambaInputWidth heads headDim groups stateDim =
      heads * headDim + heads * headDim + groups * stateDim + groups * stateDim + heads := by
  simp only [mambaInputWidth, mambaConvChannels]
  ring

/-- Routed-expert parameters: two matrices per non-gated expert, both on the latent dimension.
Router, shared expert, and latent projections are not counted. -/
def routedExpertParameters (experts latentDim innerDim : Nat) : Nat :=
  (Shape.size [experts, innerDim, latentDim]) + (Shape.size [experts, latentDim, innerDim])

/-- Each routed expert contributes an up projection and a down projection of equal size. -/
theorem routedExpertParameters_eq (experts latentDim innerDim : Nat) :
    routedExpertParameters experts latentDim innerDim = 2 * experts * latentDim * innerDim := by
  simp [routedExpertParameters, Shape.size]
  ring

/-- A latent dimension of 2048 instead of 8192 makes the routed-expert matrices four times
smaller. Because of the added latent projections and the shared expert, neither the MoE layer
nor the model shrinks fourfold. -/
theorem released_routed_parameter_ratio :
    4 * routedExpertParameters 512 2048 5120 = routedExpertParameters 512 8192 5120 := by
  decide +kernel

/-- Released dimensions agree with the value expansion, B/C grouping, and attention projections. -/
theorem released_projection_dimensions :
    256 * 64 = 2 * 8192 ∧
    mambaConvChannels 256 64 8 128 = 18432 ∧
    mambaInputWidth 256 64 8 128 = 35072 ∧
    64 * 128 = 8192 ∧
    2 * 128 = 256 := by
  decide +kernel

/-- Exactly 384 MiB of FP32 recurrent payload and 6144 bytes of FP8 KV payload per token. -/
theorem released_cache_payloads (tokens : Nat) :
    ssmBytes releasedSchedule 256 64 128 4 = 402653184 ∧
    kvBytes releasedSchedule tokens 2 128 1 = 6144 * tokens := by
  have hc := releasedSchedule_counts
  simp [ssmBytes, kvBytes, ssmShape_size, kvShape_size, hc.1, hc.2.1]
  ring

/-- FP8 KV payload stays at or below the FP32 recurrent payload up to 64 Ki tokens, where the
two are equal. -/
theorem released_fp32_fp8_crossover (tokens : Nat) :
    kvBytes releasedSchedule tokens 2 128 1 ≤ ssmBytes releasedSchedule 256 64 128 4 ↔
      tokens ≤ 65536 := by
  rw [(released_cache_payloads tokens).1, (released_cache_payloads tokens).2]
  omega

/-- Moving the recurrent payload to FP16 halves its crossover to 32 Ki tokens. -/
theorem released_fp16_fp8_crossover (tokens : Nat) :
    kvBytes releasedSchedule tokens 2 128 1 ≤ ssmBytes releasedSchedule 256 64 128 2 ↔
      tokens ≤ 32768 := by
  rw [(released_cache_payloads tokens).2]
  have hc := releasedSchedule_counts.1
  norm_num [ssmBytes, ssmShape_size, hc]
  omega

end Nemotron.Architecture

module

public import Nemotron.SSM
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Layers.Activation
import TorchLean.NN.Gradients.Activation
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum

/-!
# Grouped Mamba-2 coefficient preparation

Builds the prepared inputs of `Nemotron.SSM` from the grouped recurrence in the model source.
TorchLean's own `SelectiveMamba` is a different architecture and is not used for Ultra. Source,
pinned at the inspected revision:
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c8b25ab3af135bcfd9496eff3ef507303da17f15/src/transformers/models/nemotron_h/modeling_nemotron_h.py

`mamba2_selective_state_update` (lines 191–249) expands each B/C group across contiguous heads,
uses `exp(dt*A)`, writes `state*dA + (dt*B)*x`, reads that new state against C, and adds D*x.
`NemotronHMamba2Mixer` sets `A = -exp(A_log)` (line 461) and supplies softplus time steps.
Chunked prefill also clamps each time step below at `time_step_min` (lines 275, 394,
574), and the decode update has no clamp. `Parameters.timeStepMin` selects either path.

Inputs arrive *after* input projection and causal convolution, as values, B, C, and raw
time-step logits. This module covers discretization, contiguous grouping, the state update, and
the D skip. It omits convolution state, grouped gated RMS normalization, output
projection, padding, finite casts, and native kernels. All theorems are exact-real statements
for fixed prepared inputs. Like the source, `step` reads the new state before any storage cast,
so quantizing the cache does not change the readout.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.Architecture.Mamba2

open TorchLean

/-- Contiguous group assignment, as expand-then-reshape gives in the source. Writing the head
count as `groups * headsPerGroup` builds in divisibility. -/
def groupIndex {groups headsPerGroup : Nat} (hHeadsPerGroup : 0 < headsPerGroup)
    (head : Fin (groups * headsPerGroup)) : Fin groups :=
  ⟨head.val / headsPerGroup, (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hHeadsPerGroup).mpr head.isLt⟩

/-- Per-head mixer parameters, fixed across tokens. -/
structure Parameters (heads : Nat) where
  logA : Tensor ℝ [heads]
  dtBias : Tensor ℝ [heads]
  skip : Tensor ℝ [heads]
  /-- Lower time-step limit: `time_step_min` (0.001 in the released configuration) for the
  chunked path, or `0` for the decode update, which has no clamp. -/
  timeStepMin : ℝ

/-- One token after projection and convolution. B and C stay per group, not copied per head. -/
structure Token (groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim : Nat) where
  value : Tensor ℝ [groups * headsPerGroup, headDim]
  B : Tensor ℝ [groups, stateDim]
  C : Tensor ℝ [groups, stateDim]
  rawDt : Tensor ℝ [groups * headsPerGroup]

/-- Unit-scale softplus of `raw + bias` (TorchLean's branch-stable real definition), then the
source's lower clamp. PyTorch's large-input threshold branch and finite precision are not
modeled. -/
noncomputable def timeStep (minimum raw bias : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  max (Activation.softplus (raw + bias)) minimum

private theorem softplus_pos (x : ℝ) : 0 < Activation.softplus x := by
  rw [Activation.softplus_eq_log_one_add_exp]
  exact Real.log_pos (lt_add_of_pos_right 1 (Real.exp_pos _))

theorem timeStep_pos (minimum raw bias : ℝ) : 0 < timeStep minimum raw bias :=
  lt_max_of_lt_left (softplus_pos _)

/-- Without a positive floor the clamp does nothing: this is the decode path's plain softplus. -/
theorem timeStep_of_nonpos (minimum raw bias : ℝ) (hminimum : minimum ≤ 0) :
    timeStep minimum raw bias = Activation.softplus (raw + bias) :=
  max_eq_left (hminimum.trans (softplus_pos _).le)

/-- Per-head decay `exp(delta * A)` with the source's `A = -exp(logA)`. -/
noncomputable def retention (delta logA : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.exp (-(delta * Real.exp logA))

/-- For a nonnegative time step the decay lies in `(0, 1]`, whatever the learned log-rate, so
discretization never expands the prior state. -/
theorem retention_bounds (delta logA : ℝ) (hdelta : 0 ≤ delta) :
    0 < retention delta logA ∧ retention delta logA ≤ 1 := by
  constructor
  · exact Real.exp_pos _
  · apply Real.exp_le_one_iff.mpr
    exact neg_nonpos.mpr (mul_nonneg hdelta (Real.exp_nonneg _))

/-- Prepared SSM input for one head, where the time step scales B but not C. -/
noncomputable def prepareHead {groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim : Nat}
    (hHeadsPerGroup : 0 < headsPerGroup)
    (parameters : Parameters (groups * headsPerGroup))
    (input : Token groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim)
    (head : Fin (groups * headsPerGroup)) : SSM.Input ℝ headDim stateDim :=
  let delta := timeStep parameters.timeStepMin (input.rawDt.getScalar head)
    (parameters.dtBias.getScalar head)
  let group := groupIndex hHeadsPerGroup head
  { retention := retention delta (parameters.logA.getScalar head)
    value := Tensor.unstack input.value head
    write := Tensor.scale (Tensor.unstack input.B group) delta
    read := Tensor.unstack input.C group }

/-- Every prepared head has retention at most `1` in absolute value. -/
theorem prepareHead_bounded {groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim : Nat}
    (hHeadsPerGroup : 0 < headsPerGroup)
    (parameters : Parameters (groups * headsPerGroup))
    (input : Token groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim)
    (head : Fin (groups * headsPerGroup)) :
    |(prepareHead hHeadsPerGroup parameters input head).retention| ≤ 1 := by
  have hb := retention_bounds
    (timeStep parameters.timeStepMin (input.rawDt.getScalar head)
      (parameters.dtBias.getScalar head))
    (parameters.logA.getScalar head) (timeStep_pos _ _ _).le
  simpa only [prepareHead, abs_of_pos hb.1] using hb.2

/-- Coordinatewise, the update is the source's scalar Mamba-2 equation
`state * dA + x * (B * dt)`. -/
theorem updateHead_apply {groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim : Nat}
    (hHeadsPerGroup : 0 < headsPerGroup)
    (parameters : Parameters (groups * headsPerGroup))
    (input : Token groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim)
    (head : Fin (groups * headsPerGroup)) (state : SSM.State ℝ headDim stateDim)
    (valueIndex : Fin headDim) (stateIndex : Fin stateDim) :
    SSM.update state (prepareHead hHeadsPerGroup parameters input head)
        (valueIndex, stateIndex, PUnit.unit) =
      let delta := timeStep parameters.timeStepMin (input.rawDt.getScalar head)
        (parameters.dtBias.getScalar head)
      state (valueIndex, stateIndex, PUnit.unit) * retention delta (parameters.logA.getScalar head) +
        (Tensor.unstack input.value head).getScalar valueIndex *
          ((Tensor.unstack input.B (groupIndex hHeadsPerGroup head)).getScalar stateIndex * delta) := by
  simp [SSM.update, prepareHead, Tensor.scale, Tensor.matrix, Tensor.getScalar_eq_apply]

/-- Update every head's state matrix with its own prepared input, reusing `SSM.update`. -/
noncomputable def updateHeads {groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim : Nat}
    (hHeadsPerGroup : 0 < headsPerGroup)
    (parameters : Parameters (groups * headsPerGroup))
    (input : Token groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim)
    (state : Tensor ℝ [groups * headsPerGroup, headDim, stateDim]) :
    Tensor ℝ [groups * headsPerGroup, headDim, stateDim] :=
  Tensor.dim fun head => SSM.update (Tensor.unstack state head)
    (prepareHead hHeadsPerGroup parameters input head)

/-- One mixer step: update every head, read the new state against C, and add the D skip. -/
noncomputable def step {groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim : Nat}
    (hHeadsPerGroup : 0 < headsPerGroup)
    (parameters : Parameters (groups * headsPerGroup))
    (state : Tensor ℝ [groups * headsPerGroup, headDim, stateDim])
    (input : Token groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim) :
    Tensor ℝ [groups * headsPerGroup, headDim, stateDim] ×
      Tensor ℝ [groups * headsPerGroup, headDim] :=
  let next := updateHeads hHeadsPerGroup parameters input state
  (next, Tensor.dim fun head =>
    Tensor.matvec (Tensor.unstack next head)
      (Tensor.unstack input.C (groupIndex hHeadsPerGroup head)) +
      Tensor.scale (Tensor.unstack input.value head) (parameters.skip.getScalar head))

/-- One update over all heads does not increase a coordinate error in the prior state, since
every prepared retention is at most `1`. Both sides use the same token and parameters. -/
theorem updateHeads_within {groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim : Nat}
    (hHeadsPerGroup : 0 < headsPerGroup)
    (parameters : Parameters (groups * headsPerGroup))
    (input : Token groups headsPerGroup headDim stateDim)
    (x y : Tensor ℝ [groups * headsPerGroup, headDim, stateDim])
    (e : ℝ) (hxy : Cache.Within e x y) :
    Cache.Within e (updateHeads hHeadsPerGroup parameters input x)
      (updateHeads hHeadsPerGroup parameters input y) := by
  intro coordinate
  have hhead : Cache.Within e (Tensor.unstack x coordinate.1)
      (Tensor.unstack y coordinate.1) := by
    intro inner
    simpa [Tensor.unstack] using hxy (coordinate.1, inner)
  have hnext := SSM.update_within (Tensor.unstack x coordinate.1)
    (Tensor.unstack y coordinate.1)
    (prepareHead hHeadsPerGroup parameters input coordinate.1) 1 e (by norm_num)
    (prepareHead_bounded hHeadsPerGroup parameters input coordinate.1) hhead
  simpa [updateHeads, Tensor.dim, Tensor.dim] using hnext coordinate.2

end Nemotron.Architecture.Mamba2

module

public import Mathlib.Data.List.Count
