import Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega

/-!
# The released Ultra block schedule

Figure 2 and Table 1 of the Ultra report (pp. 3–4) describe a 108-block hybrid stack. Each
entry is a residual block containing one mixer, not a pair of mixer and feed-forward blocks.
`releasedSchedule` transcribes `layers_block_type` from the released BF16 configuration:
https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-BF16/blob/77df655d5e9f8362164ed14dd8b48f8bce657498/config.json#L19-L128

MTP is separate. Its stored shared head is attention followed by MoE, and the report's two MTP
heads share those parameters (§2.1, p. 3; §2.7, p. 12 counts 2 MTP blocks).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.Architecture

/-- The three mixer kinds in the main Ultra stack. -/
inductive BlockKind where
  | mamba
  | attention
  | moe
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq, ReflBEq, LawfulBEq, Repr

/-- Main-model residual blocks in execution order, without MTP. -/
def releasedSchedule : List BlockKind := [
  .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .attention, .moe,
  .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .attention, .moe, .mamba, .moe,
  .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .attention, .moe, .mamba, .moe,
  .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .attention, .moe, .mamba, .moe,
  .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .attention, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe,
  .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .attention, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe,
  .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .attention, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe,
  .mamba, .attention, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe,
  .mamba, .attention, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe,
  .mamba, .attention, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .attention,
  .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .attention,
  .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe, .mamba, .moe]

/-- Zero-based indices of the global-attention anchors. -/
def attentionPositions : List Nat :=
  (releasedSchedule.zipIdx.filter (fun entry => entry.1 == .attention)).map Prod.snd

/-- 108 residual blocks in the main stack. -/
theorem releasedSchedule_length : releasedSchedule.length = 108 := by decide +kernel

/-- Block counts: 48 Mamba, 12 attention, and 48 MoE. -/
theorem releasedSchedule_counts :
    releasedSchedule.count .mamba = 48 ∧
    releasedSchedule.count .attention = 12 ∧
    releasedSchedule.count .moe = 48 := by decide +kernel

/-- Zero-based positions of the twelve attention blocks in the configuration list. -/
theorem attentionPositions_eq :
    attentionPositions = [7, 14, 23, 32, 39, 48, 57, 64, 73, 82, 89, 98] := by
  decide +kernel

/-- In any schedule the three counts add up to the length, with no hidden feed-forward layer. -/
theorem counts_partition (schedule : List BlockKind) :
    schedule.count .mamba + schedule.count .attention + schedule.count .moe =
      schedule.length := by
  induction schedule with
  | nil => simp
  | cons kind rest ih =>
      cases kind <;> simp_all <;> omega

/-- The stored MTP head, reused rather than copied for each training application. -/
def mtpSchedule : List BlockKind := [.attention, .moe]

end Nemotron.Architecture

module

public import Nemotron.Cache.Replay
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Context.Real
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Datatype
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Ring.Abs
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# Errors at the checkpoint sites

Coordinate error bounds that separate recurrence sensitivity from state-storage error. Both
runs see the same prepared inputs, so a change in logits or in the sampled tokens is outside the
comparison. Rounding inside a transition belongs to `step`, and comparing against exact-real
arithmetic also needs local arithmetic-error bounds.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.Cache

open TorchLean KimiK3

/-- Every coordinate of `x` is within `error` of `y` (vacuous when a dimension is empty). -/
def Within {shape : Shape} (error : ℝ) (x y : Tensor ℝ shape) : Prop :=
  ∀ coordinate, |x coordinate - y coordinate| ≤ error

/-- A tensor is within `0` of itself. -/
theorem within_self {shape : Shape} (x : Tensor ℝ shape) : Within 0 x x := by
  intro coordinate
  simp

/-- Triangle inequality for `Within`: the allowances add. -/
theorem within_triangle {shape : Shape} {x y z : Tensor ℝ shape} {a b : ℝ}
    (hxy : Within a x y) (hyz : Within b y z) : Within (a + b) x z := by
  intro coordinate
  calc
    |x coordinate - z coordinate| =
        |(x coordinate - y coordinate) + (y coordinate - z coordinate)| := by
      congr 1
      ring
    _ ≤ |x coordinate - y coordinate| + |y coordinate - z coordinate| := abs_add_le _ _
    _ ≤ a + b := add_le_add (hxy coordinate) (hyz coordinate)

/-- A per-token sensitivity `L` becomes `L ^ inputs.length` over a whole scan. Only the
recurrent state is bounded, so the outputs can have any type. -/
theorem scan_state_within {shape : Shape} {Input Output : Type}
    (step : Tensor ℝ shape → Input → Tensor ℝ shape × Output) (L : ℝ)
    (hstep : ∀ input e x y, Within e x y → Within (L * e) (step x input).1 (step y input).1)
    (inputs : List Input) (x y : Tensor ℝ shape) (e : ℝ) (hxy : Within e x y) :
    Within (L ^ inputs.length * e)
      (CausalScan.run step x inputs).1 (CausalScan.run step y inputs).1 := by
  induction inputs generalizing x y e with
  | nil => simpa [CausalScan.run] using hxy
  | cons input rest ih =>
      have hnext := ih (step x input).1 (step y input).1 (L * e) (hstep input e x y hxy)
      simpa [CausalScan.run, pow_succ, mul_assoc, mul_left_comm, mul_comm] using hnext

/-- Error budget of a chunked run: each chunk scales the error by `L ^ chunk.length`, then its
write adds `δ`. -/
def checkpointBudget {Input : Type} (L δ : ℝ) : ℝ → List (List Input) → ℝ
  | e, [] => e
  | e, chunk :: rest => checkpointBudget L δ (L ^ chunk.length * e + δ) rest

/-- Each state this execution writes is stored within `δ`. A floating format has no single
absolute bound over every tensor value, so the bound is asked only of the written states. -/
def WritesWithin {shape : Shape} {Input Output : Type}
    (step : Tensor ℝ shape → Input → Tensor ℝ shape × Output)
    (quantize : Tensor ℝ shape → Tensor ℝ shape) (δ : ℝ) :
    Tensor ℝ shape → List (List Input) → Prop
  | _, [] => True
  | state, chunk :: rest =>
      let next := (CausalScan.run step state chunk).1
      Within δ (quantize next) next ∧ WritesWithin step quantize δ (quantize next) rest

/-- Storage bounds at the written states give an error bound for any checkpoint partition.
Sensitivity is paid per token and `δ` once per checkpoint. -/
theorem quantizedChunks_within_of_writes {shape : Shape} {Input Output : Type}
    (step : Tensor ℝ shape → Input → Tensor ℝ shape × Output)
    (quantize : Tensor ℝ shape → Tensor ℝ shape) (L δ : ℝ)
    (hstep : ∀ input e x y, Within e x y → Within (L * e) (step x input).1 (step y input).1)
    (chunks : List (List Input)) (x y : Tensor ℝ shape) (e : ℝ) (hxy : Within e x y)
    (hwrites : WritesWithin step quantize δ x chunks) :
    Within (checkpointBudget L δ e chunks)
      (quantizedChunks step quantize x chunks) (CausalScan.run step y chunks.flatten).1 := by
  induction chunks generalizing x y e with
  | nil => simpa [quantizedChunks, checkpointBudget, CausalScan.run] using hxy
  | cons chunk rest ih =>
      simp only [WritesWithin] at hwrites
      -- First propagate the old error through the chunk, then pay for its one storage write.
      have hscan := scan_state_within step L hstep chunk x y e hxy
      have hwrite := within_triangle hwrites.1 hscan
      have hwrite' : Within (L ^ chunk.length * e + δ)
          (quantize (CausalScan.run step x chunk).1) (CausalScan.run step y chunk).1 := by
        simpa [add_comm] using hwrite
      -- Both executions resume from their own resulting state with the same remaining inputs.
      have hrest := ih (quantize (CausalScan.run step x chunk).1)
        (CausalScan.run step y chunk).1 (L ^ chunk.length * e + δ) hwrite' hwrites.2
      simpa only [quantizedChunks, checkpointBudget, List.flatten_cons,
        CausalScan.run_append] using hrest

/-- Same bound, from a quantizer that is within `δ` everywhere. Fixed grids satisfy this.
Floating grids usually need a cap on the reachable states instead. -/
theorem quantizedChunks_within {shape : Shape} {Input Output : Type}
    (step : Tensor ℝ shape → Input → Tensor ℝ shape × Output)
    (quantize : Tensor ℝ shape → Tensor ℝ shape) (L δ : ℝ)
    (hstep : ∀ input e x y, Within e x y → Within (L * e) (step x input).1 (step y input).1)
    (hquantize : ∀ x, Within δ (quantize x) x)
    (chunks : List (List Input)) (x y : Tensor ℝ shape) (e : ℝ) (hxy : Within e x y) :
    Within (checkpointBudget L δ e chunks)
      (quantizedChunks step quantize x chunks) (CausalScan.run step y chunks.flatten).1 := by
  have hwrites : ∀ state parts, WritesWithin step quantize δ state parts := by
    intro state parts
    induction parts generalizing state with
    | nil => trivial
    | cons chunk rest ih => exact ⟨hquantize _, ih _⟩
  exact quantizedChunks_within_of_writes step quantize L δ hstep chunks x y e hxy
    (hwrites x chunks)

/-- With `0 ≤ L ≤ 1` the budget grows at most linearly in the number of writes. This is a
worst-case bound and does not compare the actual errors of two schedules. -/
theorem checkpointBudget_le_count {Input : Type} (L δ e : ℝ)
    (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hLone : L ≤ 1) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (he : 0 ≤ e)
    (chunks : List (List Input)) :
    checkpointBudget L δ e chunks ≤ e + chunks.length * δ := by
  induction chunks generalizing e with
  | nil => simp [checkpointBudget]
  | cons chunk rest ih =>
      have hpower : 0 ≤ L ^ chunk.length := pow_nonneg hL _
      have hpowerOne : L ^ chunk.length ≤ 1 := pow_le_one₀ hL hLone
      have hnext : 0 ≤ L ^ chunk.length * e + δ :=
        add_nonneg (mul_nonneg hpower he) hδ
      have hbound := ih (L ^ chunk.length * e + δ) hnext
      simp only [checkpointBudget, List.length_cons, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one]
      nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hpowerOne he]

module

public import KimiK3.Sequence.Scan

/-!
# SSM checkpoint replay

Section 4.5 of the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra technical report (pp. 44–46) stores an older SSM
checkpoint together with the activations needed to replay the transitions after it. The laws
reuse the shared causal scan and hold for any deterministic transition (a rounded one included),
as long as replay uses the same transition and the same prepared inputs.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.Cache

open KimiK3

/-- A stored state and the prepared inputs since that state was stored, in chronological order. -/
structure Replay (State Input : Type) where
  checkpoint : State
  pending : List Input

namespace Replay

variable {State Input Output : Type}

/-- Reconstruct the current state and the outputs since the checkpoint. -/
def observe (step : State → Input → State × Output) (cache : Replay State Input) :
    State × List Output :=
  CausalScan.run step cache.checkpoint cache.pending

/-- Retain an additional prepared input without writing the recurrent state. -/
def push (cache : Replay State Input) (input : Input) : Replay State Input :=
  ⟨cache.checkpoint, cache.pending ++ [input]⟩

/-- Commit the reconstructed state through the supplied storage quantizer. -/
def flush (step : State → Input → State × Output) (quantize : State → State)
    (cache : Replay State Input) : Replay State Input :=
  -- Clearing pending inputs prevents applying the already committed transitions twice.
  ⟨quantize (cache.observe step).1, []⟩

/-- Replaying one more input gives the same state and output as stepping the reconstructed state.
Earlier replay outputs stay at the front of the list. -/
theorem observe_push (step : State → Input → State × Output) (cache : Replay State Input)
    (input : Input) :
    (cache.push input).observe step =
      let prior := cache.observe step
      let next := step prior.1 input
      (next.1, prior.2 ++ [next.2]) := by
  simpa [observe, push, CausalScan.run] using
    CausalScan.run_append step cache.checkpoint cache.pending [input]

/-- An exact checkpoint write preserves the reconstructed current state. -/
@[simp] theorem observe_flush_id_state (step : State → Input → State × Output)
    (cache : Replay State Input) :
    ((cache.flush step id).observe step).1 = (cache.observe step).1 := by
  rfl

/-- After a flush the reconstructed state is the quantized state, so a checkpoint adds only the
quantizer's error at that state. -/
@[simp] theorem observe_flush_state (step : State → Input → State × Output)
    (quantize : State → State) (cache : Replay State Input) :
    ((cache.flush step quantize).observe step).1 = quantize (cache.observe step).1 := by
  rfl

/-- Scanning the pending inputs and a suffix from the checkpoint equals replaying, then
continuing from the reconstructed state. Every output agrees, not just the final state. -/
theorem run_from_replay (step : State → Input → State × Output)
    (cache : Replay State Input) (suffix : List Input) :
    CausalScan.run step cache.checkpoint (cache.pending ++ suffix) =
      let prior := cache.observe step
      let next := CausalScan.run step prior.1 suffix
      (next.1, prior.2 ++ next.2) :=
  CausalScan.run_append step cache.checkpoint cache.pending suffix

end Replay

/-- Run each chunk, then quantize the state once. An empty chunk still writes, so callers that
count token periods should pass nonempty chunks. -/
def quantizedChunks {State Input Output : Type}
    (step : State → Input → State × Output) (quantize : State → State) :
    State → List (List Input) → State
  | state, [] => state
  | state, chunk :: rest =>
      quantizedChunks step quantize (quantize (CausalScan.run step state chunk).1) rest

/-- Without storage loss, every chunk partition has the same final state as one full scan. -/
theorem quantizedChunks_id {State Input Output : Type}
    (step : State → Input → State × Output) (state : State) (chunks : List (List Input)) :
    quantizedChunks step id state chunks = (CausalScan.run step state chunks.flatten).1 := by
  induction chunks generalizing state with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons chunk rest ih =>
      simp only [quantizedChunks, id_eq, List.flatten_cons, ih]
      rw [CausalScan.run_append]

end Nemotron.Cache

/-!
# Reusing FloatLib rounding

Tensor rounding on FloatLib's real-valued IEEE grid, with FloatLib's proved half-ULP bound.
This grid has no upper exponent limit, so relating it to executable finite bits needs FloatLib's
finiteness refinement hypotheses. It rounds to nearest even, while the released Ultra cache
rounds stochastically (`Nemotron.Cache.Stochastic`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.Cache

open TorchLean KimiK3
open FloatLib.Floats
open FloatLib.Floats.Formats.BinaryInterchange

/-- Round every coordinate to nearest even on FloatLib's real-valued grid for `fmt`. -/
noncomputable def roundTensor {shape : Shape} (fmt : FloatFormat)
    (x : Tensor ℝ shape) : Tensor ℝ shape :=
  Tensor.map (Model.roundAt fmt) x

/-- If every coordinate's half-ULP is at most `δ`, rounding is `Within δ`. An absolute
bound covers subnormals and needs no relative error bound near zero. -/
theorem roundTensor_within {shape : Shape} (fmt : FloatFormat)
    (x : Tensor ℝ shape) (δ : ℝ)
    (hδ : ∀ coordinate, Model.ulpAt fmt (x coordinate) / 2 ≤ δ) :
    Within δ (roundTensor fmt x) x := by
  intro coordinate
  simpa only [roundTensor, Tensor.map_apply] using
    (Model.abs_roundAt_sub_le fmt (x coordinate)).trans (hδ coordinate)

namespace Counterexample

/-- FloatLib's nearest-even rounding to an integer, read back as a rational. -/
def quantize (x : ℚ) : ℚ := (FloatLib.Numerics.roundRatEven x : ℚ)

/-- Exact rational addition, so storage is the only place that rounds. -/
def addStep (state input : ℚ) : ℚ × Unit := (state + input, ())

/-- Integer rounding is within `1/2` everywhere. -/
theorem quantize_error (x : ℚ) : |quantize x - x| ≤ (1 : ℚ) / 2 :=
  FloatLib.Numerics.roundRatEven_error_le_half x

/-- Four nearest-even writes can end closer to the exact sum than two, through cancellation.
So "fewer sequential quantization steps" does not always mean less error. This is a fixed-grid
example, not a counterexample to the report's measured results. -/
theorem fewer_writes_can_increase_error :
    |quantizedChunks addStep quantize 0
        [[-9 / 10], [-9 / 10], [-1 / 2], [-1 / 10]] - (-12 / 5)| <
      |quantizedChunks addStep quantize 0
        [[-9 / 10, -9 / 10], [-1 / 2, -1 / 10]] - (-12 / 5)| := by
  decide +kernel

/-- Two half-unit updates written separately both round to the even value `0`. One write of
their sum keeps it. -/
theorem repeated_ties_lose_updates :
    quantizedChunks addStep quantize 0 [[1 / 2], [1 / 2]] = 0 ∧
      quantizedChunks addStep quantize 0 [[1 / 2, 1 / 2]] = 1 := by
  decide +kernel

end Counterexample

end Nemotron.Cache

module

public import Nemotron.SSM
public import Mathlib.Data.List.TakeDrop

/-!
# Restoring speculative recurrent state

Section 5.1 of the Ultra report (p. 48) retains an SSM snapshot at each draft step. After a
rejection, the recurrent state must belong to the accepted prefix, not the complete draft.
`snapshots` keeps every post-step state of the shared scan. Its laws hold for any state type and
deterministic transition (a stochastic one must carry its entropy in the state or the prepared
inputs). No draft acceptance rule or its probability law is modeled.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.Cache.Speculation

open KimiK3

variable {State Input Output : Type}

/-- Initial state, then the state after each draft input, in chronological order. -/
def snapshots (step : State → Input → State × Output) (initial : State) (draft : List Input) :
    List State :=
  initial :: (CausalScan.run (fun state input =>
    let next := step state input
    (next.1, next.1)) initial draft).2

/-- One snapshot is available for every accepted length, including zero and the full draft. -/
@[simp] theorem snapshots_length (step : State → Input → State × Output)
    (initial : State) (draft : List Input) :
    (snapshots step initial draft).length = draft.length + 1 := by
  simp [snapshots, CausalScan.outputs_length]

/-- Stored state after the accepted prefix, found by a bounded index with no default. -/
def restore (step : State → Input → State × Output) (initial : State) (draft : List Input)
    (accepted : Fin (draft.length + 1)) : State :=
  (snapshots step initial draft)[accepted.val]'(by
    rw [snapshots_length]
    exact accepted.isLt)

/-- Restoring gives the state after running the accepted prefix. -/
theorem restore_eq_prefix (step : State → Input → State × Output)
    (initial : State) (draft : List Input) (accepted : Fin (draft.length + 1)) :
    restore step initial draft accepted =
      (CausalScan.run step initial (draft.take accepted.val)).1 := by
  induction draft generalizing initial with
  | nil =>
      simp [restore, snapshots, CausalScan.run]
  | cons input rest ih =>
      cases accepted using Fin.cases with
      | zero => simp [restore, snapshots, CausalScan.run]
      | succ accepted =>
          simpa [restore, snapshots, CausalScan.run] using ih (step initial input).1 accepted

/-- Continuing from the restored snapshot gives the same final state and committed outputs as
scanning the accepted prefix and the continuation. Rejected draft inputs leave no trace. -/
theorem run_after_restore (step : State → Input → State × Output)
    (initial : State) (draft : List Input) (accepted : Fin (draft.length + 1))
    (continuation : List Input) :
    CausalScan.run step initial (draft.take accepted.val ++ continuation) =
      let prior := CausalScan.run step initial (draft.take accepted.val)
      let next := CausalScan.run step (restore step initial draft accepted) continuation
      (next.1, prior.2 ++ next.2) := by
  rw [restore_eq_prefix]
  exact CausalScan.run_append step initial (draft.take accepted.val) continuation

end Nemotron.Cache.Speculation

namespace Nemotron.SSM.Sequence

open TorchLean KimiK3

/-- Every draft state packed along a leading axis, with the initial state in row zero. -/
def snapshots {α : Type} [Storage α] [Add α] [Mul α] [Zero α]
    {tokens valueDim stateDim : Nat} (inputs : Sequence α tokens valueDim stateDim)
    (initial : State α valueDim stateDim) : Tensor α [tokens + 1, valueDim, stateDim] :=
  Tensor.dim fun accepted =>
    Cache.Speculation.restore step initial inputs.toList
      ⟨accepted.val, by simpa using accepted.isLt⟩

/-- Row `accepted` is the state after that many tokens. -/
theorem snapshots_unstack {α : Type} [Storage α] [Add α] [Mul α] [Zero α]
    {tokens valueDim stateDim : Nat} (inputs : Sequence α tokens valueDim stateDim)
    (initial : State α valueDim stateDim) (accepted : Fin (tokens + 1)) :
    Tensor.unstack (inputs.snapshots initial) accepted =
      (CausalScan.run step initial (inputs.toList.take accepted.val)).1 := by
  simp only [snapshots, Tensor.unstack_dim, Cache.Speculation.restore_eq_prefix]

end Nemotron.SSM.Sequence

module

public import Nemotron.SSM
public import FloatLib.Floats.Formats.BinaryInterchange.Rounding.Policy.Runtime
public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Piecewise
public import Mathlib.Order.Interval.Finset.Fin

import Mathlib.Data.Int.CardIntervalMod

/-!
# Stochastic writes on a fixed rounding grid

The Ultra report's §4.5 (pp. 44–46) uses stochastic FP16 cache writes. We reuse FloatLib's
executable stochastic quotient rounder and prove its local mean under uniform residues.
Each tensor coordinate gets its own signed grid cell, before overflow, saturation, or underflow
policies. Quanta and denominators come from the caller, so this is not an FP16
encoder. Uniform fixed-width words reduced `% den` need not give uniform residues, but they do
when `den` divides the number of words (`uniformResidues_range`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.Cache.Stochastic

open TorchLean FloatLib.Floats.Formats.BinaryInterchange

private theorem roundQuot_eq (sign : Bool) (entropy num den : Nat) :
    Model.Policy.roundQuot .stochastic sign entropy num den =
      num / den + if entropy % den < num % den then 1 else 0 := by
  by_cases h : num % den = 0
  · simp [Model.Policy.roundQuot, h]
  · simp [Model.Policy.roundQuot, h]
    split <;> simp

/-- Summed over all `den` entropy residues, FloatLib's executable stochastic quotients add up
to `num`. -/
theorem roundQuot_sum (sign : Bool) (num den : Nat) (hden : 0 < den) :
    (∑ entropy : Fin den, Model.Policy.roundQuot .stochastic sign entropy.val num den) = num := by
  classical
  let remainder : Fin den := ⟨num % den, Nat.mod_lt num hden⟩
  have hfilter : Finset.univ.filter (fun e : Fin den => e.val < num % den) =
      Finset.Iio remainder := by
    ext e
    simp [Fin.lt_def, remainder]
  have hcount : (∑ e : Fin den, if e.val < num % den then 1 else 0) = num % den := by
    rw [← Finset.card_filter, hfilter]
    exact Fin.card_Iio remainder
  simp_rw [roundQuot_eq, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (Fin.isLt _)]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, hcount]
  simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod num den

/-- One signed-grid write. Entropy is an argument, so a replay makes the same choice. -/
noncomputable def round (quantum : ℝ) (sign : Bool) (entropy num den : Nat) : ℝ :=
  (if sign then -1 else 1) * quantum *
    (Model.Policy.roundQuot .stochastic sign entropy num den : ℝ)

/-- Averaged over all `den` residues, a write equals the unrounded value of its grid cell. -/
theorem round_mean (quantum : ℝ) (sign : Bool) (num den : Nat) (hden : 0 < den) :
    (∑ entropy : Fin den, round quantum sign entropy.val num den) / (den : ℝ) =
      (if sign then -1 else 1) * quantum * ((num : ℝ) / den) := by
  have hsum : (∑ entropy : Fin den,
      (Model.Policy.roundQuot .stochastic sign entropy.val num den : ℝ)) = (num : ℝ) := by
    exact_mod_cast roundQuot_sum sign num den hden
  simp only [round, ← Finset.mul_sum, hsum]
  ring

/-- For every entropy word, a write is within one grid spacing `|quantum|` of the unrounded
value. Unbiasedness on average does not make a single write exact. -/
theorem round_error (quantum : ℝ) (sign : Bool) (entropy num den : Nat)
    (hden : 0 < den) :
    |round quantum sign entropy num den -
      (if sign then -1 else 1) * quantum * ((num : ℝ) / den)| ≤ |quantum| := by
  have hd : (0 : ℝ) < den := by exact_mod_cast hden
  have hdecomp : (den : ℝ) * (num / den : Nat) + (num % den : Nat) = num := by
    exact_mod_cast Nat.div_add_mod num den
  have hrem : (num % den : Nat) < (den : ℝ) := by
    exact_mod_cast Nat.mod_lt num hden
  have hrem0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (num % den : Nat) := Nat.cast_nonneg _
  have hlo : (num / den : Nat) ≤ (num : ℝ) / den := by
    apply (le_div_iff₀ hd).2
    nlinarith
  have hhi : (num : ℝ) / den ≤ (num / den : Nat) + 1 := by
    apply (div_le_iff₀ hd).2
    nlinarith
  have hunit : |(Model.Policy.roundQuot .stochastic sign entropy num den : ℝ) -
      (num : ℝ) / den| ≤ 1 := by
    rw [roundQuot_eq]
    split <;> simp only [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one, add_zero]
    all_goals rw [abs_le]; constructor <;> linarith
  have hsign : |(if sign then (-1 : ℝ) else 1)| = 1 := by cases sign <;> norm_num
  calc
    _ = |(if sign then (-1 : ℝ) else 1) * quantum| *
        |(Model.Policy.roundQuot .stochastic sign entropy num den : ℝ) -
          (num : ℝ) / den| := by rw [round, ← mul_sub, abs_mul]
    _ ≤ |(if sign then (-1 : ℝ) else 1) * quantum| * 1 :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hunit (abs_nonneg _)
    _ = |quantum| := by rw [abs_mul, hsign, one_mul, mul_one]

/-- A finite family of entropy words with uniform residues modulo `den`: every residue below
`den` is hit by `samples / den` words. -/
def UniformResidues {samples : Nat} (den : Nat) (entropy : Fin samples → Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ r < den, den * (Finset.univ.filter fun i => entropy i % den = r).card = samples

private theorem card_residue_lt {samples den : Nat} {entropy : Fin samples → Nat}
    (huniform : UniformResidues den entropy) :
    ∀ m ≤ den, den * (Finset.univ.filter fun i => entropy i % den < m).card = m * samples := by
  intro m
  induction m with
  | zero => intro _; simp
  | succ m ih =>
      intro hm
      have hsplit : (Finset.univ.filter fun i => entropy i % den < m + 1) =
          (Finset.univ.filter fun i => entropy i % den < m) ∪
            (Finset.univ.filter fun i => entropy i % den = m) := by
        ext i
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_union]
        omega
      have hdisjoint : Disjoint (Finset.univ.filter fun i => entropy i % den < m)
          (Finset.univ.filter fun i => entropy i % den = m) := by
        rw [Finset.disjoint_filter]
        intro i _ h
        omega
      rw [hsplit, Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisjoint, mul_add, ih (by omega),
        huniform m (by omega)]
      ring

/-- `roundQuot_sum` for any finite ensemble with uniform residues. -/
theorem roundQuot_ensemble_sum (sign : Bool) (num den : Nat) (hden : 0 < den)
    {samples : Nat} (entropy : Fin samples → Nat) (huniform : UniformResidues den entropy) :
    den * (∑ i, Model.Policy.roundQuot .stochastic sign (entropy i) num den) =
      samples * num := by
  classical
  simp_rw [roundQuot_eq]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.card_filter, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ,
    Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul, mul_add, card_residue_lt huniform _ (Nat.mod_lt num hden).le]
  conv_rhs => rw [← Nat.div_add_mod num den]
  ring

/-- Over a nonempty ensemble with uniform residues, the mean write is the unrounded value. -/
theorem round_ensemble_mean (quantum : ℝ) (sign : Bool) (num den : Nat) (hden : 0 < den)
    {samples : Nat} (hsamples : 0 < samples) (entropy : Fin samples → Nat)
    (huniform : UniformResidues den entropy) :
    (∑ i, round quantum sign (entropy i) num den) / (samples : ℝ) =
      (if sign then -1 else 1) * quantum * ((num : ℝ) / den) := by
  have hsum : (den : ℝ) *
      (∑ i, (Model.Policy.roundQuot .stochastic sign (entropy i) num den : ℝ)) =
        samples * num := by
    exact_mod_cast roundQuot_ensemble_sum sign num den hden entropy huniform
  have hd : (den : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  have hs : (samples : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  have hrq : (∑ i, (Model.Policy.roundQuot .stochastic sign (entropy i) num den : ℝ)) =
      samples * num / den := by
    rw [eq_div_iff hd, mul_comm]
    exact hsum
  simp only [round, ← Finset.mul_sum, hrq]
  field_simp

/-- Apply `round` coordinatewise. Each coordinate has its own sign, quantum, denominator,
numerator, and entropy word, so mixed signs and cells are allowed. -/
noncomputable def roundTensor {shape : Shape} (quantum : Tensor ℝ shape)
    (sign : Tensor Bool shape) (den numerators entropy : Tensor Nat shape) : Tensor ℝ shape :=
  TorchLean.Tensor.Rep.ofFn fun coordinate =>
    round (quantum coordinate) (sign coordinate) (entropy coordinate) (numerators coordinate)
      (den coordinate)

/-- Signed value of each coordinate's grid cell before rounding. -/
noncomputable def unrounded {shape : Shape} (quantum : Tensor ℝ shape)
    (sign : Tensor Bool shape) (den numerators : Tensor Nat shape) : Tensor ℝ shape :=
  TorchLean.Tensor.Rep.ofFn fun coordinate =>
    (if sign coordinate then -1 else 1) * quantum coordinate *
      ((numerators coordinate : ℝ) / den coordinate)

/-- If every coordinate's grid spacing is at most `δ`, a stochastic tensor write is `Within δ`
of the unrounded tensor, however the entropy words are correlated. -/
theorem roundTensor_within {shape : Shape} (quantum : Tensor ℝ shape)
    (sign : Tensor Bool shape) (den numerators entropy : Tensor Nat shape) (δ : ℝ)
    (hden : ∀ coordinate, 0 < den coordinate)
    (hδ : ∀ coordinate, |quantum coordinate| ≤ δ) :
    Within δ (roundTensor quantum sign den numerators entropy)
      (unrounded quantum sign den numerators) := by
  intro coordinate
  simpa [roundTensor, unrounded] using
    (round_error (quantum coordinate) (sign coordinate) (entropy coordinate)
      (numerators coordinate) (den coordinate) (hden coordinate)).trans (hδ coordinate)

private theorem sum_apply {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] {shape : Shape}
    (values : ι → Tensor ℝ shape) (coordinate : Shape.Coord shape) :
    (∑ i, values i) coordinate = ∑ i, values i coordinate := by
  classical
  let evaluation : Tensor ℝ shape →+ ℝ :=
    { toFun := fun x => x coordinate
      map_zero' := by simp
      map_add' := by intros; simp }
  exact map_sum evaluation values Finset.univ

/-- Coordinatewise mean of a finite tensor ensemble. Mean laws require a nonempty sample axis. -/
noncomputable def mean {samples : Nat} {shape : Shape}
    (values : Tensor ℝ (samples :: shape)) : Tensor ℝ shape :=
  (samples : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ i : Fin samples, Tensor.unstack values i

private theorem mean_apply {samples : Nat} {shape : Shape}
    (values : Tensor ℝ (samples :: shape)) (coordinate : Shape.Coord shape) :
    mean values coordinate =
      (∑ i : Fin samples, Tensor.unstack values i coordinate) / samples := by
  simp [mean, sum_apply, div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm]

private theorem mean_add {samples : Nat} {shape : Shape}
    (x y : Tensor ℝ (samples :: shape)) :
    mean (x + y) = mean x + mean y := by
  apply TorchLean.Tensor.Rep.ext
  intro coordinate
  simp [mean_apply, Tensor.add_def, Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_div]

/-- Each coordinate is unbiased when its own entropy residues are uniform. Nothing is assumed
about how the words of different coordinates are related. One word shared by every coordinate
and independent words both satisfy the premise (`roundTensor_mean_shared`,
`roundTensor_mean_independent`), though shared words give correlated coordinate errors. -/
theorem roundTensor_mean {samples : Nat} {shape : Shape} (quantum : Tensor ℝ shape)
    (sign : Tensor Bool shape) (den numerators : Tensor Nat shape)
    (entropy : Fin samples → Tensor Nat shape) (hsamples : 0 < samples)
    (hden : ∀ coordinate, 0 < den coordinate)
    (huniform : ∀ coordinate,
      UniformResidues (den coordinate) fun i => entropy i coordinate) :
    mean (Tensor.dim fun i => roundTensor quantum sign den numerators (entropy i)) =
      unrounded quantum sign den numerators := by
  apply TorchLean.Tensor.Rep.ext
  intro coordinate
  simpa [mean_apply, roundTensor, unrounded] using
    round_ensemble_mean (quantum coordinate) (sign coordinate) (numerators coordinate)
      (den coordinate) (hden coordinate) hsamples (fun i => entropy i coordinate)
      (huniform coordinate)

/-- Words `0, …, words - 1` have uniform residues modulo every divisor of `words`. -/
theorem uniformResidues_range {words den : Nat} (hden : 0 < den) (hdvd : den ∣ words) :
    UniformResidues den fun i : Fin words => i.val := by
  intro r hr
  have hcount := Nat.count_modEq_card (b := words) hden r
  rw [Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd hdvd] at hcount
  simp only [Nat.not_lt_zero, ite_false, add_zero] at hcount
  have hmap : (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin words => i.val % den = r).map Fin.valEmbedding =
      (Finset.range words).filter fun k => k ≡ r [MOD den] := by
    ext k
    simp only [Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
      Fin.valEmbedding_apply, Finset.mem_range, Nat.ModEq, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hr]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨i.isLt, hi⟩
    · rintro ⟨hk, hmod⟩
      exact ⟨⟨k, hk⟩, hmod, rfl⟩
  rw [← Finset.card_map Fin.valEmbedding, hmap, ← Nat.count_eq_card_filter_range, hcount]
  exact Nat.mul_div_cancel' hdvd

/-- Mean law for one word shared by every coordinate, drawn uniformly from `words` values that
every denominator divides (say a `2^k`-valued word and power-of-two denominators up to `2^k`).
Coordinate means are exact although coordinate errors are strongly correlated. -/
theorem roundTensor_mean_shared {shape : Shape} (quantum : Tensor ℝ shape)
    (sign : Tensor Bool shape) (den numerators : Tensor Nat shape) (words : Nat)
    (hwords : 0 < words) (hden : ∀ coordinate, 0 < den coordinate)
    (hdvd : ∀ coordinate, den coordinate ∣ words) :
    mean (Tensor.dim fun e : Fin words =>
      roundTensor quantum sign den numerators (Tensor.full shape e.val)) =
      unrounded quantum sign den numerators := by
  apply roundTensor_mean quantum sign den numerators _ hwords hden
  intro coordinate
  simpa using uniformResidues_range (hden coordinate) (hdvd coordinate)

private theorem card_fiber_eq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {d : ι → Nat}
    (c : ι) (r r' : Fin (d c)) :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun ω : (j : ι) → Fin (d j) => ω c = r).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun ω : (j : ι) → Fin (d j) => ω c = r').card := by
  apply Finset.card_nbij' (fun ω => Function.update ω c r') (fun ω => Function.update ω c r)
  · intro ω _
    simp
  · intro ω _
    simp
  · intro ω hω
    have hω' : ω c = r := by simpa using hω
    funext j
    by_cases hj : j = c
    · subst hj
      simp [hω']
    · simp [hj]
  · intro ω hω
    have hω' : ω c = r' := by simpa using hω
    funext j
    by_cases hj : j = c
    · subst hj
      simp [hω']
    · simp [hj]

private theorem card_fiber_mul {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {d : ι → Nat}
    (c : ι) (r : Fin (d c)) :
    d c * (Finset.univ.filter fun ω : (j : ι) → Fin (d j) => ω c = r).card =
      Fintype.card ((j : ι) → Fin (d j)) := by
  have hfibers := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
    (s := (Finset.univ : Finset ((j : ι) → Fin (d j))))
    (f := fun ω : (j : ι) → Fin (d j) => ω c) (t := Finset.univ) (by simp)
  rw [← Finset.card_univ, hfibers, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r' _ => card_fiber_eq c r' r]
  simp

/-- Product ensemble: every assignment of one residue to each coordinate occurs once, so
different coordinates get independent uniform words. -/
noncomputable def independentEntropy {shape : Shape} (den : Tensor Nat shape) :
    Fin (Fintype.card ((coordinate : Shape.Coord shape) → Fin (den coordinate))) →
      Tensor Nat shape :=
  fun i => TorchLean.Tensor.Rep.ofFn fun coordinate =>
    ((Fintype.equivFin _).symm i coordinate).val

/-- Independent uniform residues, one per coordinate, also give exact coordinate means. -/
theorem roundTensor_mean_independent {shape : Shape} (quantum : Tensor ℝ shape)
    (sign : Tensor Bool shape) (den numerators : Tensor Nat shape)
    (hden : ∀ coordinate, 0 < den coordinate) :
    mean (Tensor.dim fun i =>
      roundTensor quantum sign den numerators (independentEntropy den i)) =
      unrounded quantum sign den numerators := by
  classical
  have hsamples : 0 < Fintype.card ((coordinate : Shape.Coord shape) → Fin (den coordinate)) :=
    Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨fun coordinate => ⟨0, hden coordinate⟩⟩
  apply roundTensor_mean quantum sign den numerators _ hsamples hden
  intro coordinate r hr
  refine Eq.trans ?_ (card_fiber_mul (d := fun coordinate => den coordinate) coordinate ⟨r, hr⟩)
  congr 1
  apply Finset.card_equiv (Fintype.equivFin _).symm
  intro i
  simp [independentEntropy, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (Fin.isLt _), Fin.ext_iff]

/-- A fixed prepared SSM update is affine, so it commutes with the mean of a nonempty ensemble.
`scan_mean` uses this to compose conditionally unbiased state writes. Input-dependent token
selection, normalization, and nonlinear decoder layers fall outside the identity. -/
theorem update_mean {samples valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (states : Tensor ℝ [samples, valueDim, stateDim])
    (input : SSM.Input ℝ valueDim stateDim) (hsamples : 0 < samples) :
    SSM.update (mean states) input =
      mean (Tensor.dim fun i => SSM.update (Tensor.unstack states i) input) := by
  apply TorchLean.Tensor.Rep.ext
  intro coordinate
  have hn : (samples : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast Nat.ne_of_gt hsamples
  simp only [SSM.update, Tensor.add_apply, Tensor.scale, Tensor.map_apply,
    mean_apply, Tensor.unstack_dim]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_mul]
  simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
  field_simp

end Nemotron.Cache.Stochastic

namespace Nemotron.SSM

open TorchLean KimiK3
open Cache.Stochastic

/-- If the ensemble mean follows one `update` per token, it follows the whole scan. `states`
can index all finite random histories, with repetitions for their weights. This needs the mean
over those histories at every step, which an encoder unbiased in isolation does not supply. -/
private theorem scan_mean_of_step {samples valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (inputs : List (Input ℝ valueDim stateDim))
    (states : Nat → Tensor ℝ [samples, valueDim, stateDim])
    (hstep : ∀ i : Fin inputs.length, mean (states (i.val + 1)) =
      update (mean (states i.val)) inputs[i.val]) :
    mean (states inputs.length) = (CausalScan.run step (mean (states 0)) inputs).1 := by
  induction inputs generalizing states with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons input rest ih =>
      have hfirst := hstep ⟨0, by simp⟩
      have hrest := ih (fun n => states (n + 1)) (fun i => by
        simpa [Nat.add_assoc] using hstep i.succ)
      simpa [CausalScan.run, step, hfirst] using hrest

/-- If each step updates every sample and then adds storage errors of mean zero, the ensemble
mean follows the exact scan from the initial mean. Conditionally unbiased writes can supply
`herrors` on finite histories. Neither independence nor zero error on a single history is
assumed. -/
theorem scan_mean {samples valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (inputs : List (Input ℝ valueDim stateDim))
    (states errors : Nat → Tensor ℝ [samples, valueDim, stateDim]) (hsamples : 0 < samples)
    (hstep : ∀ i : Fin inputs.length, states (i.val + 1) =
      (Tensor.dim fun sample =>
        update (Tensor.unstack (states i.val) sample) inputs[i.val]) + errors i.val)
    (herrors : ∀ i : Fin inputs.length,
      mean (errors i.val) = Tensor.full [valueDim, stateDim] 0) :
    mean (states inputs.length) = (CausalScan.run step (mean (states 0)) inputs).1 := by
  apply scan_mean_of_step inputs states
  intro i
  rw [hstep i, Cache.Stochastic.mean_add, herrors i]
  rw [← update_mean (states i.val) inputs[i.val] hsamples]
  apply TorchLean.Tensor.Rep.ext
  intro coordinate
  simp

end Nemotron.SSM

module

public import Nemotron.Cache.Error
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Sequence
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Arithmetic
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Contract
public import TorchLean.Tensor.OfFn
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Operations
public import Mathlib.Data.List.GetD

import TorchLean.Tensor.Algebra

/-!
# A prepared single-head SSM core

The Ultra report names Mamba-2 in §2.1 and Table 1 (pp. 3–4), but §4.5 does not give the full
selective SSM equations. Here `retention`, `write`, `value`, and `read` arrive already projected
and discretized, and the recurrence is `S' = a S + x Bᵀ`, `y = S' C`. This is the
scalar-transition core of one head, with the matrix transposed so each row belongs to a value
channel. Convolution, groups, gating, normalization, and the output skip are left out, and
nothing here builds the coefficients from a Nemotron checkpoint (`Nemotron.Architecture.Mamba2`
adds grouping and the D skip).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.SSM

open TorchLean KimiK3

/-- State of a single head, with one row per value channel and one column per SSM coordinate. -/
abbrev State (α : Type) [Storage α] (valueDim stateDim : Nat) :=
  Tensor α [valueDim, stateDim]

/-- Prepared coefficients for one token, after projection and discretization. -/
structure Input (α : Type) [Storage α] (valueDim stateDim : Nat) where
  retention : α
  value : Tensor α [valueDim]
  write : Tensor α [stateDim]
  read : Tensor α [stateDim]

/-- One recurrent update `S' = a S + x Bᵀ`: scalar retention plus a rank-one write. -/
def update {α : Type} [Storage α] [Add α] [Mul α]
    {valueDim stateDim : Nat} (state : State α valueDim stateDim)
    (input : Input α valueDim stateDim) : State α valueDim stateDim :=
  state.scale input.retention +
    Tensor.matrix (fun i j => input.value.getScalar i * input.write.getScalar j)

/-- Update the state, then read the new state against the token's read vector. -/
def step {α : Type} [Storage α] [Add α] [Mul α] [Zero α]
    {valueDim stateDim : Nat} (state : State α valueDim stateDim)
    (input : Input α valueDim stateDim) :
    State α valueDim stateDim × Tensor α [valueDim] :=
  let next := update state input
  (next, Tensor.matvec next input.read)

/-- Applying the same prepared input to two states cancels the rank-one write. -/
theorem update_sub_apply {valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (x y : State ℝ valueDim stateDim) (input : Input ℝ valueDim stateDim)
    (coordinate : Shape.Coord [valueDim, stateDim]) :
    update x input coordinate - update y input coordinate =
      input.retention * (x coordinate - y coordinate) := by
  simp [update, Tensor.scale]
  ring

/-- If `|retention| ≤ L`, one update scales a coordinate error bound by `L`, for any dimensions. -/
theorem update_within {valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (x y : State ℝ valueDim stateDim) (input : Input ℝ valueDim stateDim)
    (L e : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hretention : |input.retention| ≤ L)
    (hxy : Cache.Within e x y) : Cache.Within (L * e) (update x input) (update y input) := by
  intro coordinate
  rw [update_sub_apply, abs_mul]
  exact mul_le_mul hretention (hxy coordinate) (abs_nonneg _) hL

/-- A fixed read vector turns a coordinatewise state error into an output error, scaled by the
read vector's absolute sum. So a stable state alone does not give a small readout error. -/
theorem read_within {valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (x y : State ℝ valueDim stateDim) (read : Tensor ℝ [stateDim])
    (e : ℝ) (hxy : Cache.Within e x y) :
    Cache.Within (e * ∑ j : Fin stateDim, |read.getScalar j|)
      (Tensor.matvec x read) (Tensor.matvec y read) := by
  rintro ⟨i, rest⟩
  cases rest
  change |(Tensor.matvec x read).getScalar i -
    (Tensor.matvec y read).getScalar i| ≤ _
  rw [Tensor.matvec, Tensor.matvec, Tensor.getScalar_contract_matVec_eq_sum,
    Tensor.getScalar_contract_matVec_eq_sum, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib,
    Finset.mul_sum]
  calc
    |∑ j : Fin stateDim, (Tensor.get2 x i j * read.getScalar j - Tensor.get2 y i j * read.getScalar j)|
        ≤ ∑ j : Fin stateDim,
            |Tensor.get2 x i j * read.getScalar j - Tensor.get2 y i j * read.getScalar j| :=
      Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ ≤ ∑ j : Fin stateDim, e * |read.getScalar j| := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro j _
      rw [← sub_mul, abs_mul]
      apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right _ (abs_nonneg _)
      simpa only [Tensor.get2_eq_apply] using
        hxy ⟨i, j, ()⟩

/-- Output error after one step: the state bound `L * e` times the read vector's absolute sum. -/
theorem step_output_within {valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (x y : State ℝ valueDim stateDim) (input : Input ℝ valueDim stateDim)
    (L e : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hretention : |input.retention| ≤ L)
    (hxy : Cache.Within e x y) :
    Cache.Within ((L * e) * ∑ j : Fin stateDim, |input.read.getScalar j|)
      (step x input).2 (step y input).2 :=
  read_within _ _ input.read (L * e) (update_within x y input L e hL hretention hxy)

/-- Prepared inputs for a whole token sequence, one row per token. -/
structure Sequence (α : Type) [Storage α] (tokens valueDim stateDim : Nat) where
  retention : Tensor α [tokens]
  value : Tensor α [tokens, valueDim]
  write : Tensor α [tokens, stateDim]
  read : Tensor α [tokens, stateDim]

namespace Sequence

/-- Prepared input at token `i`. -/
def token {α : Type} [Storage α] {tokens valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (inputs : Sequence α tokens valueDim stateDim) (i : Fin tokens) :
    Input α valueDim stateDim :=
  ⟨inputs.retention.getScalar i, Tensor.unstack inputs.value i,
    Tensor.unstack inputs.write i, Tensor.unstack inputs.read i⟩

/-- Tokens in chronological order, as a list for the shared causal scan. -/
def toList {α : Type} [Storage α] {tokens valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (inputs : Sequence α tokens valueDim stateDim) : List (Input α valueDim stateDim) :=
  (List.finRange tokens).map inputs.token

@[simp] theorem toList_length {α : Type} [Storage α] {tokens valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (inputs : Sequence α tokens valueDim stateDim) : inputs.toList.length = tokens := by
  simp [toList]

/-- Run the scan over a whole sequence and pack its outputs into a `[tokens, valueDim]` tensor. -/
def run {α : Type} [Storage α] [Add α] [Mul α] [Zero α]
    {tokens valueDim stateDim : Nat} (inputs : Sequence α tokens valueDim stateDim)
    (initial : State α valueDim stateDim) :
    State α valueDim stateDim × Tensor α [tokens, valueDim] :=
  let result := CausalScan.run step initial inputs.toList
  (result.1, Tensor.dim fun i =>
    result.2.getD i.val (Tensor.full [valueDim] 0))

/-- Every bounded output index is present, so packing does not use the default zero vector. -/
theorem output_index_lt {α : Type} [Storage α] [Add α] [Mul α] [Zero α]
    {tokens valueDim stateDim : Nat} (inputs : Sequence α tokens valueDim stateDim)
    (initial : State α valueDim stateDim) (i : Fin tokens) :
    i.val < (CausalScan.run step initial inputs.toList).2.length := by
  rw [CausalScan.outputs_length, inputs.toList_length]
  exact i.isLt

/-- Row `i` of the packed output is the scan's `i`-th output. -/
theorem run_unstack {α : Type} [Storage α] [Add α] [Mul α] [Zero α]
    {tokens valueDim stateDim : Nat} (inputs : Sequence α tokens valueDim stateDim)
    (initial : State α valueDim stateDim) (i : Fin tokens) :
    Tensor.unstack (inputs.run initial).2 i =
      (CausalScan.run step initial inputs.toList).2[i.val]'(inputs.output_index_lt initial i) := by
  simp only [run, Tensor.unstack_dim]
  exact List.getD_eq_getElem _ _ (inputs.output_index_lt initial i)

end Sequence

/-- Prepared inputs that carry a proof of `|retention| ≤ L`, as an error certificate needs. -/
abbrev BoundedInput (L : ℝ) (valueDim stateDim : Nat) :=
  { input : Input ℝ valueDim stateDim // |input.retention| ≤ L }

/-- `step` restricted to inputs with a retention bound. -/
noncomputable def boundedStep {valueDim stateDim : Nat} (L : ℝ)
    (state : State ℝ valueDim stateDim)
    (input : BoundedInput L valueDim stateDim) :
    State ℝ valueDim stateDim × Tensor ℝ [valueDim] :=
  step state input.val

/-- `Cache.quantizedChunks_within_of_writes` for the tensor SSM core. Retention and
storage-error bounds are hypotheses, not inferred from a precision format or trained weights. -/
theorem checkpoint_error {valueDim stateDim : Nat}
    (quantize : State ℝ valueDim stateDim → State ℝ valueDim stateDim)
    (L δ : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L)
    (initial : State ℝ valueDim stateDim)
    (chunks : List (List (BoundedInput L valueDim stateDim)))
    (hwrites : Cache.WritesWithin (boundedStep L) quantize δ initial chunks) :
    Cache.Within (Cache.checkpointBudget L δ 0 chunks)
      (Cache.quantizedChunks (boundedStep L) quantize initial chunks)
      (CausalScan.run (boundedStep L) initial chunks.flatten).1 := by
  apply Cache.quantizedChunks_within_of_writes (boundedStep L) quantize L δ
    (fun input e x y hxy => update_within x y input.val L e hL input.property hxy)
    chunks initial initial 0 (Cache.within_self initial) hwrites

end Nemotron.SSM

module

public import Nemotron.Cache.Error
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Arithmetic
public import FloatLib.Numerics.Reduction.Error
public import FloatLib.Floats.Formats.BinaryInterchange.Arithmetic.Runtime

/-!
# Gradient accumulation and lost contributions

The report's §2.7 (pp. 11–13) attributes its first training divergence to lowering the output
layer's local gradient accumulation from FP32 to BF16. Small MTP contributions were lost.
Here the gradient tensors are leaves of a FloatLib `ReductionTree`, which fixes the caller's
reduction order, and the bound pays for each rounded addition in that tree. Nothing assumes a
native backend used the same order or that the leaves are exact gradients.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Nemotron.Training

open TorchLean FloatLib.Numerics

/-- Combine gradient tensors in the supplied order, with the caller's scalar arithmetic. -/
def accumulate {α : Type} [Storage α] {shape : Shape} (combine : α → α → α)
    (schedule : ReductionTree (Tensor α shape)) : Tensor α shape :=
  schedule.eval (Tensor.zipWith combine) id

/-- A tensor reduction follows the same scalar schedule at every coordinate. -/
theorem accumulate_apply {α : Type} [Storage α] {shape : Shape} (combine : α → α → α)
    (schedule : ReductionTree (Tensor α shape)) (coordinate : Shape.Coord shape) :
    accumulate combine schedule coordinate = schedule.eval combine (fun x => x coordinate) := by
  induction schedule with
  | leaf x => rfl
  | node left right hl hr =>
      simpa [accumulate, ReductionTree.eval, Tensor.zipWith_apply] using congrArg₂ combine hl hr

/-- Accumulation error is at most FloatLib's sum of per-addition allowances, for any tensor shape
and scalar type. Errors in producing the leaves are not counted, since the reference adds the
interpreted leaves in exact real arithmetic.
-/
theorem accumulate_within {α : Type} [Storage α] {shape : Shape}
    (combine : α → α → α) (interpret : α → ℝ)
    (schedule : ReductionTree (Tensor α shape))
    (allowance : Tensor α shape → Tensor α shape → ℝ)
    (h : schedule.AllNodes (Tensor.zipWith combine) id (fun x y =>
      Cache.Within (allowance x y) (Tensor.map interpret (Tensor.zipWith combine x y))
        (Tensor.map interpret x + Tensor.map interpret y))) :
    Cache.Within (schedule.errorBudget (Tensor.zipWith combine) id allowance)
      (Tensor.map interpret (accumulate combine schedule))
      (accumulate (· + ·) (schedule.map (Tensor.map interpret))) := by
  intro coordinate
  have hError := schedule.abs_eval_sub_exact_le_errorBudget (Tensor.zipWith combine) id
    (fun x => interpret (x coordinate)) allowance
    (by
      induction schedule with
      | leaf x => trivial
      | node left right hl hr =>
          -- Project each node's tensor bound to this coordinate.
          exact ⟨hl h.1, hr h.2.1, by
            simpa [Tensor.map_apply, Tensor.add_apply] using h.2.2 coordinate⟩)
  change |interpret (accumulate combine schedule coordinate) -
    schedule.eval (· + ·) (fun x => interpret (x coordinate))| ≤ _ at hError
  rw [accumulate_apply] at hError
  simpa [accumulate_apply, ReductionTree.eval_map, Function.comp_def, Tensor.map_apply] using hError

/-- With one allowance `δ` per addition the error is at most `nodeCount * δ`, in any order. -/
theorem accumulate_within_nodeCount {α : Type} [Storage α] {shape : Shape}
    (combine : α → α → α) (interpret : α → ℝ)
    (schedule : ReductionTree (Tensor α shape)) (δ : ℝ)
    (h : schedule.AllNodes (Tensor.zipWith combine) id (fun x y =>
      Cache.Within δ (Tensor.map interpret (Tensor.zipWith combine x y))
        (Tensor.map interpret x + Tensor.map interpret y))) :
    Cache.Within (schedule.nodeCount * δ)
      (Tensor.map interpret (accumulate combine schedule))
      (accumulate (· + ·) (schedule.map (Tensor.map interpret))) := by
  simpa only [ReductionTree.errorBudget_const] using
    accumulate_within combine interpret schedule (fun _ _ => δ) h

namespace Counterexample

open FloatLib.Floats.Formats.BinaryInterchange

/-- In BF16, `256 + 1` is a tie and rounds back to the even neighbor `256`. These numbers
illustrate the mechanism and are not recorded gradients from NVIDIA's run. -/
theorem bf16_add_one_eq_self :
    Model.add (Model.roundRat .bfloat16 false 256 1) (Model.roundRat .bfloat16 false 1 1) =
      Model.roundRat .bfloat16 false 256 1 := by
  decide +kernel

/-- In binary32 the same addition is exact. -/
theorem binary32_add_one_eq_sum :
    Model.add (Model.roundRat .binary32 false 256 1) (Model.roundRat .binary32 false 1 1) =
      Model.roundRat .binary32 false 257 1 := by
  decide +kernel

end Counterexample

end Nemotron.Training

module

public import HeuristicEstimation.Basic

/-!
# Attention scores from moments

An unscaled query–key score is the ordinary tensor dot product. Its expectation is the score
of the means plus the trace of the query–key cross-covariance, and that trace survives when both
means vanish. Coordinates, queries and keys may depend on each other arbitrarily.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation.Attention

open TorchLean MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

/-- Unscaled attention score `qᵀ k` of one query and key. -/
def score {α : Type} [Storage α] [Add α] [Mul α] [Zero α] {d : Nat}
    (query key : Tensor α [d]) : α :=
  Tensor.sum (query * key)

/-- Over ℝ, the score unfolds to a sum over coordinates. -/
theorem score_eq_sum {d : Nat} (query key : Tensor ℝ [d]) :
    score query key = ∑ i : Fin d, query.getScalar i * key.getScalar i := by
  rw [score, vector_sum_eq]
  simp only [Tensor.getScalar_mul]

/-- Covariance-aware estimate of a score: the score of the means plus the trace of the supplied
cross-covariance. -/
def estimate {α : Type} [Storage α] [Add α] [Mul α] [Zero α] {d : Nat}
    (queryMean keyMean : Tensor α [d]) (crossCovariance : Tensor α [d, d]) : α :=
  score queryMean keyMean + Tensor.sum (Tensor.ofFn fun (i : Fin d) => crossCovariance[(i, i)])

/-- With the true means and cross-covariance, `estimate` is the expected score. Each coordinate
needs a finite second moment, and no Gaussian or independence assumption is made. -/
theorem score_mean {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d : Nat} (query key : Ω → Tensor ℝ [d])
    (hq : ∀ i, MemLp (fun ω => (query ω).getScalar i) 2 μ)
    (hk : ∀ i, MemLp (fun ω => (key ω).getScalar i) 2 μ) :
    (∫ ω, score (query ω) (key ω) ∂μ) =
      estimate (Tensor.ofFn fun i => ∫ ω, (query ω).getScalar i ∂μ)
        (Tensor.ofFn fun i => ∫ ω, (key ω).getScalar i ∂μ)
        (Tensor.matrix fun i j => covariance
          (fun ω => (query ω).getScalar i) (fun ω => (key ω).getScalar j) μ) := by
  simp_rw [score_eq_sum]
  rw [integral_finsetSum Finset.univ
    (f := fun i ω => (query ω).getScalar i * (key ω).getScalar i)
    (fun i _ => (hq i).integrable_mul (hk i))]
  simp only [estimate, score_eq_sum, vector_sum_eq, Tensor.getScalar_ofFn]
  simp only [matrix_entry, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => product_mean (hq i) (hk i)

/-- Projecting query and key with a symmetric idempotent matrix `P` loses `qᵀ (k - P k)`, the
score against the discarded part of the key. -/
theorem score_projection_error {d : Nat} (projection : Tensor ℝ [d, d])
    (hsym : ∀ i j : Fin d, projection[(i, j)] = projection[(j, i)])
    (hid : Tensor.matmul projection projection = projection) (query key : Tensor ℝ [d]) :
    score query key - score (Tensor.matvec projection query) (Tensor.matvec projection key) =
      score query (key - Tensor.matvec projection key) := by
  have hadjoint (x y : Tensor ℝ [d]) :
      score (Tensor.matvec projection x) y = score x (Tensor.matvec projection y) := by
    simp only [score_eq_sum, Tensor.matvec, Tensor.getScalar_contract_matVec_eq_sum,
      Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro j _
    change projection[(j, i)] * x.getScalar i * y.getScalar j =
      x.getScalar i * (projection[(i, j)] * y.getScalar j)
    rw [hsym j i]
    ring
  have htwice : Tensor.matvec projection (Tensor.matvec projection key) =
      Tensor.matvec projection key := by
    simp only [Tensor.matvec]
    rw [Tensor.contract_matVec_assoc, hid]
  rw [hadjoint, htwice]
  simp only [score_eq_sum, Tensor.getScalar_sub, mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]

end HeuristicEstimation.Attention

module

public import HeuristicEstimation.Basic
public import HeuristicEstimation.Composition

/-!
# Averaging a graph's discarded input

`Composition.eval_difference` splits a graph's output change into a pulled-back input change
and local nonlinear remainders. If the discarded input is centered for every retained state, the
pulled-back term averages to zero, and local certificates bound what remains.

Each row of `law` is the conditional distribution of the discarded state, so it is nonnegative
and sums to one. Centering is required of the graph inputs, coordinate by coordinate, and
uncorrelated intermediate activations don't imply it. Output seeds may depend on the retained
state but not on the discarded one, which is what lets the linear term cancel. Remainders at
later nodes need not be centered.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation.Averaging

open TorchLean
open Tape (Graph)
open scoped BigOperators

private theorem sum_dot_eq_zero {n : Nat} {shape : Shape}
    (weights : Fin n → ℝ) (values : Fin n → Tensor ℝ shape) (seed : Tensor ℝ shape)
    (hmean : ∀ coordinate, ∑ i : Fin n, weights i * values i coordinate = 0) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, weights i * Tensor.Rep.dot (values i) seed) = 0 := by
  have hdot (i : Fin n) : Tensor.Rep.dot (values i) seed =
      ∑ coordinate : shape.Coord, values i coordinate * seed coordinate := by
    rfl
  simp_rw [hdot, Finset.mul_sum, ← mul_assoc]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  simp_rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hmean, zero_mul, Finset.sum_const_zero]

private theorem sum_dotList_eq_zero {n : Nat} {shapes : List Shape}
    (weights : Fin n → ℝ) (values : Fin n → TensorPack ℝ shapes)
    (seed : TensorPack ℝ shapes)
    (hmean : ∀ (position : Fin shapes.length) (coordinate : (shapes.get position).Coord),
      ∑ i : Fin n, weights i * (values i).get position coordinate = 0) :
    (∑ i : Fin n,
      weights i * TensorPack.dotList (values i) seed) = 0 := by
  induction shapes with
  | nil =>
      have hnil (i : Fin n) :
          TensorPack.dotList (values i) seed = 0 := by
        cases values i
        cases seed
        rfl
      simp only [hnil, mul_zero, Finset.sum_const_zero]
  | cons shape shapes ih =>
      cases seed with
      | cons first rest =>
          have hhead (coordinate : shape.Coord) :
              ∑ i : Fin n, weights i * (values i).head coordinate = 0 := by
            convert hmean ⟨0, by simp⟩ coordinate using 1
            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
            intro i _
            cases values i
            rfl
          have htail (position : Fin shapes.length)
              (coordinate : (shapes.get position).Coord) :
              ∑ i : Fin n, weights i * (values i).tail.get position coordinate = 0 := by
            convert hmean position.succ coordinate using 1
            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
            intro i _
            cases values i
            rfl
          have hsplit (i : Fin n) :
              TensorPack.dotList (values i) (.cons first rest) =
                Tensor.Rep.dot (values i).head first +
                  TensorPack.dotList (values i).tail rest := by
            cases values i
            rfl
          simp_rw [hsplit, mul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
          rw [sum_dot_eq_zero weights _ first hhead, ih _ rest htail, zero_add]

private theorem abs_weighted_sum_le {n : Nat} (weights values bounds : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hweights : ∀ i, 0 ≤ weights i) (hbound : ∀ i, |values i| ≤ bounds i) :
    |∑ i : Fin n, weights i * values i| ≤ ∑ i : Fin n, weights i * bounds i := by
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin n, |weights i * values i| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => by
      rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (hweights i)]
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hbound i) (hweights i)

/-- Under conditional centering, the weighted mean output change equals the weighted mean of
the graph remainders. The outer weights need not be normalized. -/
theorem mean_difference {retained discarded : Nat} {data : Type}
    {inputs outputs : List Shape} (graph : Graph (α := ℝ) data inputs outputs)
    (weights : Tensor ℝ [retained]) (law : Tensor ℝ [retained, discarded])
    (values : Fin retained → Fin discarded → TensorPack ℝ inputs)
    (reference : Fin retained → TensorPack ℝ inputs) (parameters : data)
    (seed : Fin retained → TensorPack ℝ (inputs ++ outputs))
    (hmean : ∀ (i : Fin retained) (position : Fin inputs.length)
      (coordinate : (inputs.get position).Coord),
      ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
        (Composition.subtract (values i j) (reference i)).get position coordinate = 0) :
    (∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
      TensorPack.dotList
        (Composition.subtract (graph.toData.eval (values i j) parameters)
          (graph.toData.eval (reference i) parameters)) (seed i)) =
      ∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
        Composition.remainder graph.toData (values i j) (reference i) parameters (seed i) := by
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  congr 1
  simp_rw [Composition.eval_difference graph.toData graph.correct, mul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  rw [sum_dotList_eq_zero (fun j => law[(i, j)])
    (fun j => Composition.subtract (values i j) (reference i))
    (graph.toData.backpropCtx (reference i) parameters (seed i)) (hmean i), zero_add]

/-- Bounds on the graph remainder at every pair of states bound the expected output error. The
reference term is averaged over retained states only. With normalized outer weights, both sides
are expectations. -/
private theorem mean_error_le_of_bound {retained discarded : Nat} {data : Type}
    {inputs outputs : List Shape} (graph : Graph (α := ℝ) data inputs outputs)
    (weights : Tensor ℝ [retained]) (law budget : Tensor ℝ [retained, discarded])
    (values : Fin retained → Fin discarded → TensorPack ℝ inputs)
    (reference : Fin retained → TensorPack ℝ inputs) (parameters : data)
    (seed : Fin retained → TensorPack ℝ (inputs ++ outputs))
    (hweights : ∀ i : Fin retained, 0 ≤ weights.getScalar i)
    (hlaw : ∀ (i : Fin retained) (j : Fin discarded), 0 ≤ law[(i, j)])
    (hmass : ∀ i : Fin retained, ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] = 1)
    (hmean : ∀ (i : Fin retained) (position : Fin inputs.length)
      (coordinate : (inputs.get position).Coord),
      ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
        (Composition.subtract (values i j) (reference i)).get position coordinate = 0)
    (hbound : ∀ (i : Fin retained) (j : Fin discarded),
      |Composition.remainder graph.toData (values i j) (reference i) parameters (seed i)| ≤
        budget[(i, j)]) :
    |(∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
      TensorPack.dotList (graph.toData.eval (values i j) parameters) (seed i)) -
      (∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i *
        TensorPack.dotList
          (graph.toData.eval (reference i) parameters) (seed i))| ≤
      ∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * ∑ j : Fin discarded,
        law[(i, j)] * budget[(i, j)] := by
  have hdifference :
      (∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
        TensorPack.dotList (graph.toData.eval (values i j) parameters) (seed i)) -
        (∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i *
          TensorPack.dotList
            (graph.toData.eval (reference i) parameters) (seed i)) =
      ∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
        TensorPack.dotList
          (Composition.subtract (graph.toData.eval (values i j) parameters)
            (graph.toData.eval (reference i) parameters)) (seed i) := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    simp_rw [Composition.dotList_sub_left, mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hmass i, one_mul, mul_sub]
  rw [hdifference, mean_difference graph weights law values reference parameters seed hmean]
  apply abs_weighted_sum_le _ _ _ hweights
  intro i
  exact abs_weighted_sum_le _ _ _ (hlaw i) (hbound i)

/-- Local remainder certificates bound the expected output error by a budget computed from
retained states alone. One radius pack per retained state must cover every discarded state in
its row. Producing those radii is a separate, operation-specific job. -/
theorem mean_error_le {retained discarded : Nat} {data : Type}
    {inputs outputs : List Shape} (graph : Graph (α := ℝ) data inputs outputs)
    (weights : Tensor ℝ [retained]) (law : Tensor ℝ [retained, discarded])
    (values : Fin retained → Fin discarded → TensorPack ℝ inputs)
    (reference : Fin retained → TensorPack ℝ inputs) (parameters : data)
    (seed : Fin retained → TensorPack ℝ (inputs ++ outputs))
    (radii : Fin retained → TensorPack ℝ outputs)
    (hweights : ∀ i : Fin retained, 0 ≤ weights.getScalar i)
    (hlaw : ∀ (i : Fin retained) (j : Fin discarded), 0 ≤ law[(i, j)])
    (hmass : ∀ i : Fin retained, ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] = 1)
    (hmean : ∀ (i : Fin retained) (position : Fin inputs.length)
      (coordinate : (inputs.get position).Coord),
      ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
        (Composition.subtract (values i j) (reference i)).get position coordinate = 0)
    (hlocal : ∀ (i : Fin retained) (j : Fin discarded),
      Composition.Within graph.toData (values i j) (reference i) parameters (radii i)) :
    |(∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
      TensorPack.dotList (graph.toData.eval (values i j) parameters) (seed i)) -
      (∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i *
        TensorPack.dotList
          (graph.toData.eval (reference i) parameters) (seed i))| ≤
      ∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i *
        Composition.bound graph.toData (reference i) parameters (seed i) (radii i) := by
  let budget := Tensor.matrix fun i (_ : Fin discarded) =>
    Composition.bound graph.toData (reference i) parameters (seed i) (radii i)
  have hbound (i : Fin retained) (j : Fin discarded) :
      |Composition.remainder graph.toData (values i j) (reference i) parameters (seed i)| ≤
        budget[(i, j)] := by
    dsimp only [budget]
    rw [matrix_entry]
    exact Composition.remainder_le_bound graph.toData _ _ _ _ _ (hlocal i j)
  have h := mean_error_le_of_bound graph weights law budget values reference parameters seed
    hweights hlaw hmass hmean hbound

module

public import Mathlib.Probability.Moments.Covariance
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Context.Real
public import TorchLean.Tensor.LinearAlgebra.Real
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Operations
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Reduce.Real

/-!
# Shared inputs and expectation identities

The four equally weighted positions of `signs` and `independentSigns` enumerate two independent
signs. Feeding one of them into both factors of `response` creates a correlation that mean-only
propagation discards. Definitions work over any scalar type, and the probability results are
stated over ℝ.

`projection_error` measures what is lost when a partial result is replaced before a later
multiplication.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation

open TorchLean MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

/-- Entry `(i, j)` of `Tensor.matrix f` is `f i j`. -/
theorem matrix_entry {α : Type} [Storage α] {m n : Nat}
    (f : Fin m → Fin n → α) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n) :
    (Tensor.matrix f)[(i, j)] = f i j := by
  change (Tensor.unstack (Tensor.matrix f) i).getScalar j = _
  simp [Tensor.matrix]

/-- Multiply one input by a mixture of itself and a second input, entry by entry. -/
def response {α : Type} [Storage α] [One α] [Mul α] [Add α] [Sub α]
    {shape : Shape} (shared : α) (x z : Tensor α shape) : Tensor α shape :=
  x * (x.scale shared + z.scale (1 - shared))

/-- Coordinatewise form of `response`. -/
theorem response_apply {α : Type} [Storage α] [One α] [Mul α] [Add α] [Sub α]
    {shape : Shape} (shared : α) (x z : Tensor α shape) (i : shape.Coord) :
    response shared x z i = x i * (x i * shared + z i * (1 - shared)) := by
  simp [response, Tensor.scale]

/-- The scalar sum of a vector equals the finite sum over its indices. -/
theorem vector_sum_eq {α : Type} [Storage α] [AddCommMonoid α] {n : Nat}
    (values : Tensor α [n]) :
    values.sum = ∑ i : Fin n, values.getScalar i := by
  classical
  rw [Tensor.sum_eq_coord_sum, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  simp [Tensor.getScalar_eq_apply]

/-- Reduce the sole axis of a vector to its scalar mean. -/
def vectorMean {α : Type} [Storage α] [Context α] {n : Nat} (values : Tensor α [n]) : α :=
  Tensor.item (Tensor.castShape (Tensor.mean values (List.finRange (Shape.rank [n])) false)
    (Shape.reduce_finRange [n]))

/-- The real vector mean divides the coordinate sum by the totalized vector length. -/
theorem vectorMean_eq {n : Nat} (values : Tensor ℝ [n]) :
    vectorMean values = (∑ i : Fin n, values.getScalar i) / (Tensor.meanDenominator [n] : ℝ) := by
  rw [vectorMean, Tensor.mean_finRange_item, Context.divNat_real, vector_sum_eq]

/-- First coordinates of the four equally likely sign pairs. -/
def signs {α : Type} [Storage α] [One α] [Neg α] : Tensor α [4] :=
  Tensor.ofFn fun i => if i.val < 2 then -1 else 1

/-- Second coordinates of the same pairs. With `signs`, the four positions enumerate the product
of two independent fair signs. -/
def independentSigns {α : Type} [Storage α] [One α] [Neg α] : Tensor α [4] :=
  Tensor.ofFn fun i => if i.val % 2 = 0 then -1 else 1

/-- Averaged over the four pairs, the response is `shared`, for every real `shared`. -/
theorem response_mean (shared : ℝ) :
    vectorMean (response shared (signs : Tensor ℝ [4]) independentSigns) = shared := by
  rw [vectorMean_eq]
  simp [Tensor.getScalar_eq_apply, response_apply, signs, independentSigns, Tensor.ofFn,
    Fin.sum_univ_succ, Tensor.meanDenominator, Shape.size]
  ring

/-- Over the four pairs, the response has population variance `(1 - shared) ^ 2`. -/
theorem response_variance (shared : ℝ) :
    vectorMean (Tensor.square
      (response shared (signs : Tensor ℝ [4]) independentSigns - Tensor.full [4] shared)) =
      (1 - shared) ^ 2 := by
  rw [vectorMean_eq]
  simp [Tensor.getScalar_eq_apply, Tensor.square,
    response_apply, signs, independentSigns, Tensor.ofFn, Fin.sum_univ_succ,
    Tensor.meanDenominator, Shape.size]
  ring

/-- The mean of a product is the product of the means plus the covariance. Both factors need
finite second moments, and nothing is assumed about how they depend on each other. -/
theorem product_mean {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {x y : Ω → ℝ} (hx : MemLp x 2 μ) (hy : MemLp y 2 μ) :
    (∫ ω, x ω * y ω ∂μ) =
      (∫ ω, x ω ∂μ) * (∫ ω, y ω ∂μ) + covariance x y μ := by
  rw [covariance_eq_sub hx hy]
  simp only [Pi.mul_apply]
  ring

/-- A surrogate's mean plus the mean of its residual is the target's mean. Control variates rest
on this identity. -/
theorem residual_correction {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    {target surrogate : Ω → ℝ} (ht : Integrable target μ) (hs : Integrable surrogate μ) :
    (∫ ω, surrogate ω ∂μ) + (∫ ω, target ω - surrogate ω ∂μ) =
      ∫ ω, target ω ∂μ := by
  rw [integral_sub ht hs]
  ring

/-- Replacing `head` by `sketch` before multiplying by `tail` changes the mean by
`E[tail * (head - sketch)]`. A projection rule has to control this correlation between the
later factor and the discarded part. -/
theorem projection_error {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    {tail head sketch : Ω → ℝ}
    (hh : Integrable (fun ω => tail ω * head ω) μ)
    (hs : Integrable (fun ω => tail ω * sketch ω) μ) :
    (∫ ω, tail ω * head ω ∂μ) - (∫ ω, tail ω * sketch ω ∂μ) =
      ∫ ω, tail ω * (head ω - sketch ω) ∂μ := by
  simp_rw [mul_sub]
  exact (integral_sub hh hs).symm

end HeuristicEstimation
