module

public import HeuristicEstimation.Basic
public import TorchLean.NN.Op.Piecewise

/-!
# Expected error at a ReLU boundary

Replacing a conditionally centered perturbation by zero removes its linear contribution to a
ReLU's expected output. What remains is nonnegative, and it vanishes unless the center lies
within the perturbation radius of zero. In `mean_error_le` the perturbation's law may depend on
the retained state, but its mean must vanish for each retained state separately.

The sensitivity may depend on the retained state too. It stays inside the weighted sum, so its
correlation with the boundary event is kept.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation.Boundary

open TorchLean
open scoped BigOperators

/-- What remains of `relu (center + perturbation)` after linearizing ReLU at `center`. The
slope at zero is taken to be zero. -/
noncomputable def remainder (center perturbation : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Activation.relu (center + perturbation) - Activation.relu center -
    if 0 < center then perturbation else 0

/-- The remainder is nonnegative: ReLU lies above its linearization at every center, zero
included. -/
theorem remainder_nonneg (center perturbation : ℝ) : 0 ≤ remainder center perturbation := by
  unfold remainder
  simp only [Activation.relu_eq_max]
  by_cases hcenter : 0 < center
  · rw [ite_eq_left hcenter, max_eq_left hcenter.le]
    have h := le_max_left (center + perturbation) 0
    linarith
  · rw [ite_eq_right hcenter, max_eq_right (le_of_not_gt hcenter)]
    have h := le_max_right (center + perturbation) 0
    linarith

/-- A perturbation of size at most `radius` leaves a remainder of at most
`max 0 (radius - |center|)`, the distance it can carry the input past zero. A center at least
`radius` from zero leaves none. -/
theorem remainder_le (center perturbation radius : ℝ) (hperturbation : |perturbation| ≤ radius) :
    remainder center perturbation ≤ max 0 (radius - |center|) := by
  have hbounds := abs_le.mp hperturbation
  unfold remainder
  simp only [Activation.relu_eq_max]
  by_cases hcenter : 0 < center
  · rw [ite_eq_left hcenter, max_eq_left hcenter.le, abs_of_pos hcenter]
    by_cases hpositive : 0 ≤ center + perturbation
    · rw [max_eq_left hpositive]
      linarith [le_max_left 0 (radius - center)]
    · rw [max_eq_right (le_of_not_ge hpositive)]
      linarith [le_max_right 0 (radius - center)]
  · rw [ite_eq_right hcenter, max_eq_right (le_of_not_gt hcenter),
      abs_of_nonpos (le_of_not_gt hcenter)]
    by_cases hpositive : 0 ≤ center + perturbation
    · rw [max_eq_left hpositive]
      linarith [le_max_right 0 (radius - -center)]
    · rw [max_eq_right (le_of_not_ge hpositive)]
      linarith [le_max_left 0 (radius - -center)]

/-- Coarser form of `remainder_le`: at most `radius` when `|center| ≤ radius`, else zero. -/
theorem remainder_le_boundary (center perturbation radius : ℝ)
    (hperturbation : |perturbation| ≤ radius) :
    remainder center perturbation ≤ if |center| ≤ radius then radius else 0 := by
  apply (remainder_le center perturbation radius hperturbation).trans
  by_cases h : |center| ≤ radius
  · rw [ite_eq_left h]
    exact max_le ((abs_nonneg perturbation).trans hperturbation)
      (sub_le_self _ (abs_nonneg _))
  · rw [ite_eq_right h]
    exact max_le le_rfl (sub_nonpos.mpr (le_of_not_ge h))

/-- The Jacobian-vector product registered for TorchLean's ReLU. -/
noncomputable def reluJvp {shape : Shape} (reference direction : Tensor ℝ shape) :
    Tensor ℝ shape :=
  let rule := ((Op.relu (s := shape)).rule? (α := ℝ)).get (by rw [Op.rule?_relu]; rfl)
  let applyJvp := rule.jvp?.get rfl
  (applyJvp (reference, ()) (direction, ())).1

/-- Subtracting TorchLean's ReLU JVP from the change in output leaves `remainder` in every
coordinate, so `remainder` and the JVP use the same slope at zero. -/
theorem relu_remainder_eq {shape : Shape} (actual reference : Tensor ℝ shape) :
    Tensor.relu actual - Tensor.relu reference - reluJvp reference (actual - reference) =
      Tensor.zipWith remainder reference (actual - reference) := by
  apply Tensor.Rep.ext
  intro coordinate
  have hshift : reference coordinate + (actual coordinate - reference coordinate) =
      actual coordinate := by ring
  change (Tensor.relu actual - Tensor.relu reference -
      Tensor.map Activation.reluDeriv reference * (actual - reference)) coordinate = _
  simp only [Tensor.relu, Tensor.map_apply, Tensor.mul_apply, Tensor.Rep.hSub_apply,
    Tensor.zipWith_apply, Activation.reluDeriv, remainder]
  by_cases h : 0 < reference coordinate <;> simp [h, hshift]

/-- Paired with a cotangent `seed`, the ReLU remainder is at most
`∑ |seed| * max 0 (radius - |reference|)` in absolute value, for any tensor shape. -/
theorem relu_error_le {shape : Shape} (actual reference radius seed : Tensor ℝ shape)
    (hperturbation : ∀ coordinate : shape.Coord,
      |actual coordinate - reference coordinate| ≤ radius coordinate) :
    |Tensor.Rep.dot
      (Tensor.relu actual - Tensor.relu reference - reluJvp reference (actual - reference)) seed| ≤
      ∑ coordinate : shape.Coord, |seed coordinate| *
        max 0 (radius coordinate - |reference coordinate|) := by
  classical
  rw [relu_remainder_eq]
  simp only [Tensor.Rep.dot, Tensor.zipWith_apply, Tensor.Rep.hSub_apply]
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ coordinate : shape.Coord,
        |remainder (reference coordinate) (actual coordinate - reference coordinate) *
          seed coordinate| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ = ∑ coordinate : shape.Coord, |seed coordinate| *
        remainder (reference coordinate) (actual coordinate - reference coordinate) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro coordinate _
      rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (remainder_nonneg _ _), mul_comm]
    _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_le_sum fun coordinate _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
      (remainder_le _ _ _ (hperturbation coordinate)) (abs_nonneg _)

/-- If the perturbation is centered under `law` for every retained state, the linear term
cancels, and the sensitivity-weighted mean change in ReLU output is at most
`∑ wᵢ * |sᵢ| * max 0 (rᵢ - |cᵢ|)` in absolute value. Retained weights need not sum to one.
When they do, both sides are expectations under the finite conditional law. -/
theorem mean_error_le {retained discarded : Nat}
    (weights center radius sensitivity : Tensor ℝ [retained])
    (law perturbation : Tensor ℝ [retained, discarded])
    (hweights : ∀ i : Fin retained, 0 ≤ weights.getScalar i)
    (hlaw : ∀ (i : Fin retained) (j : Fin discarded), 0 ≤ law[(i, j)])
    (hmass : ∀ i : Fin retained, ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] = 1)
    (hmean : ∀ i : Fin retained,
      ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] * perturbation[(i, j)] = 0)
    (hperturbation : ∀ (i : Fin retained) (j : Fin discarded),
      |perturbation[(i, j)]| ≤ radius.getScalar i) :
    |∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * sensitivity.getScalar i *
      ((∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
        Activation.relu (center.getScalar i + perturbation[(i, j)])) -
          Activation.relu (center.getScalar i))| ≤
      ∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * |sensitivity.getScalar i| *
        max 0 (radius.getScalar i - |center.getScalar i|) := by
  classical
  let residual := fun i : Fin retained => ∑ j : Fin discarded,
    law[(i, j)] * remainder (center.getScalar i) perturbation[(i, j)]
  let budget := fun i : Fin retained =>
    max 0 (radius.getScalar i - |center.getScalar i|)
  have heq (i : Fin retained) :
      (∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] *
        Activation.relu (center.getScalar i + perturbation[(i, j)])) -
          Activation.relu (center.getScalar i) = residual i := by
    dsimp [residual]
    by_cases h : 0 < center.getScalar i <;>
      simp [remainder, h, mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, ← Finset.sum_mul, hmass, hmean]
  have hnonneg (i : Fin retained) : 0 ≤ residual i :=
    Finset.sum_nonneg fun j _ => mul_nonneg (hlaw i j) (remainder_nonneg _ _)
  have hbound (i : Fin retained) : residual i ≤ budget i := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ j : Fin discarded, law[(i, j)] * budget i :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
          (remainder_le _ _ _ (hperturbation i j)) (hlaw i j)
      _ = _ := by rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hmass, one_mul]
  simp_rw [heq]
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin retained,
        |weights.getScalar i * sensitivity.getScalar i * residual i| :=
      Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ = ∑ i : Fin retained, weights.getScalar i * |sensitivity.getScalar i| * residual i := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i _
      rw [abs_mul, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (hweights i), abs_of_nonneg (hnonneg i)]
    _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hbound i)
      (mul_nonneg (hweights i) (abs_nonneg _))

end HeuristicEstimation.Boundary

module

public import TorchLean.NN.Tape.Graph
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Reduce.Real
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Group.Finset
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# Output discrepancies weighted by the existing reverse pass

Two executions of the same TorchLean graph are compared node by node. At each node, the change
in output minus the node's JVP at the reference execution is a local remainder. Each remainder
reaches the final answer through the cotangent of TorchLean's reverse pass.

`eval_difference` is an identity and needs no smoothness. It uses only each node's JVP/VJP
adjoint law, so it covers piecewise-linear nodes with a fixed convention at their kinks.
`remainder_le_bound` bounds the total remainder from local certificates, and `Averaging` cancels
the input term in expectation.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation.Composition

open TorchLean Tape
open Tensor.Rep (dot)
open scoped BigOperators

variable {α : Type} [Storage α]

/-- Subtract corresponding tensors in two contexts of the same shapes. -/
abbrev subtract [Sub α] {shapes : List Shape} (left right : TensorPack α shapes) :
    TensorPack α shapes :=
  Pack.zipWith (· - ·) left right

variable [CommRing α]

/-- Subtracting tensors subtracts their pairings with a fixed output cotangent. -/
theorem dot_sub_left {shape : Shape} (left right seed : Tensor α shape) :
    dot (left - right) seed = dot left seed - dot right seed := by
  have cancel : left - right + right = left := sub_add_cancel _ _
  have paired := congrArg (fun value => dot value seed) cancel
  rw [Tensor.dot_add_left] at paired
  exact eq_sub_of_add_eq paired

/-- For a typed context of tensors too, the pairing of a difference is the difference of the
pairings. -/
theorem dotList_sub_left {shapes : List Shape}
    (left right seed : TorchLean.TensorPack α shapes) :
    TensorPack.dotList (subtract left right) seed =
      TensorPack.dotList left seed - TensorPack.dotList right seed := by
  induction shapes with
  | nil =>
      cases left; cases right; cases seed
      simp [subtract, TensorPack.dotList]
  | cons shape shapes ih =>
      cases left with
      | cons first rest =>
          cases right with
          | cons other remaining =>
              cases seed with
              | cons output outputs =>
                  change dot (first - other) output +
                    TensorPack.dotList (subtract rest remaining) outputs =
                      (dot first output + TensorPack.dotList rest outputs) -
                        (dot other output + TensorPack.dotList remaining outputs)
                  rw [dot_sub_left, ih]
                  ring

private theorem sub_cast {before after : List Shape} (same : before = after)
    (left right : TorchLean.TensorPack α before) :
    subtract (Pack.cast same left)
        (Pack.cast same right) =
      Pack.cast same (subtract left right) := by
  cases same
  rfl

/-- Part of a node's output change that its JVP at the reference inputs does not explain. -/
def nodeRemainder {data : Type} {inputs : List Shape} {output : Shape}
    (node : NodeData α data inputs output)
    (values reference : TorchLean.TensorPack α inputs) (parameters : data) : Tensor α output :=
  node.forward values parameters - node.forward reference parameters -
    node.jvp reference (subtract values reference) parameters

/-- Paired with `seed`, a node's output change is its input change paired with the VJP of
`seed`, plus the paired remainder. -/
theorem node_difference {data : Type} {inputs : List Shape} {output : Shape}
    (node : NodeData α data inputs output) (correct : node.Correct)
    (values reference : TorchLean.TensorPack α inputs) (parameters : data)
    (seed : Tensor α output) :
    dot (node.forward values parameters - node.forward reference parameters)
        seed =
      TensorPack.dotList (subtract values reference)
          (node.vjp reference parameters seed) +
        dot (nodeRemainder node values reference parameters) seed := by
  simp only [nodeRemainder, dot_sub_left, correct reference (subtract values reference)
    parameters seed]
  ring

/-- Sum of node remainders, each paired with its cotangent from the reference reverse pass.

The recursion follows `GraphData.backpropCtx`, with the same saved reference values, VJPs and context
addition.
-/
def remainder {data : Type} {inputs : List Shape} {outputs : List Shape}
    (graph : GraphData α data inputs outputs)
    (values reference : TorchLean.TensorPack α inputs) (parameters : data)
    (seed : TorchLean.TensorPack α (inputs ++ outputs)) : α :=
  match graph with
  | .nil => 0
  | .snoc (ss := previousShapes) (τ := output) previous node =>
      let previousSeed := Pack.cast
        (List.append_assoc inputs previousShapes [output]).symm seed
      let split := Pack.unsnoc previousSeed
      let referenceContext := previous.eval reference parameters
      let contribution := node.vjp referenceContext parameters split.2
      remainder previous values reference parameters
          (TorchLean.TensorPack.add split.1 contribution) +
        dot (nodeRemainder node (previous.eval values parameters) referenceContext parameters)
          split.2

/-- A graph's paired output change is its input change paired with the reverse-pass cotangent,
plus `remainder`. The seed covers the whole typed context, so shared nodes and seeds on
intermediate values are included. -/
theorem eval_difference {data : Type} {inputs : List Shape} {outputs : List Shape}
    (graph : GraphData α data inputs outputs) (correct : graph.Correct) :
    ∀ (values reference : TorchLean.TensorPack α inputs) (parameters : data)
      (seed : TorchLean.TensorPack α (inputs ++ outputs)),
      TensorPack.dotList
          (subtract (graph.eval values parameters)
            (graph.eval reference parameters))
          seed =
        TensorPack.dotList (subtract values reference)
            (graph.backpropCtx reference parameters seed) +
          remainder graph values reference parameters seed := by
  induction graph with
  | nil =>
      intro values reference parameters seed
      simp only [GraphData.eval, GraphData.backpropCtx, remainder, sub_cast,
        TensorPack.dotList_cast_left, add_zero]
  | snoc previous node ih =>
      intro values reference parameters seed
      rename_i previousShapes output
      obtain ⟨previousCorrect, nodeCorrect⟩ := correct
      let fullContext := previous.eval values parameters
      let referenceContext := previous.eval reference parameters
      let same : (inputs ++ previousShapes) ++ [output] =
          inputs ++ (previousShapes ++ [output]) := List.append_assoc inputs previousShapes [output]
      let previousSeed := Pack.cast same.symm seed
      let split := Pack.unsnoc previousSeed
      let contribution := node.vjp referenceContext parameters split.2
      let accumulated := TorchLean.TensorPack.add split.1 contribution
      have seed_split : Pack.snoc split.1 split.2 = previousSeed :=
        Pack.snoc_unsnoc previousSeed
      have output_split :
          TensorPack.dotList
              (subtract ((GraphData.snoc previous node).eval values parameters)
                ((GraphData.snoc previous node).eval reference parameters)) seed =
            TensorPack.dotList (subtract fullContext referenceContext) split.1 +
              dot (node.forward fullContext parameters -
                node.forward referenceContext parameters) split.2 := by
        change TensorPack.dotList
            (subtract
              (Pack.cast same
                (Pack.snoc fullContext (node.forward fullContext parameters)))
              (Pack.cast same
                (Pack.snoc referenceContext
                  (node.forward referenceContext parameters)))) seed = _
        rw [sub_cast, TensorPack.dotList_cast_left, dotList_sub_left]
        change TensorPack.dotList
              (Pack.snoc fullContext (node.forward fullContext parameters))
              previousSeed -
            TensorPack.dotList
              (Pack.snoc referenceContext
                (node.forward referenceContext parameters))
              previousSeed = _
        rw [← seed_split, TensorPack.dotList_snoc, TensorPack.dotList_snoc,
          dotList_sub_left, dot_sub_left]
        ring
      calc
        _ = TensorPack.dotList (subtract fullContext referenceContext) split.1 +
            dot (node.forward fullContext parameters -
              node.forward referenceContext parameters) split.2 := output_split
        _ = TensorPack.dotList (subtract fullContext referenceContext) accumulated +
            dot (nodeRemainder node fullContext referenceContext parameters) split.2 := by
              rw [node_difference node nodeCorrect, TensorPack.dotList_add_right]
              ring
        _ = TensorPack.dotList (subtract values reference)
              (previous.backpropCtx reference parameters accumulated) +
            (remainder previous values reference parameters accumulated +
              dot (nodeRemainder node fullContext referenceContext parameters) split.2) := by
              rw [ih previousCorrect]
              ring
        _ = _ := rfl

/-! ## Bounds from local tensor certificates -/

/-- Coordinatewise bounds on `error` bound its pairing with any cotangent `seed` by the pairing
of `|seed|` with `radius`. -/
theorem dot_abs_le {shape : Shape} (error seed radius : Tensor ℝ shape)
    (within : ∀ coordinate, |error coordinate| ≤ radius coordinate) :
    |dot error seed| ≤ dot (Tensor.map abs seed) radius := by
  classical
  simp only [Tensor.Rep.dot, Tensor.map_apply]
  calc
    |∑ coordinate : shape.Coord, error coordinate * seed coordinate| ≤
        ∑ coordinate : shape.Coord, |error coordinate * seed coordinate| :=
      Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ ≤ ∑ coordinate : shape.Coord, |seed coordinate| * radius coordinate := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro coordinate _
      rw [abs_mul, mul_comm]
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (within coordinate) (abs_nonneg _)

/-- Each radius tensor bounds the remainder of its node, coordinate by coordinate.

This is the local proof obligation for whatever computes the radii, typically from the reference
execution and the input region.
-/
def Within {data : Type} {inputs : List Shape} {outputs : List Shape}
    (graph : GraphData ℝ data inputs outputs)
    (values reference : TorchLean.TensorPack ℝ inputs) (parameters : data)
    (radii : TorchLean.TensorPack ℝ outputs) : Prop :=
  match graph with
  | .nil => True
  | .snoc previous node =>
      let split := Pack.unsnoc radii
      Within previous values reference parameters split.1 ∧
        ∀ coordinate,
          |nodeRemainder node (previous.eval values parameters)
            (previous.eval reference parameters) parameters coordinate| ≤ split.2 coordinate

/-- Budget for `remainder`: local radii paired with absolute cotangents from the reference
reverse pass.

Only the reference execution is evaluated. Cotangents still accumulate at shared nodes as they
do in the reverse pass.
-/
noncomputable def bound {data : Type} {inputs : List Shape} {outputs : List Shape}
    (graph : GraphData ℝ data inputs outputs)
    (reference : TorchLean.TensorPack ℝ inputs) (parameters : data)
    (seed : TorchLean.TensorPack ℝ (inputs ++ outputs))
    (radii : TorchLean.TensorPack ℝ outputs) : ℝ :=
  match graph with
  | .nil => 0
  | .snoc (ss := previousShapes) (τ := output) previous node =>
      let previousSeed := Pack.cast
        (List.append_assoc inputs previousShapes [output]).symm seed
      let splitSeed := Pack.unsnoc previousSeed
      let splitRadius := Pack.unsnoc radii
      let referenceContext := previous.eval reference parameters
      let contribution := node.vjp referenceContext parameters splitSeed.2
      bound previous reference parameters
          (TorchLean.TensorPack.add splitSeed.1 contribution) splitRadius.1 +
        dot (Tensor.map abs splitSeed.2) splitRadius.2

/-- Local remainder certificates (`Within`) bound the whole graph remainder by `bound`, which
uses only the reference execution. -/
theorem remainder_le_bound {data : Type} {inputs : List Shape} {outputs : List Shape}
    (graph : GraphData ℝ data inputs outputs) :
    ∀ (values reference : TorchLean.TensorPack ℝ inputs) (parameters : data)
      (seed : TorchLean.TensorPack ℝ (inputs ++ outputs))
      (radii : TorchLean.TensorPack ℝ outputs),
      Within graph values reference parameters radii →
        |remainder graph values reference parameters seed| ≤
          bound graph reference parameters seed radii := by
  induction graph with
  | nil =>
      intro values reference parameters seed radii _
      simp only [remainder, bound, abs_zero, le_refl]
  | snoc previous node ih =>
      intro values reference parameters seed radii within
      rename_i previousShapes output
      let previousSeed := Pack.cast
        (List.append_assoc inputs previousShapes [output]).symm seed
      let splitSeed := Pack.unsnoc previousSeed
      let splitRadius := Pack.unsnoc radii
      let contribution := node.vjp (previous.eval reference parameters) parameters splitSeed.2
      let accumulated := TorchLean.TensorPack.add splitSeed.1 contribution

          dot (Tensor.map abs splitSeed.2) splitRadius.2

module

public import HeuristicEstimation.Sketch
public import FloatLib.Numerics.Quantization.Deterministic.Rational

/-!
# Finite-precision sketch coefficients

FloatLib supplies executable nearest-even rounding of rationals to integers, with a proved
half-unit error. Scaling it gives `round`, which encodes onto a grid of any positive rational
spacing with error at most half the spacing. This is a fixed grid, not an IEEE format with a
finite exponent range.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation.Encoding

open TorchLean Sketch
open scoped BigOperators

/-- Nearest-even rounding of `value` to a multiple of `spacing`, using FloatLib. -/
def round (spacing value : Rat) : Rat :=
  spacing * (FloatLib.Numerics.roundRatEven (value / spacing) : Rat)

/-- Rounding moves a value by at most half the spacing, ties included. -/
theorem round_error {spacing : Rat} (hspacing : 0 < spacing) (value : Rat) :
    |round spacing value - value| ≤ spacing / 2 := by
  have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
    (FloatLib.Numerics.roundRatEven_error_le_half (value / spacing)) hspacing.le
  calc
    _ = |spacing * ((FloatLib.Numerics.roundRatEven (value / spacing) : Rat) -
        value / spacing)| := by
      congr 1
      dsimp [round]
      field_simp
    _ = spacing * |(FloatLib.Numerics.roundRatEven (value / spacing) : Rat) -
        value / spacing| := by rw [abs_mul, abs_of_pos hspacing]
    _ ≤ _ := by simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv, one_mul] using h

/-- Rounding every coordinate leaves an error vector of energy at most `d * (spacing / 2) ^ 2`. -/
theorem energy_round_error {d : Nat} {spacing : Rat} (hspacing : 0 < spacing)
    (values : Tensor Rat [d]) :
    energy (Tensor.ofFn fun i => round spacing (values.getScalar i) - values.getScalar i) ≤
      (d : Rat) * (spacing / 2) ^ 2 := by
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ _i : Fin d, (spacing / 2) ^ 2 := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro i _
      simp only [Tensor.getScalar_ofFn]
      have h := (sq_le_sq₀ (abs_nonneg _) (by positivity : 0 ≤ spacing / 2)).mpr
        (round_error hspacing (values.getScalar i))
      simpa only [sq_abs] using h
    _ = _ := by simp

/-- Energy of a sum is at most twice the sum of the energies. The factor two pays for the
cross-term between arbitrary vectors. Vectors with disjoint supports, as in a coordinate
sketch, would not need it. -/
theorem energy_add_le {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommRing α] [LinearOrder α]
    [IsStrictOrderedRing α] {d : Nat} (residual rounding : Tensor α [d]) :
    energy (Tensor.ofFn fun i => residual.getScalar i + rounding.getScalar i) ≤
      2 * energy residual + 2 * energy rounding := by
  simp only [energy, Tensor.getScalar_ofFn, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro i _
  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (residual.getScalar i - rounding.getScalar i)]

/-- A passing Gram check also bounds downstream error after the coefficients are rounded. The
energies of `discarded` and of the rounding error each enter with factor `2 * bound`
(`energy_add_le`), so the two may overlap. -/
theorem encoded_error_le {contexts d : Nat} (weights : Tensor Rat [contexts])
    (tails : Tensor Rat [contexts, d]) (bound : Rat) (hbound : 0 ≤ bound)
    (hcheck : check (gram weights tails) bound = true) {spacing : Rat}
    (hspacing : 0 < spacing) (discarded coefficients : Tensor Rat [d]) :
    error weights tails (Tensor.ofFn fun i => discarded.getScalar i +
      (round spacing (coefficients.getScalar i) - coefficients.getScalar i)) ≤
        2 * bound * energy discarded + 2 * bound * (d : Rat) * (spacing / 2) ^ 2 := by
  let rounding : Tensor Rat [d] := Tensor.ofFn fun i =>
    round spacing (coefficients.getScalar i) - coefficients.getScalar i
  have hadd := energy_add_le discarded rounding
  have hround := energy_round_error hspacing coefficients
  calc
    _ ≤ bound * energy (Tensor.ofFn fun i => discarded.getScalar i + rounding.getScalar i) := by
      simpa only [rounding, Tensor.getScalar_ofFn] using
        error_le_of_check weights tails bound hcheck
          (Tensor.ofFn fun i => discarded.getScalar i + rounding.getScalar i)
    _ ≤ bound * (2 * energy discarded + 2 * energy rounding) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hadd hbound
    _ ≤ _ := by
      have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hround (by positivity : 0 ≤ 2 * bound)
      dsimp [rounding] at *
      nlinarith

end HeuristicEstimation.Encoding

module

public import Mathlib.Probability.CDF
public import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Real
public import TorchLean.Tensor.Layers.Activation

/-!
# ReLU moments of a Gaussian preactivation

Let `Z` have law `gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2)` with `0 < σ`. Write `φ` for the standard normal density
`gaussianPDFReal 0 1` and `Φ` for mathlib's distribution function `cdf (gaussianReal 0 1)`, so
`Φ t` is the probability that a standard normal variable is at most `t`. Then

* `E[ReLU Z] = μ Φ(μ / σ) + σ φ(μ / σ)` (`relu_mean`),
* `E[(ReLU Z)²] = (μ² + σ²) Φ(μ / σ) + μ σ φ(μ / σ)` (`relu_second_moment`).

With `μ = 0` these are `σ / √(2π)` and `σ² / 2`. Both moments are integrals over `(0, ∞)`
against the density. Since `x - μ` times the density is `-σ²` times its derivative, the
fundamental theorem of calculus evaluates them.

Covariance propagation passes means and covariances through affine layers exactly
(`Moments.affine_mean`, `Moments.affine_covariance`) and applies these formulas at each ReLU.
This makes the per-neuron ReLU moment rule exact whenever the preactivation is Gaussian, so
its error in the estimator comes only from treating non-Gaussian preactivations as Gaussian,
which is the closure. The covariance of two different ReLU outputs needs the bivariate
Gaussian formula, which is not proved here.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation.Gaussian

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Filter Topology Real TorchLean
open scoped NNReal

/-- The Gaussian density solves `p' = -((x - μ) / v) p`. -/
private theorem hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal (μ : ℝ) {v : ℝ≥0} (hv : v ≠ 0) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (gaussianPDFReal μ v) (-((x - μ) / v) * gaussianPDFReal μ v x) x := by
  have hv' : (v : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hv
  have hsq : HasDerivAt (fun x => (x - μ) ^ 2) (2 * (x - μ)) x := by
    simpa using ((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const μ).fun_pow 2
  have hexponent : HasDerivAt (fun x => -(x - μ) ^ 2 / (2 * (v : ℝ))) (-((x - μ) / v)) x := by
    convert hsq.neg.div_const (2 * (v : ℝ)) using 1
    field_simp
  rw [gaussianPDFReal_def]
  convert hexponent.exp.const_mul (√(2 * π * v))⁻¹ using 1
  ring

/-- A function integrable for `gaussianReal μ v` is Lebesgue integrable after weighting by the
density. -/
private theorem integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul {μ : ℝ} {v : ℝ≥0} (hv : v ≠ 0) {g : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hg : Integrable g (gaussianReal μ v)) :
    Integrable (fun x => gaussianPDFReal μ v x * g x) := by
  rw [gaussianReal_of_var_ne_zero _ hv, integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul'
    (measurable_gaussianPDF _ _) (ae_of_all _ fun _ => gaussianPDF_lt_top)] at hg
  simpa using hg

private theorem integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_id (μ : ℝ) {v : ℝ≥0} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    Integrable (fun x => gaussianPDFReal μ v x * x) :=
  integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul hv ((memLp_id_gaussianReal 1).integrable le_rfl)

private theorem integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sq (μ : ℝ) {v : ℝ≥0} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    Integrable (fun x => gaussianPDFReal μ v x * x ^ 2) :=
  integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul hv (memLp_id_gaussianReal 2).integrable_sq

private theorem integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sub (μ : ℝ) {v : ℝ≥0} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    Integrable (fun x => gaussianPDFReal μ v x * (x - μ)) := by
  refine ((integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_id μ hv).sub
    ((integrable_gaussianPDFReal μ v).mul_const μ)).congr (ae_of_all _ fun x => ?_)
  simp only [Pi.sub_apply]
  ring

/-- Above any threshold `a`, the first moment about the mean is `v` times the density at `a`. -/
private theorem integral_Ioi_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sub (μ : ℝ) {v : ℝ≥0} (hv : v ≠ 0) (a : ℝ) :
    ∫ x in Ioi a, gaussianPDFReal μ v x * (x - μ) = v * gaussianPDFReal μ v a := by
  have hv' : (v : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hv
  have hderiv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt (fun x => -(v * gaussianPDFReal μ v x))
      (gaussianPDFReal μ v x * (x - μ)) x := by
    intro x
    convert ((hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal μ hv x).const_mul (v : ℝ)).neg using 1
    field_simp
  have hint := integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sub μ hv
  have hlim : Tendsto (fun x => -(v * gaussianPDFReal μ v x)) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
    tendsto_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrableOn_Ioi (a := a) (fun x _ => hderiv x)
      hint.integrableOn ((integrable_gaussianPDFReal μ v).const_mul _).neg.integrableOn
  rw [integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto' (fun x _ => hderiv x) hint.integrableOn hlim]
  ring

/-- Above zero, the second moment is `v` times the mass plus `μ` times the first moment. -/
private theorem integral_Ioi_zero_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sq (μ : ℝ) {v : ℝ≥0} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    ∫ x in Ioi 0, gaussianPDFReal μ v x * x ^ 2 =
      v * (∫ x in Ioi 0, gaussianPDFReal μ v x) +
        μ * ∫ x in Ioi 0, gaussianPDFReal μ v x * x := by
  have hv' : (v : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hv
  set p := gaussianPDFReal μ v
  have hderiv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt (fun x => -(v * (p x * x)))
      (p x * x ^ 2 - (v * p x + μ * (p x * x))) x := by
    intro x
    convert (((hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal μ hv x).fun_mul (hasDerivAt_id' x)).const_mul
      (v : ℝ)).neg using 1
    field_simp
    ring
  have hmass : Integrable (fun x => (v : ℝ) * p x) :=
    (integrable_gaussianPDFReal μ v).const_mul _
  have hfirst : Integrable (fun x => μ * (p x * x)) :=
    (integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_id μ hv).const_mul _
  have hlower : Integrable (fun x => (v : ℝ) * p x + μ * (p x * x)) := hmass.add hfirst
  have hint : Integrable (fun x => p x * x ^ 2 - (v * p x + μ * (p x * x))) :=
    (integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sq μ hv).sub hlower
  have hlim : Tendsto (fun x => -(v * (p x * x))) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
    tendsto_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrableOn_Ioi (a := 0) (fun x _ => hderiv x)
      hint.integrableOn ((integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_id μ hv).const_mul _).neg.integrableOn
  have h := integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto' (a := 0) (fun x _ => hderiv x)
    hint.integrableOn hlim
  rw [integral_sub (integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sq μ hv).integrableOn hlower.integrableOn,
    integral_add hmass.integrableOn hfirst.integrableOn, integral_const_mul,
    integral_const_mul] at h
  simp only [mul_zero, neg_zero, sub_zero] at h
  linarith

/-- The mass of `gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2)` above zero is `Φ(μ / σ)`. -/
private theorem integral_Ioi_zero_gaussianPDFReal (μ : ℝ) {σ : ℝ≥0} (hσ : 0 < σ) :
    ∫ x in Ioi 0, gaussianPDFReal μ (σ ^ 2) x = cdf (gaussianReal 0 1) (μ / σ) := by
  have hσ' : (0 : ℝ) < σ := hσ
  have hv : σ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hσ.ne'
  have hstandard :
      ((gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2)).map (μ - ·)).map (· / (σ : ℝ)) = gaussianReal 0 1 := by
    rw [gaussianReal_map_const_sub, gaussianReal_map_div_const, sub_self, zero_div]
    congr 1
    ext
    simp [hσ'.ne']
  have hpreimage : (fun x => (μ - x) / (σ : ℝ)) ⁻¹' Iic (μ / σ) = Ici 0 := by
    ext x
    simp [div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hσ']
  rw [cdf_eq_real, ← hstandard, Measure.map_map (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop),
    map_measureReal_apply (by fun_prop) measurableSet_Iic]
  rw [show ((· / (σ : ℝ)) ∘ (μ - ·)) = fun x => (μ - x) / (σ : ℝ) from rfl, hpreimage,
    measureReal_def, gaussianReal_apply_eq_integral _ hv, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal
      (setIntegral_nonneg measurableSet_Ici fun x _ => gaussianPDFReal_nonneg _ _ _),
    integral_Ici_eq_integral_Ioi]

/-- The density of `gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2)` at zero, times `σ ^ 2`, is `σ φ(μ / σ)`. -/
private theorem var_mul_gaussianPDFReal_zero (μ : ℝ) {σ : ℝ≥0} (hσ : 0 < σ) :
    ((σ ^ 2 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) * gaussianPDFReal μ (σ ^ 2) 0 = σ * gaussianPDFReal 0 1 (μ / σ) := by
  have hσ' : (0 : ℝ) < σ := hσ
  simp only [gaussianPDFReal, NNReal.coe_pow, NNReal.coe_one]
  rw [show 2 * π * (σ : ℝ) ^ 2 = 2 * π * 1 * (σ : ℝ) ^ 2 by ring,
    Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity), Real.sqrt_sq hσ'.le]
  have hexponent : -(0 - μ) ^ 2 / (2 * (σ : ℝ) ^ 2) = -(μ / σ - 0) ^ 2 / (2 * 1) := by
    field_simp
    ring
  rw [hexponent]
  field_simp

/-- A positive power of ReLU, weighted by `f`, is the same power of the identity restricted to
`(0, ∞)`. -/
private theorem mul_relu_pow_eq_indicator (f : ℝ → ℝ) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    (fun x => f x * Activation.relu x ^ n) =
      (Ioi 0).indicator (fun x => f x * x ^ n) := by
  funext x
  by_cases hx : 0 < x
  · simp [hx, hx.le]
  · simp [hx, le_of_not_gt hx, hn]

/-- `relu_mean` as an integral against `gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2)`. -/
private theorem integral_gaussianReal_relu (μ : ℝ) {σ : ℝ≥0} (hσ : 0 < σ) :
    ∫ x, Activation.relu x ∂gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2) =
      μ * cdf (gaussianReal 0 1) (μ / σ) + σ * gaussianPDFReal 0 1 (μ / σ) := by
  have hv : σ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hσ.ne'
  have hrelu := mul_relu_pow_eq_indicator (gaussianPDFReal μ (σ ^ 2)) one_ne_zero
  simp only [pow_one] at hrelu
  have hsplit : ∫ x in Ioi 0, gaussianPDFReal μ (σ ^ 2) x * x =
      ∫ x in Ioi 0,
        (μ * gaussianPDFReal μ (σ ^ 2) x + gaussianPDFReal μ (σ ^ 2) x * (x - μ)) := by
    congr 1
    funext x
    ring
  rw [integral_gaussianReal_eq_integral_smul hv]
  simp only [smul_eq_mul]
  rw [hrelu, integral_indicator measurableSet_Ioi, hsplit,
    integral_add ((integrable_gaussianPDFReal μ _).const_mul _).integrableOn
      (integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sub μ hv).integrableOn,
    integral_const_mul, integral_Ioi_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sub μ hv,
    integral_Ioi_zero_gaussianPDFReal μ hσ, var_mul_gaussianPDFReal_zero μ hσ]

/-- `relu_second_moment` as an integral against `gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2)`. -/
private theorem integral_gaussianReal_relu_sq (μ : ℝ) {σ : ℝ≥0} (hσ : 0 < σ) :
    ∫ x, Activation.relu x ^ 2 ∂gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2) =
      (μ ^ 2 + σ ^ 2) * cdf (gaussianReal 0 1) (μ / σ) +
        μ * σ * gaussianPDFReal 0 1 (μ / σ) := by
  have hv : σ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hσ.ne'
  have hmean := integral_gaussianReal_relu μ hσ
  have hrelu := mul_relu_pow_eq_indicator (gaussianPDFReal μ (σ ^ 2)) one_ne_zero
  simp only [pow_one] at hrelu
  rw [integral_gaussianReal_eq_integral_smul hv] at hmean ⊢
  simp only [smul_eq_mul] at hmean ⊢
  rw [hrelu, integral_indicator measurableSet_Ioi] at hmean
  rw [mul_relu_pow_eq_indicator _ two_ne_zero, integral_indicator measurableSet_Ioi,
    integral_Ioi_zero_gaussianPDFReal_mul_sq μ hv, hmean, integral_Ioi_zero_gaussianPDFReal μ hσ]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- Half of a centered Gaussian lies below zero: `Φ(0) = 1 / 2`. -/
private theorem cdf_gaussianReal_zero : cdf (gaussianReal 0 1) 0 = 1 / 2 := by
  have := nullSingletonClass_gaussianReal (μ := 0) (v := 1) one_ne_zero
  have hneg : (gaussianReal 0 1).map (fun x => -x) = gaussianReal 0 1 := by
    rw [gaussianReal_map_neg, neg_zero]
  have hsymm : (gaussianReal 0 1).real (Iic 0) = (gaussianReal 0 1).real (Ioi 0) := by
    calc (gaussianReal 0 1).real (Iic 0)
        = ((gaussianReal 0 1).map (fun x => -x)).real (Iic 0) := by rw [hneg]
      _ = (gaussianReal 0 1).real (Ici 0) := by
        rw [map_measureReal_apply measurable_neg measurableSet_Iic]
        congr 1
        ext x
        simp
      _ = (gaussianReal 0 1).real (Ioi 0) := measureReal_congr Ioi_ae_eq_Ici.symm
  have htotal := probReal_compl_eq_one_sub (μ := gaussianReal 0 1) (measurableSet_Iic (a := 0))
  rw [compl_Iic] at htotal
  rw [cdf_eq_real]
  linarith

/-- ReLU is continuous, so it is a.e. strongly measurable for every measure. -/
private theorem aestronglyMeasurable_relu (ν : Measure ℝ) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable (Activation.relu : ℝ → ℝ) ν := by
  have hrelu : (Activation.relu : ℝ → ℝ) = fun x => max x 0 :=
    funext Activation.relu_eq_max
  rw [hrelu]
  fun_prop

variable {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} {Z : Ω → ℝ}

/-- For a preactivation `Z ~ N(μ, σ²)` with `0 < σ`,
`E[ReLU Z] = μ Φ(μ / σ) + σ φ(μ / σ)`, where `Φ = cdf (gaussianReal 0 1)` and
`φ = gaussianPDFReal 0 1`. -/
theorem relu_mean {μ : ℝ} {σ : ℝ≥0} (hσ : 0 < σ) (hZ : HasLaw Z (gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2)) P) :
    ∫ ω, Activation.relu (Z ω) ∂P =
      μ * cdf (gaussianReal 0 1) (μ / σ) + σ * gaussianPDFReal 0 1 (μ / σ) := by
  rw [← integral_gaussianReal_relu μ hσ]
  exact hZ.integral_comp (aestronglyMeasurable_relu _)

/-- For a preactivation `Z ~ N(μ, σ²)` with `0 < σ`,
`E[(ReLU Z)²] = (μ² + σ²) Φ(μ / σ) + μ σ φ(μ / σ)`. -/
theorem relu_second_moment {μ : ℝ} {σ : ℝ≥0} (hσ : 0 < σ)
    (hZ : HasLaw Z (gaussianReal μ (σ ^ 2)) P) :
    ∫ ω, Activation.relu (Z ω) ^ 2 ∂P =
      (μ ^ 2 + σ ^ 2) * cdf (gaussianReal 0 1) (μ / σ) +
        μ * σ * gaussianPDFReal 0 1 (μ / σ) := by
  rw [← integral_gaussianReal_relu_sq μ hσ]
  exact hZ.integral_comp ((aestronglyMeasurable_relu _).pow 2)

/-- A centered Gaussian preactivation `Z ~ N(0, σ²)` has `E[ReLU Z] = σ / √(2π)`. -/
theorem relu_mean_centered {σ : ℝ≥0} (hσ : 0 < σ) (hZ : HasLaw Z (gaussianReal 0 (σ ^ 2)) P) :
    ∫ ω, Activation.relu (Z ω) ∂P = σ / √(2 * π) := by
  rw [relu_mean hσ hZ]
  simp [gaussianPDFReal, div_eq_mul_inv]

/-- A centered Gaussian preactivation `Z ~ N(0, σ²)` has `E[(ReLU Z)²] = σ² / 2`. -/
theorem relu_second_moment_centered {σ : ℝ≥0} (hσ : 0 < σ)
    (hZ : HasLaw Z (gaussianReal 0 (σ ^ 2)) P) :
    ∫ ω, Activation.relu (Z ω) ^ 2 ∂P = σ ^ 2 / 2 := by
  rw [relu_second_moment hσ hZ, zero_div, cdf_gaussianReal_zero]
  ring

module

public import HeuristicEstimation.Basic

/-!
# Moments through affine tensor maps

Means and cross-covariances pass through affine tensor maps by mathlib's integration and
covariance rules. Two maps may read the same random input, whose coordinates may depend on each
other in any way. Mean and variance alone don't fix a fourth moment
(`moments_do_not_determine_fourth`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation.Moments

open TorchLean MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

/-- An affine layer commutes with expectation whenever the input coordinates are integrable. -/
theorem affine_mean {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {inputs outputs : Nat} (weights : Tensor ℝ [outputs, inputs])
    (bias : Tensor ℝ [outputs]) (values : Ω → Tensor ℝ [inputs])
    (h : ∀ j, Integrable (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar j) μ) (i : Fin outputs) :
    (∫ ω, Tensor.getScalar (Tensor.matvec weights (values ω) + bias) i ∂μ) =
      Tensor.getScalar (Tensor.matvec weights
        (Tensor.ofFn fun j => ∫ ω, (values ω).getScalar j ∂μ) + bias) i := by
  simp only [Tensor.getScalar_add, Tensor.matvec, Tensor.getScalar_contract_matVec_eq_sum,
    Tensor.getScalar_ofFn]
  have hint (j : Fin inputs) := (h j).const_mul (Tensor.get2 weights i j)
  rw [integral_add (f := fun ω => ∑ j, Tensor.get2 weights i j * (values ω).getScalar j)
    (g := fun _ => bias.getScalar i) (integrable_finsetSum _ fun j _ => hint j)
    (integrable_const _)]
  rw [integral_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun j _ => hint j)]
  simp only [integral_const_mul, integral_const, probReal_univ, one_smul]

/-- The covariance between outputs of two affine maps of one input is `L Σ Rᵀ`, where `Σ` is the
input covariance. Biases drop out, and taking both maps equal gives `W Σ Wᵀ`. -/
theorem affine_covariance {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {inputs leftSize rightSize : Nat}
    (left : Tensor ℝ [leftSize, inputs]) (right : Tensor ℝ [rightSize, inputs])
    (leftBias : Tensor ℝ [leftSize]) (rightBias : Tensor ℝ [rightSize])
    (values : Ω → Tensor ℝ [inputs])
    (h : ∀ k, MemLp (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar k) 2 μ)
    (i : Fin leftSize) (j : Fin rightSize) :
    covariance (fun ω => Tensor.getScalar (Tensor.matvec left (values ω) + leftBias) i)
      (fun ω => Tensor.getScalar (Tensor.matvec right (values ω) + rightBias) j) μ =
        ∑ k : Fin inputs, ∑ l : Fin inputs,
          left[(i, k)] * covariance (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar k)
            (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar l) μ * right[(j, l)] := by
  simp only [Tensor.getScalar_add, Tensor.matvec, Tensor.getScalar_contract_matVec_eq_sum]
  have hleft (k : Fin inputs) := (h k).const_mul (Tensor.get2 left i k)
  have hright (k : Fin inputs) := (h k).const_mul (Tensor.get2 right j k)
  rw [covariance_add_const_left
    ((memLp_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun k _ => hleft k)).integrable (by norm_num))]
  rw [covariance_add_const_right
    ((memLp_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun k _ => hright k)).integrable (by norm_num))]
  rw [covariance_fun_sum_fun_sum hleft hright]
  simp only [covariance_const_mul_left, covariance_const_mul_right]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro k _
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro l _
  change _ = Tensor.get2 left i k * _ * Tensor.get2 right j l
  ring

/-- Two equally weighted four-point distributions share mean `0` and second moment `1`, but
their fourth moments are `1` and `2`. -/
theorem moments_do_not_determine_fourth :
    ∃ a b : Tensor ℝ [4],
      vectorMean a = 0 ∧ vectorMean b = 0 ∧
      vectorMean (Tensor.square a) = 1 ∧ vectorMean (Tensor.square b) = 1 ∧
      vectorMean (Tensor.square (Tensor.square a)) = 1 ∧
      vectorMean (Tensor.square (Tensor.square b)) = 2 := by
  refine ⟨signs, Tensor.ofFn (fun i =>
    if i.val = 0 then -Real.sqrt 2 else if i.val = 3 then Real.sqrt 2 else 0), ?_⟩
  norm_num [vectorMean_eq, Tensor.getScalar_eq_apply,
    Tensor.square, signs, Tensor.ofFn, Fin.sum_univ_succ,
    Tensor.meanDenominator, Shape.size, Real.mul_self_sqrt (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)]

end HeuristicEstimation.Moments

module

public import HeuristicEstimation.Basic
public import Mathlib.Probability.Moments.Variance

/-!
# Correcting an estimate with residual samples

Adding the average of sampled residuals to a surrogate's known mean corrects the surrogate's
bias. What remains is sampling error, the residual variance divided by the sample count, for
which pairwise uncorrelated samples suffice. Each tensor coordinate here is one sample.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation.Sampling

open TorchLean MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

/-- For a nonempty vector, `vectorMean` is the coordinate sum divided by the length. -/
theorem mean_eq_sum {n : Nat} (hn : 0 < n) (values : Tensor ℝ [n]) :
    vectorMean values = (∑ i : Fin n, values.getScalar i) / (n : ℝ) := by
  simp [vectorMean_eq, Tensor.meanDenominator, Shape.size, Nat.ne_of_gt hn]

/-- Expectation of a sample average is the average of the samples' expectations. -/
theorem mean_expectation {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} {n : Nat}
    (hn : 0 < n) (values : Ω → Tensor ℝ [n])
    (h : ∀ i, Integrable (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar i) μ) :
    (∫ ω, vectorMean (values ω) ∂μ) =
      (∑ i : Fin n, ∫ ω, (values ω).getScalar i ∂μ) / (n : ℝ) := by
  simp_rw [mean_eq_sum hn]
  rw [integral_div]
  congr 1
  exact integral_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => h i)

/-- For pairwise uncorrelated samples, the variance of their average is `∑ Var(Xᵢ) / n ^ 2`.
Samples may have different variances. -/
theorem mean_variance {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : Nat} (hn : 0 < n) (values : Ω → Tensor ℝ [n])
    (h : ∀ i, MemLp (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar i) 2 μ)
    (hcov : ∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j →
      covariance (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar i)
        (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar j) μ = 0) :
    variance (fun ω => vectorMean (values ω)) μ =
      (∑ i : Fin n, variance (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar i) μ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  classical
  simp_rw [mean_eq_sum hn]
  simp_rw [div_eq_mul_inv]
  rw [variance_mul_const, variance_fun_sum h]
  simp only [inv_pow]
  congr 1
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
  · exact covariance_self (h i).aemeasurable
  · intro j _ hji
    exact hcov i j hji.symm
  · simp

/-- If every sample has mean `mean`, so does their average. The sample count must be positive,
since an empty tensor has no average. -/
theorem mean_unbiased {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} {n : Nat}
    (hn : 0 < n) (values : Ω → Tensor ℝ [n]) (mean : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ i, Integrable (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar i) μ)
    (hm : ∀ i, (∫ ω, (values ω).getScalar i ∂μ) = mean) :
    (∫ ω, vectorMean (values ω) ∂μ) = mean := by
  rw [mean_expectation hn values h]
  simp only [hm, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
  exact mul_div_cancel_left₀ mean (Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.ne_of_gt hn))

/-- Averaging finitely many samples keeps a finite second moment. -/
theorem mean_memLp {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} {n : Nat}
    (hn : 0 < n) (values : Ω → Tensor ℝ [n])
    (h : ∀ i, MemLp (fun ω => (values ω).getScalar i) 2 μ) :
    MemLp (fun ω => vectorMean (values ω)) 2 μ := by
  simp_rw [mean_eq_sum hn, div_eq_mul_inv]
  exact (memLp_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => h i)).mul_const _

/-- Mean squared error about `target` is variance plus squared bias, for any value with a finite
second moment. -/
theorem mse_eq_variance_add_bias {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {value : Ω → ℝ} (h : MemLp value 2 μ) (target : ℝ) :
    (∫ ω, (value ω - target) ^ 2 ∂μ) =
      variance value μ + ((∫ ω, value ω ∂μ) - target) ^ 2 := by
  have hexpand : (fun ω => (value ω - target) ^ 2) =
      (fun ω => value ω ^ 2 + (-2 * target) * value ω + target ^ 2) := by
    funext ω
    ring
  have hint := h.integrable (by norm_num)
  rw [hexpand,
    integral_add (f := fun ω => value ω ^ 2 + (-2 * target) * value ω)
      (g := fun _ => target ^ 2)
      (h.integrable_sq.add (hint.const_mul (-2 * target))) (integrable_const _),
    integral_add (f := fun ω => value ω ^ 2) (g := fun ω => (-2 * target) * value ω)
      h.integrable_sq (hint.const_mul (-2 * target)),
    integral_const_mul, integral_const, variance_eq_sub h]
  simp only [probReal_univ, one_smul, Pi.pow_apply]
  ring

/-- Mean squared error of `knownMean + average(residuals)` as an estimate of
`surrogateMean + residualMean`: the residual variance over `n`, plus the squared error of
`knownMean`. With `surrogateMean = E[S]` and `residualMean = E[T - S]`, that target is `E[T]` by
`residual_correction`. Samples need only be pairwise uncorrelated. -/
theorem residual_mse {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : Nat} (hn : 0 < n)
    (residuals : Ω → Tensor ℝ [n]) (residualMean residualVariance : ℝ)
    (knownMean surrogateMean : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ i, MemLp (fun ω => (residuals ω).getScalar i) 2 μ)
    (hm : ∀ i, (∫ ω, (residuals ω).getScalar i ∂μ) = residualMean)
    (hv : ∀ i, variance (fun ω => (residuals ω).getScalar i) μ = residualVariance)
    (hcov : ∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j →
      covariance (fun ω => (residuals ω).getScalar i)
        (fun ω => (residuals ω).getScalar j) μ = 0) :
    (∫ ω, (knownMean + vectorMean (residuals ω) -
      (surrogateMean + residualMean)) ^ 2 ∂μ) =
        residualVariance / (n : ℝ) + (knownMean - surrogateMean) ^ 2 := by
  have havg := mean_memLp hn residuals h
  have havgMean := mean_unbiased hn residuals residualMean
    (fun i => (h i).integrable (by norm_num)) hm
  have havgVariance : variance (fun ω => vectorMean (residuals ω)) μ =
      residualVariance / (n : ℝ) := by
    rw [mean_variance hn residuals h hcov]
    simp only [hv, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
    field_simp
  have hexpand : (fun ω => (knownMean + vectorMean (residuals ω) -
      (surrogateMean + residualMean)) ^ 2) =
      (fun ω => (vectorMean (residuals ω) -
        (surrogateMean + residualMean - knownMean)) ^ 2) := by
    funext ω
    ring
  rw [hexpand, mse_eq_variance_add_bias havg, havgMean, havgVariance]
  ring

end HeuristicEstimation.Sampling

module

public import HeuristicEstimation.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Ring.Finset

/-!
# Downstream-aware finite sketches

Each row of `tails` is a later linear observation of the intermediate vector, and `weights`
gives each row's context weight. Their weighted Gram matrix is computed once and reused for every
residual. `check` tests absolute row sums in exact rationals. Its soundness theorems turn one
passing check into a quadratic-error bound for all residuals at once.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace HeuristicEstimation.Sketch

open TorchLean
open scoped BigOperators

/-- Weighted second-moment matrix of the downstream observation vectors. -/
def gram {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommSemiring α] {contexts d : Nat}
    (weights : Tensor α [contexts]) (tails : Tensor α [contexts, d]) : Tensor α [d, d] :=
  Tensor.matrix fun i j => ∑ c : Fin contexts,
    weights.getScalar c * tails[(c, i)] * tails[(c, j)]

/-- Weighted squared error of a residual, measured through the downstream observations. -/
def error {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommSemiring α] {contexts d : Nat}
    (weights : Tensor α [contexts]) (tails : Tensor α [contexts, d])
    (residual : Tensor α [d]) : α :=
  ∑ c : Fin contexts, weights.getScalar c *
    (∑ i : Fin d, tails[(c, i)] * residual.getScalar i) ^ 2

/-- Quadratic form `rᵀ M r` of a square tensor matrix. -/
def quadratic {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommSemiring α] {d : Nat}
    (matrix : Tensor α [d, d]) (residual : Tensor α [d]) : α :=
  ∑ i : Fin d, ∑ j : Fin d,
    matrix[(i, j)] * residual.getScalar i * residual.getScalar j

/-- Entry `(i, j)` of `gram` is the weighted sum of `tails[(c, i)] * tails[(c, j)]`. -/
theorem gram_entry {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommSemiring α] {contexts d : Nat}
    (weights : Tensor α [contexts]) (tails : Tensor α [contexts, d]) (i j : Fin d) :
    (gram weights tails)[(i, j)] = ∑ c : Fin contexts,
      weights.getScalar c * tails[(c, i)] * tails[(c, j)] := by
  exact matrix_entry _ i j

/-- Downstream error equals the Gram matrix's quadratic form at the residual. -/
theorem error_eq_quadratic {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommSemiring α] {contexts d : Nat}
    (weights : Tensor α [contexts]) (tails : Tensor α [contexts, d])
    (residual : Tensor α [d]) :
    error weights tails residual = quadratic (gram weights tails) residual := by
  classical
  simp only [error, quadratic, gram_entry, pow_two, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro c _
  ring

/-- Gram matrices are symmetric, whatever the signs of the weights. -/
theorem gram_symmetric {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommSemiring α] {contexts d : Nat}
    (weights : Tensor α [contexts]) (tails : Tensor α [contexts, d]) (i j : Fin d) :
    (gram weights tails)[(i, j)] = (gram weights tails)[(j, i)] := by
  simp only [gram_entry]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro c _
  ring

/-- Nonnegative weights make the Gram quadratic form nonnegative for every residual. -/
theorem gram_nonneg {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommRing α] [LinearOrder α]
    [IsStrictOrderedRing α] {contexts d : Nat}
    (weights : Tensor α [contexts]) (tails : Tensor α [contexts, d])
    (hw : ∀ c, 0 ≤ weights.getScalar c) (residual : Tensor α [d]) :
    0 ≤ quadratic (gram weights tails) residual := by
  rw [← error_eq_quadratic]
  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun c _ => mul_nonneg (hw c) (sq_nonneg _)

/-- Squared Euclidean norm of a vector. -/
def energy {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommSemiring α] {d : Nat}
    (residual : Tensor α [d]) : α :=
  ∑ i : Fin d, residual.getScalar i ^ 2

/-- What a coordinate sketch leaves out, `g - g̃`. Retained coordinates (`true`) become zero
and discarded coordinates keep their values. -/
def residual {α : Type} [Storage α] [Zero α] {d : Nat}
    (keep : Tensor Bool [d]) (values : Tensor α [d]) : Tensor α [d] :=
  Tensor.ofFn fun i => if keep.getScalar i then 0 else values.getScalar i

/-- Zero the rows and columns of retained coordinates, keeping the block on discarded ones.
Its quadratic form measures what a coordinate sketch leaves out (`quadratic_restrict`). -/
def restrict {α : Type} [Storage α] [Zero α] {d : Nat}
    (keep : Tensor Bool [d]) (matrix : Tensor α [d, d]) : Tensor α [d, d] :=
  Tensor.matrix fun i j =>
    if keep.getScalar i || keep.getScalar j then 0 else matrix[(i, j)]

/-- Zeroing retained coordinates in the matrix is equivalent to zeroing them in the vector. -/
theorem quadratic_restrict {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommSemiring α] {d : Nat}
    (keep : Tensor Bool [d]) (matrix : Tensor α [d, d]) (values : Tensor α [d]) :
    quadratic (restrict keep matrix) values = quadratic matrix (residual keep values) := by
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  simp only [restrict, matrix_entry, residual, Tensor.getScalar_ofFn]
  cases keep.getScalar i <;> cases keep.getScalar j <;> simp

/-- Retaining more coordinates never increases residual energy. That controls the certified
budget, but actual downstream error can still grow, because its terms can cancel. -/
theorem residual_energy_mono {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommRing α] [LinearOrder α]
    [IsStrictOrderedRing α] {d : Nat} (coarse fine : Tensor Bool [d])
    (hkeep : ∀ i, coarse.getScalar i = true → fine.getScalar i = true)
    (values : Tensor α [d]) : energy (residual fine values) ≤ energy (residual coarse values) := by
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro i _
  simp only [residual, Tensor.getScalar_ofFn]
  cases hc : coarse.getScalar i
  · cases fine.getScalar i <;> simp [sq_nonneg]
  · simp [hkeep i hc]

/-- If a symmetric matrix has absolute row sums at most `bound`, its quadratic form is at most
`bound * energy` at every residual. No eigensolver is trusted, at the price of a possibly loose
bound. -/
theorem quadratic_le {α : Type} [Storage α] [CommRing α] [LinearOrder α]
    [IsStrictOrderedRing α] {d : Nat} (matrix : Tensor α [d, d]) (bound : α)
    (hsym : ∀ i j : Fin d, matrix[(i, j)] = matrix[(j, i)])
    (hrow : ∀ i : Fin d, ∑ j : Fin d, |matrix[(i, j)]| ≤ bound)
    (residual : Tensor α [d]) :
    quadratic matrix residual ≤ bound * energy residual := by
  classical
  have hentry (i j : Fin d) :
      2 * (matrix[(i, j)] * residual.getScalar i * residual.getScalar j) ≤
        |matrix[(i, j)]| * residual.getScalar i ^ 2 +
          |matrix[(i, j)]| * residual.getScalar j ^ 2 := by
    have hab := le_abs_self (matrix[(i, j)] * residual.getScalar i * residual.getScalar j)
    rw [abs_mul, abs_mul] at hab
    have hsq := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
      (two_mul_le_add_sq |residual.getScalar i| |residual.getScalar j|)
      (abs_nonneg matrix[(i, j)])
    simp only [sq_abs] at hsq
    nlinarith
  have hswap :
      (∑ i : Fin d, ∑ j : Fin d, |matrix[(i, j)]| * residual.getScalar j ^ 2) =
        ∑ i : Fin d, (∑ j : Fin d, |matrix[(i, j)]|) * residual.getScalar i ^ 2 := by
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro j _
    rw [hsym j i]
  have hsum : (∑ i : Fin d, (∑ j : Fin d, |matrix[(i, j)]|) *
      residual.getScalar i ^ 2) ≤ bound * energy residual := by
    rw [energy, Finset.mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hrow i) (sq_nonneg _)
  have htotal : 2 * quadratic matrix residual ≤
      2 * (∑ i : Fin d, (∑ j : Fin d, |matrix[(i, j)]|) *
        residual.getScalar i ^ 2) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin d, ∑ j : Fin d,
          (|matrix[(i, j)]| * residual.getScalar i ^ 2 +
            |matrix[(i, j)]| * residual.getScalar j ^ 2) := by
        simp only [quadratic, Finset.mul_sum]
        exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => hentry i j
      _ = _ := by
        simp_rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
        rw [hswap]
        simp only [← Finset.sum_mul, two_mul]
  linarith

/-- Decide in exact rationals whether every absolute row sum is at most `bound`. Off-diagonal
entries count, and a negative bound fails unless the matrix is empty. -/
def check {d : Nat} (matrix : Tensor Rat [d, d]) (bound : Rat) : Bool :=
  decide (∀ i : Fin d, ∑ j : Fin d, |matrix[(i, j)]| ≤ bound)

/-- `check` passes if and only if every absolute row sum is at most `bound`. -/
theorem check_iff {d : Nat} (matrix : Tensor Rat [d, d]) (bound : Rat) :
    check matrix bound = true ↔ ∀ i : Fin d, ∑ j : Fin d, |matrix[(i, j)]| ≤ bound := by
  simp [check]

/-- For a symmetric matrix, a passing check bounds the quadratic form at every rational
residual. Symmetry is necessary: `[[1, 0], [1, 0]]` passes with bound `1`, yet its form at
`(1, 1/2)` is `3/2`, above `5/4`. -/
theorem check_sound {d : Nat} (matrix : Tensor Rat [d, d]) (bound : Rat)
    (hsym : ∀ i j : Fin d, matrix[(i, j)] = matrix[(j, i)])
    (hcheck : check matrix bound = true) (residual : Tensor Rat [d]) :
    quadratic matrix residual ≤ bound * energy residual :=
  quadratic_le matrix bound hsym ((check_iff matrix bound).mp hcheck) residual

/-- For a symmetric rational matrix, a passing check also bounds its real interpretation at every
real residual, rational or not. -/
theorem check_sound_real {d : Nat} (matrix : Tensor Rat [d, d]) (bound : Rat)
    (hsym : ∀ i j : Fin d, matrix[(i, j)] = matrix[(j, i)])
    (hcheck : check matrix bound = true) (residual : Tensor ℝ [d]) :
    quadratic (Tensor.matrix fun i j => ((matrix[(i, j)] : Rat) : ℝ)) residual ≤
      (bound : ℝ) * energy residual := by
  apply quadratic_le
  · intro i j
    simp only [matrix_entry, hsym i j]
  · intro i
    simp only [matrix_entry]
    exact_mod_cast ((check_iff matrix bound).mp hcheck i)

/-- A passing check on the Gram matrix bounds downstream error at every residual. Weights need
not sum to one. When they do, `error` is a mean squared error. -/
theorem error_le_of_check {contexts d : Nat} (weights : Tensor Rat [contexts])
    (tails : Tensor Rat [contexts, d]) (bound : Rat)
    (hcheck : check (gram weights tails) bound = true) (residual : Tensor Rat [d]) :
    error weights tails residual ≤ bound * energy residual := by
  rw [error_eq_quadratic]
  exact check_sound _ bound (gram_symmetric weights tails) hcheck residual

/-- A passing check on the restricted Gram matrix bounds a coordinate sketch's downstream error
at every input. With bound `0` the error is at most zero for all inputs, hence zero when the
weights are nonnegative. -/
theorem masked_error_le_of_check {contexts d : Nat} (weights : Tensor Rat [contexts])
    (tails : Tensor Rat [contexts, d]) (keep : Tensor Bool [d]) (bound : Rat)
    (hcheck : check (restrict keep (gram weights tails)) bound = true)
    (values : Tensor Rat [d]) :
    error weights tails (residual keep values) ≤ bound * energy (residual keep values) := by
  have hid : residual keep (residual keep values) = residual keep values := by
    apply Tensor.ext_vector
    intro i
    simp only [residual, Tensor.getScalar_ofFn]
    cases keep.getScalar i <;> simp
  rw [error_eq_quadratic, ← hid, ← quadratic_restrict, hid]
  apply check_sound _ bound _ hcheck
  intro i j
  simp only [restrict, matrix_entry]
  rw [Bool.or_comm, gram_symmetric weights tails i j]

end HeuristicEstimation.Sketch

module

public import ProgramEquilibrium.Modal

/-!
# Modal agents and the outcome table

A `Universe` is a population of agents in the style of Barasz et al. (2014). Each agent has a
`schema`: a modalized formula whose atoms are `Target.me` ("my opponent cooperates with me") and
`Target.agent c` ("my opponent cooperates with `c`"). The same schema is used against every
opponent, so an agent cannot look at who it is playing, only at what is provable about how the
opponent plays. Barasz et al. also order agents by rank, so that an agent only mentions
simpler ones; the computation here does not need that.

`play n a b` is whether `a` cooperates with `b` at world `n`. It is computed world by world, which
works because a modalized formula at world `n` only reads worlds below `n`. `play_eq` says the
table satisfies every agent's defining equation at every world, `play_unique` says it is the only
valuation that does, and `play_stabilizes` says every matchup settles from some world on, so that
`cooperates_or_defects` gives each matchup one eventual outcome.

For agents given by arithmetic formulas whose defining equations Peano arithmetic proves, ordered
by rank, and assuming arithmetic is sound, that eventual value is what an agent does in the
standard model. Getting there takes the closed modal representatives of Barasz et al. (Theorem
4.7, from the modal fixed point theorem, Theorems 4.2 and 4.3, after Lindström, and the
arithmetic soundness of GL, Theorem 4.1), the soundness of the chain for GL together with
`play_unique`, and the arithmetic truth of the resulting letterless formulas. Only the chain part
is proved here.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ProgramEquilibrium

open Form

/-- What an agent's formula can mention: whether its opponent cooperates with the agent itself,
or with the fixed agent `c`. -/
inductive Target (Agent : Type) where
  | me
  | agent (c : Agent)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- A population of modal agents. -/
structure Universe where
  /-- The agents. -/
  Agent : Type
  /-- Each agent's formula, the same against every opponent. -/
  schema : Agent → Form (Target Agent)
  /-- Every atom in an agent's schema occurs under a box. -/
  modalized : ∀ a, (schema a).modalized = true

namespace Universe

variable (U : Universe)

/-- `a`'s formula against `b`, over the atoms "`x` cooperates with `y`". -/
def rule (a b : U.Agent) : Form (U.Agent × U.Agent) :=
  (U.schema a).map fun
    | .me => (b, a)
    | .agent c => (b, c)

theorem rule_modalized (a b : U.Agent) : (U.rule a b).modalized = true := by
  simp [rule, U.modalized a]

/-- `play n a b`: whether `a` cooperates with `b` at world `n`. -/
def play (n : ℕ) (a b : U.Agent) : Bool :=
  eval (fun m p => if _ : m < n then play m p.1 p.2 else false) n (U.rule a b)
termination_by n

/-- The table satisfies every agent's defining equation at every world. -/
theorem play_eq (n : ℕ) (a b : U.Agent) :
    U.play n a b = eval (fun m p => U.play m p.1 p.2) n (U.rule a b) := by
  rw [play]
  exact eval_congr_of_modalized (fun m hm p => by simp [hm]) (U.rule_modalized a b)

/-- Any valuation that satisfies the agents' equations at every world is the table. -/
theorem play_unique (V : ℕ → U.Agent → U.Agent → Bool)
    (hV : ∀ n a b, V n a b = eval (fun m p => V m p.1 p.2) n (U.rule a b)) :
    ∀ n a b, V n a b = U.play n a b := by
  intro n
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ n ih =>
    intro a b
    rw [hV, U.play_eq]
    exact eval_congr_of_modalized (fun m hm p => ih m hm p.1 p.2) (U.rule_modalized a b)

/-- Every matchup settles: from some world on, its entry in the table no longer changes. -/
theorem play_stabilizes (a b : U.Agent) : ∃ K, ∀ n ≥ K, U.play n a b = U.play K a b := by
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := stabilizes_of_modalized (fun m p => U.play m p.1 p.2) (U.rule_modalized a b)
  exact ⟨K, fun n hn => by rw [U.play_eq, U.play_eq K, hK n hn]⟩

/-- From some world on, `a` cooperates with `b`. -/
def Cooperates (a b : U.Agent) : Prop :=
  ∃ K, ∀ n ≥ K, U.play n a b = true

/-- From some world on, `a` defects against `b`. -/
def Defects (a b : U.Agent) : Prop :=
  ∃ K, ∀ n ≥ K, U.play n a b = false

/-- Every matchup has an eventual outcome. -/
theorem cooperates_or_defects (a b : U.Agent) : U.Cooperates a b ∨ U.Defects a b := by
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := U.play_stabilizes a b
  cases h : U.play K a b
  · exact Or.inr ⟨K, fun n hn => (hK n hn).trans h⟩
  · exact Or.inl ⟨K, fun n hn => (hK n hn).trans h⟩

/-- Cooperation and defection cannot both be eventual outcomes. -/
theorem not_cooperates_and_defects (a b : U.Agent) : ¬ (U.Cooperates a b ∧ U.Defects a b) := by
  rintro ⟨⟨K, hK⟩, ⟨L, hL⟩⟩
  have := (hK (max K L) (by omega)).symm.trans (hL (max K L) (by omega))
  simp at this

section FairBot

variable {U} {f : U.Agent}

/-- FairBot's formula, `□ [opponent cooperates with me]`, against `b`. -/
theorem fair_rule (hf : U.schema f = box (atom .me)) (b : U.Agent) :
    U.rule f b = box (atom (b, f)) := by
  simp [rule, hf, map]

/-- FairBot defects at every world above one where `b` defects against it. -/
theorem fair_defects_above (hf : U.schema f = box (atom .me)) {b : U.Agent} {m : ℕ}
    (hm : U.play m b f = false) : ∀ n > m, U.play n f b = false := by
  intro n hn
  rw [U.play_eq, fair_rule hf]
  apply Bool.eq_false_iff.2
  intro h
  have := (eval_box _ n _).1 h m hn
  simp [eval, hm] at this

/-- FairBot cannot be exploited: if `b` eventually defects against it, it eventually defects
against `b`. -/
theorem fair_unexploitable (hf : U.schema f = box (atom .me)) {b : U.Agent}
    (h : U.Defects b f) : U.Defects f b := by
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := h
  exact ⟨K + 1, fun n hn => fair_defects_above hf (hK K (Nat.le_refl K)) n (by omega)⟩

/-- FairBot eventually cooperates with `b` exactly when `b` cooperates with FairBot at every
world. -/
theorem fair_cooperates_iff (hf : U.schema f = box (atom .me)) (b : U.Agent) :
    U.Cooperates f b ↔ ∀ m, U.play m b f = true := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨K, hK⟩ m
    have h := hK (max K (m + 1)) (by omega)
    rw [U.play_eq, fair_rule hf] at h
    exact (eval_box _ _ _).1 h m (by omega)
  · intro h
    refine ⟨0, fun n _ => ?_⟩
    rw [U.play_eq, fair_rule hf]
    exact (eval_box _ _ _).2 fun m _ => h m

end FairBot

end Universe

end ProgramEquilibrium

module

public import ProgramEquilibrium.Agents

/-!
# CooperateBot, DefectBot, FairBot and PrudentBot

The agents of Barasz et al. (2014), as schemas over "my opponent cooperates with …":

* CooperateBot always cooperates, and DefectBot always defects.
* FairBot cooperates when it can prove that its opponent cooperates with it: `□ me`.
* `twin` is FairBot written differently, `□ (me ∨ ⊥)`. The two have different formulas, so an
  agent that only cooperates with exact copies of itself would not cooperate with both.
* PrudentBot also wants a proof, assuming arithmetic is consistent, that its opponent defects
  against DefectBot: `□ me ∧ □ (¬□⊥ → ¬ [opponent cooperates with DefectBot])`.
* `cupod` cooperates unless it can prove that its opponent defects against it: `¬□¬ me`. It is
  the modal idealization of Critch, Dennis and Russell's CUPOD(k), with ordinary provability in
  place of a bounded proof search; the same idealization of their DUPOC(k) is FairBot.

The theorems below prove the article's matchups at every world of the chain, and `outcomes`
collects their eventual values. Every box holds at world `0`, so FairBot and PrudentBot cooperate
with DefectBot there, and PrudentBot cooperates with CooperateBot at worlds `0` and `1`. In the
limit FairBot, its twin and PrudentBot cooperate with each other, DefectBot exploits none of
them, and PrudentBot, unlike FairBot, defects against CooperateBot.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ProgramEquilibrium

open Form

/-- The agents of the article. -/
inductive Bot where
  | cooperate
  | defect
  | fair
  | twin
  | prudent
  | cupod
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

namespace Bot

/-- Each agent's formula, the same against every opponent. -/
def schema : Bot → Form (Target Bot)
  | cooperate => top
  | defect => bot
  | fair => box (atom .me)
  | twin => box (or (atom .me) bot)
  | prudent => and (box (atom .me)) (box (imp (not (box bot)) (not (atom (.agent defect)))))
  | cupod => not (box (not (atom .me)))

end Bot

/-- The population of the article's agents. -/
abbrev bots : Universe where
  Agent := Bot
  schema := Bot.schema
  modalized a := by cases a <;> rfl

namespace Bot

theorem cooperate_play (n : ℕ) (b : Bot) : bots.play n cooperate b = true := by
  rw [Universe.play_eq]
  rfl

theorem defect_play (n : ℕ) (b : Bot) : bots.play n defect b = false := by
  rw [Universe.play_eq]
  rfl

theorem fair_play (n : ℕ) (b : Bot) :
    bots.play n fair b = true ↔ ∀ m < n, bots.play m b fair = true := by
  rw [Universe.play_eq]
  exact eval_box (fun m p => bots.play m p.1 p.2) n (atom (b, fair))

theorem twin_play (n : ℕ) (b : Bot) :
    bots.play n twin b = true ↔ ∀ m < n, bots.play m b twin = true := by
  rw [Universe.play_eq]
  change eval (fun m p => bots.play m p.1 p.2) n (box (or (atom (b, twin)) bot)) = true ↔ _
  rw [eval_box]
  exact forall₂_congr fun m _ => by simp [eval]

theorem prudent_play (n : ℕ) (b : Bot) :
    bots.play n prudent b = true ↔
      (∀ m < n, bots.play m b prudent = true) ∧ ∀ m < n, m ≠ 0 → bots.play m b defect = false := by
  rw [Universe.play_eq]
  change (eval (fun m p => bots.play m p.1 p.2) n (box (atom (b, prudent))) &&
      eval (fun m p => bots.play m p.1 p.2) n
        (box (imp (not (box bot)) (not (atom (b, defect)))))) = true ↔ _
  rw [Bool.and_eq_true, eval_box, eval_box]
  refine and_congr Iff.rfl (forall₂_congr fun m _ => ?_)
  rw [eval_imp, eval_not, eval_not, Bool.eq_false_iff, ne_eq, eval_box_bot]
  rfl

/-- FairBot cooperates with FairBot at every world: Löb's theorem in the table. -/
theorem fair_fair (n : ℕ) : bots.play n fair fair = true := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ n ih => exact (fair_play n fair).2 ih

/-- FairBot and its twin cooperate with each other at every world, though their formulas
differ. -/
theorem fair_twin (n : ℕ) : bots.play n fair twin = true ∧ bots.play n twin fair = true := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ n ih =>
    exact ⟨(fair_play n twin).2 fun m hm => (ih m hm).2,
      (twin_play n fair).2 fun m hm => (ih m hm).1⟩

/-- FairBot cooperates with DefectBot only at world `0`. -/
theorem fair_defect (n : ℕ) : bots.play n fair defect = true ↔ n = 0 := by
  rw [fair_play]
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hn
    have := h 0 (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn)
    simp [defect_play] at this
  · rintro rfl m hm
    omega

theorem fair_cooperate (n : ℕ) : bots.play n fair cooperate = true :=
  (fair_play n cooperate).2 fun m _ => cooperate_play m fair

/-- PrudentBot cooperates with DefectBot only at world `0`. -/
theorem prudent_defect (n : ℕ) : bots.play n prudent defect = true ↔ n = 0 := by
  rw [prudent_play]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h, -⟩
    by_contra hn
    have := h 0 (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn)
    simp [defect_play] at this
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨fun m hm => by omega, fun m hm => by omega⟩

/-- PrudentBot cooperates with CooperateBot only at worlds `0` and `1`. -/
theorem prudent_cooperate (n : ℕ) : bots.play n prudent cooperate = true ↔ n ≤ 1 := by
  rw [prudent_play]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨-, h⟩
    by_contra hn
    have := h 1 (by omega) Nat.one_ne_zero
    simp [cooperate_play] at this
  · intro hn
    exact ⟨fun m _ => cooperate_play m prudent, fun m hm h0 => by omega⟩

/-- PrudentBot cooperates with PrudentBot at every world. -/
theorem prudent_prudent (n : ℕ) : bots.play n prudent prudent = true := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ n ih =>
    refine (prudent_play n prudent).2 ⟨ih, fun m _ hm => ?_⟩
    exact Bool.eq_false_iff.2 fun h => hm ((prudent_defect m).1 h)

/-- PrudentBot and FairBot cooperate with each other at every world. -/
theorem prudent_fair (n : ℕ) : bots.play n prudent fair = true ∧ bots.play n fair prudent = true := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ n ih =>
    refine ⟨(prudent_play n fair).2 ⟨fun m hm => (ih m hm).2, fun m _ hm => ?_⟩,
      (fair_play n prudent).2 fun m hm => (ih m hm).1⟩
    exact Bool.eq_false_iff.2 fun h => hm ((fair_defect m).1 h)

theorem cupod_play (n : ℕ) (b : Bot) :
    bots.play n cupod b = true ↔ ∃ m < n, bots.play m b cupod = true := by
  rw [Universe.play_eq]
  change eval (fun m p => bots.play m p.1 p.2) n (not (box (not (atom (b, cupod))))) = true ↔ _
  rw [eval_not, Bool.eq_false_iff, ne_eq, eval_box]
  simp only [eval_not, not_forall, Bool.not_eq_false]
  exact exists_congr fun m => ⟨fun ⟨h, e⟩ => ⟨h, e⟩, fun ⟨h, e⟩ => ⟨h, e⟩⟩

/-- CUPOD defects against CUPOD at every world, as CUPOD(k) does for large `k`
(Critch, Dennis and Russell, Theorem 3.4). -/
theorem cupod_cupod (n : ℕ) : bots.play n cupod cupod = false := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ n ih =>
    apply Bool.eq_false_iff.2
    intro h
    obtain ⟨m, hm, hc⟩ := (cupod_play n cupod).1 h
    simp [ih m hm] at hc

/-- Against CUPOD, FairBot cooperates only at world `0`, and CUPOD cooperates from world `1` on.
Critch, Dennis and Russell conjecture the same outcome, (D, C), for DUPOC(k) against CUPOD(k)
(their Open Problem 3). -/
theorem fair_cupod (n : ℕ) :
    (bots.play n fair cupod = true ↔ n = 0) ∧ (bots.play n cupod fair = true ↔ 1 ≤ n) := by
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ n ih =>
    constructor
    · rw [fair_play]
      constructor
      · intro h
        by_contra hn
        have := (ih 0 (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn)).2.1 (h 0 (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn))
        omega
      · rintro rfl m hm
        omega
    · rw [cupod_play]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨m, hm, -⟩
        omega
      · intro hn
        exact ⟨0, by omega, (ih 0 (by omega)).1.2 rfl⟩

/-- The eventual outcome of every matchup the article discusses. -/
theorem outcomes :
    bots.Cooperates fair fair ∧ bots.Cooperates fair twin ∧ bots.Cooperates twin fair ∧
    bots.Cooperates fair cooperate ∧ bots.Defects fair defect ∧
    bots.Cooperates prudent prudent ∧ bots.Cooperates prudent fair ∧
    bots.Cooperates fair prudent ∧ bots.Defects prudent defect ∧
    bots.Defects prudent cooperate ∧ bots.Defects cupod cupod ∧ bots.Defects fair cupod ∧
    bots.Cooperates cupod fair := by
  refine ⟨⟨0, fun n _ => fair_fair n⟩, ⟨0, fun n _ => (fair_twin n).1⟩,
    ⟨0, fun n _ => (fair_twin n).2⟩, ⟨0, fun n _ => fair_cooperate n⟩, ⟨1, fun n hn => ?_⟩,
    ⟨0, fun n _ => prudent_prudent n⟩, ⟨0, fun n _ => (prudent_fair n).1⟩,
    ⟨0, fun n _ => (prudent_fair n).2⟩, ⟨1, fun n hn => ?_⟩, ⟨2, fun n hn => ?_⟩,
    ⟨0, fun n _ => cupod_cupod n⟩, ⟨1, fun n hn => ?_⟩, ⟨1, fun n hn => (fair_cupod n).2.2 hn⟩⟩
  · exact Bool.eq_false_iff.2 fun h => by have := (fair_defect n).1 h; omega
  · exact Bool.eq_false_iff.2 fun h => by have := (prudent_defect n).1 h; omega
  · exact Bool.eq_false_iff.2 fun h => by have := (prudent_cooperate n).1 h; omega
  · exact Bool.eq_false_iff.2 fun h => by have := (fair_cupod n).1.1 h; omega

/-- FairBot cannot be exploited in the eventual outcomes. -/
theorem fair_unexploitable {b : Bot} (h : bots.Defects b fair) : bots.Defects fair b :=
  Universe.fair_unexploitable (U := bots) (f := fair) rfl h
