module

public import Mathlib.Data.List.Find

/-!
# Cooperation with a certificate budget

Unlike the modal-chain evaluator, these agents return an actual move after a finite search.
The budget counts UTF-8 bytes in a cooperation certificate. The two certificate rules cover
constant cooperators and pairs of searchers that can afford each other's reciprocal certificate.
The latter rule is justified by `Certificate.check_sound`, not assumed as a reflection axiom.

This is a restricted certificate calculus, not an arithmetization of Lean or Peano arithmetic.
It does not establish the parametric bounded Löb theorem or solve Open Problem 4 of Critch,
Dennis and Russell, <https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07006>. In particular, a certificate's byte count
is not the length of its expanded Lean proof, and search exhaustion says nothing about proofs
outside these two rules. The program registry is fixed throughout each theorem.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ProgramEquilibrium.Bounded

/-- Registered code. A searcher chooses a byte budget and which certificate rule to try first.
Other total Lean functions may be opponents, even when neither rule can certify them. -/
inductive Program where
  | cooperate
  | defect
  | search (certificateBytes : Nat) (reciprocalFirst : Bool)
  | other (action : String → Bool)

/-- Evidence that the named subject cooperates with the named opponent, in a fixed registry. -/
inductive Certificate where
  | constant (subject opponent : String)
  | reciprocal (subject opponent : String)
  deriving Repr

namespace Certificate

/-- The program whose move is certified. -/
def subject : Certificate → String
  | constant a _ | reciprocal a _ => a

/-- The program it is playing against. -/
def opponent : Certificate → String
  | constant _ b | reciprocal _ b => b

/-- Literal certificate text, with quoted names. Names refer to the supplied registry;
they are not hashes of source code. -/
def encode (p : Certificate) : String :=
  -- Use total string operations so concrete certificate sizes can also be kernel-reduced.
  let quoteName (name : String) :=
    "\"" ++ String.join (name.toList.map fun c => c.quoteCore (inString := true)) ++ "\""
  match p with
  | constant a b => "C(" ++ quoteName a ++ "," ++ quoteName b ++ ")"
  | reciprocal a b => "R(" ++ quoteName a ++ "," ++ quoteName b ++ ")"

/-- The budget counts this text, including names and delimiters. -/
def bytes (p : Certificate) : Nat := p.encode.utf8ByteSize

end Certificate

/-- Check both searchers' budgets without running either searcher. -/
def reciprocalCheck (program : String → Program) (a b : String) : Bool :=
  match program a, program b with
  | .search ka _, .search kb _ =>
    decide ((Certificate.reciprocal b a).bytes ≤ ka ∧
      (Certificate.reciprocal a b).bytes ≤ kb)
  | _, _ => false

/-- The constant rule inspects the subject's code. The reciprocal rule inspects both programs
and their budgets. Neither rule accepts an opaque `Program.other` function. -/
def Certificate.check (program : String → Program) : Certificate → Bool
  | constant a _ => match program a with
    | .cooperate => true
    | _ => false
  | reciprocal a b => reciprocalCheck program a b

/-- Two heuristic orders over the same finite certificate calculus. -/
def candidates (a b : String) (reciprocalFirst : Bool) : List Certificate :=
  if reciprocalFirst then [.reciprocal a b, .constant a b]
  else [.constant a b, .reciprocal a b]

/-- Return the first valid certificate that fits the byte budget. The search terminates after
at most two candidates; it does not enumerate all Lean proofs of the goal. -/
def findCertificate (program : String → Program) (certificateBytes : Nat)
    (reciprocalFirst : Bool) (a b : String) : Option Certificate :=
  (candidates a b reciprocalFirst).find? fun p =>
    decide (p.bytes ≤ certificateBytes) && p.check program

/-- A searcher cooperates exactly when it finds an affordable certificate of its opponent's
cooperation. `true` means cooperation; `false` means defection. -/
def run (program : String → Program) (a b : String) : Bool :=
  match program a with
  | .cooperate => true
  | .defect => false
  | .other action => action b
  | .search budget order => (findCertificate program budget order b a).isSome

private theorem findCertificate_success (program : String → Program) (k : Nat) (order : Bool)
    (a b : String) :
    (findCertificate program k order a b).isSome = true ↔
      ((Certificate.constant a b).bytes ≤ k ∧ (Certificate.constant a b).check program = true) ∨
      ((Certificate.reciprocal a b).bytes ≤ k ∧
        (Certificate.reciprocal a b).check program = true) := by
  cases order <;> simp [findCertificate, candidates, List.find?_isSome, or_comm]

/-- Every accepted certificate describes an actual move of the terminating program.
The reciprocal case unfolds both searches: each contains the affordable certificate whose
validity the checker has already established from the program descriptions. -/
theorem Certificate.check_sound (program : String → Program) (p : Certificate)
    (h : p.check program = true) : run program p.subject p.opponent = true := by
  cases p with
  | constant a b =>
    cases ha : program a <;> simp [Certificate.check, run, Certificate.subject, ha] at h ⊢
  | reciprocal a b =>
    cases ha : program a <;> cases hb : program b <;>
      simp only [Certificate.check, reciprocalCheck, ha, hb, Bool.false_eq_true] at h
    rename_i ka oa kb ob
    have limits : (Certificate.reciprocal b a).bytes ≤ ka ∧
        (Certificate.reciprocal a b).bytes ≤ kb := of_decide_eq_true h
    simp only [Certificate.subject, Certificate.opponent, run, ha]
    apply (findCertificate_success program ka oa b a).2
    refine Or.inr ⟨limits.1, ?_⟩
    simp [Certificate.check, reciprocalCheck, ha, hb, limits.1, limits.2]

/-- A successful search never exceeds its declared certificate budget. -/
theorem findCertificate_bytes {program : String → Program} {k : Nat} {order : Bool}
    {a b : String} {p : Certificate} (h : findCertificate program k order a b = some p) :
    p.bytes ≤ k := by
  have hp := List.find?_some h
  exact of_decide_eq_true (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp hp).1

/-- A returned certificate proves the requested ordered pair, not merely some cooperation. -/
theorem findCertificate_sound {program : String → Program} {k : Nat} {order : Bool}
    {a b : String} {p : Certificate} (h : findCertificate program k order a b = some p) :
    run program a b = true := by
  have hp := List.find?_some h
  have checked : p.check program = true := (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp hp).2
  have hmem := List.mem_of_find?_eq_some h
  have goal : (p.subject, p.opponent) = (a, b) := by
    cases order <;> simp [candidates] at hmem <;>
      rcases hmem with rfl | rfl <;> rfl
  have cooperation := p.check_sound program checked
  have hs : p.subject = a := congrArg Prod.fst goal
  have ho : p.opponent = b := congrArg Prod.snd goal
  simpa only [hs, ho] using cooperation

/-- Against any registered opponent, including arbitrary total code, a searcher never
cooperates unilaterally. No eventual-world or population cutoff is involved. -/
theorem search_not_exploited {program : String → Program} {a b : String}
    {k : Nat} {order : Bool} (ha : program a = .search k order)
    (h : run program a b = true) : run program b a = true := by
  simp only [run, ha] at h
  rcases (findCertificate_success program k order b a).1 h with h | h
  · exact Certificate.check_sound program (.constant b a) h.2
  · exact Certificate.check_sound program (.reciprocal b a) h.2

/-- The exact self-play threshold, for every name, budget, search order and fixed registry.
This is a theorem about the two certificate rules above, not a bounded Löb theorem for PA. -/
theorem self_cooperates_iff {program : String → Program} {a : String}
    {k : Nat} {order : Bool} (ha : program a = .search k order) :
    run program a a = true ↔ (Certificate.reciprocal a a).bytes ≤ k := by
  simp [run, ha, findCertificate_success, Certificate.check, reciprocalCheck]

end ProgramEquilibrium.Bounded

module

public import ProgramEquilibrium.Agents

/-!
# Certificates for finite modal populations

A certificate supplies a world and an outcome table. Agreement of every nested box
between that world and its successor proves that the entire table has settled.
The executable checker binds the supplied table to those permanent outcomes.
Acceptance additionally requires non-exploitation, self-cooperation and a partner.
Its conclusions cover exactly the supplied population, in chain semantics.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ProgramEquilibrium
namespace Form

variable {α : Type}

/-- Every nested box agrees between the two worlds. Atoms outside boxes are not compared. -/
def BoxesAgree (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (m n : ℕ) : Form α → Prop
  | atom _ | top | bot => True
  | not φ => BoxesAgree V m n φ
  | and φ ψ | or φ ψ | imp φ ψ => BoxesAgree V m n φ ∧ BoxesAgree V m n ψ
  | box φ => eval V m (box φ) = eval V n (box φ) ∧ BoxesAgree V m n φ

theorem eval_eq_of_boxes {V : ℕ → α → Bool} {m n : ℕ}
    (hV : ∀ a, V m a = V n a) (φ : Form α) (h : BoxesAgree V m n φ) :
    eval V m φ = eval V n φ := by
  induction φ with
  | atom a => exact hV a
  | top | bot => rfl
  | not φ ih => exact congrArg (! ·) (ih h)
  | and φ ψ ihφ ihψ => exact congrArg₂ (· && ·) (ihφ h.1) (ihψ h.2)
  | or φ ψ ihφ ihψ => exact congrArg₂ (· || ·) (ihφ h.1) (ihψ h.2)
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ => exact congrArg₂ (fun x y => !x || y) (ihφ h.1) (ihψ h.2)
  | box φ => exact h.1

theorem eval_eq_of_modalized_boxes {V : ℕ → α → Bool} {m n : ℕ}
    {φ : Form α} (hφ : φ.modalized = true) (h : BoxesAgree V m n φ) :
    eval V m φ = eval V n φ := by
  induction φ with
  | atom a => simp [modalized] at hφ
  | top | bot => rfl
  | not φ ih => exact congrArg (! ·) (ih hφ h)
  | and φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    simp only [modalized, Bool.and_eq_true] at hφ
    exact congrArg₂ (· && ·) (ihφ hφ.1 h.1) (ihψ hφ.2 h.2)
  | or φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    simp only [modalized, Bool.and_eq_true] at hφ
    exact congrArg₂ (· || ·) (ihφ hφ.1 h.1) (ihψ hφ.2 h.2)
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    simp only [modalized, Bool.and_eq_true] at hφ
    exact congrArg₂ (fun x y => !x || y) (ihφ hφ.1 h.1) (ihψ hφ.2 h.2)
  | box φ => exact h.1

theorem eval_box_succ (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (n : ℕ) (φ : Form α) :
    eval V (n + 1) (box φ) = (eval V n (box φ) && eval V n φ) := by
  simp [eval, List.range_succ, List.all_append]

theorem boxes_agree_succ {V : ℕ → α → Bool} {m n : ℕ}
    (hV : ∀ a, V m a = V n a) (φ : Form α) (h : BoxesAgree V m n φ) :
    BoxesAgree V (m + 1) (n + 1) φ := by
  induction φ with
  | atom | top | bot => trivial
  | not φ ih => exact ih h
  | and φ ψ ihφ ihψ | or φ ψ ihφ ihψ | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    exact ⟨ihφ h.1, ihψ h.2⟩
  | box φ ih =>
    refine ⟨?_, ih h.2⟩
    rw [eval_box_succ, eval_box_succ, h.1, eval_eq_of_boxes hV φ h.2]

end Form

namespace Universe

variable (U : Universe)

/-- A certificate records agreement of every nested box, not merely the visible play table. -/
def Stopped (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b, Form.BoxesAgree (fun k p => U.play k p.1 p.2) n (n + 1) (U.rule a b)

theorem play_eq_succ_of_stopped {n : ℕ} (h : U.Stopped n) (a b : U.Agent) :
    U.play n a b = U.play (n + 1) a b := by
  rw [U.play_eq, U.play_eq]
  exact Form.eval_eq_of_modalized_boxes (U.rule_modalized a b) (h a b)

theorem stopped_succ {n : ℕ} (h : U.Stopped n) : U.Stopped (n + 1) := by
  intro a b
  exact Form.boxes_agree_succ (fun p => U.play_eq_succ_of_stopped h p.1 p.2)
    (U.rule a b) (h a b)

/-- Once the complete box state stops changing, every matchup is permanently settled. -/
theorem play_eq_of_stopped {n : ℕ} (h : U.Stopped n) {m : ℕ} (hm : n ≤ m)
    (a b : U.Agent) : U.play m a b = U.play n a b := by
  have step : ∀ k, U.Stopped (n + k) := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => exact h
    | succ k ih => exact U.stopped_succ ih
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hm
  clear hm
  induction k with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
    exact (U.play_eq_succ_of_stopped (step k) a b).symm.trans ih

end Universe
end ProgramEquilibrium

namespace ProgramEquilibrium.Certificate

open ProgramEquilibrium

namespace Form

/-- Executable comparison of all box occurrences, including those nested below other boxes. -/
def boxesAgree {α : Type} (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (m n : ℕ) :
    ProgramEquilibrium.Form α → Bool
  | .atom _ | .top | .bot => true
  | .not φ => boxesAgree V m n φ
  | .and φ ψ | .or φ ψ | .imp φ ψ => boxesAgree V m n φ && boxesAgree V m n ψ
  | .box φ => (ProgramEquilibrium.Form.eval V m (.box φ) ==
      ProgramEquilibrium.Form.eval V n (.box φ)) && boxesAgree V m n φ

theorem boxesAgree_sound {α : Type} {V : ℕ → α → Bool} {m n : ℕ}
    (φ : ProgramEquilibrium.Form α) (h : boxesAgree V m n φ = true) :
    ProgramEquilibrium.Form.BoxesAgree V m n φ := by
  induction φ with
  | atom | top | bot => trivial
  | not φ ih => exact ih h
  | and φ ψ ihφ ihψ | or φ ψ ihφ ihψ | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    exact ⟨ihφ (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).1, ihψ (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).2⟩
  | box φ ih =>
    exact ⟨by simpa only [beq_iff_eq] using
      (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).1, ih (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).2⟩

end Form

variable (U : Universe) (agents : List U.Agent)

/-- The row agent acts against the column agent. -/
def table (world : ℕ) : List (List Bool) :=
  agents.map fun a => agents.map fun b => U.play world a b

/-- Check the complete box state rather than only equality of successive outcome tables. -/
def stoppedCheck (world : ℕ) : Bool :=
  agents.all fun a => agents.all fun b =>
    Form.boxesAgree (fun k p => U.play k p.1 p.2) world (world + 1) (U.rule a b)

theorem stoppedCheck_sound (complete : ∀ a, a ∈ agents) {world : ℕ}
    (h : stoppedCheck U agents world = true) : U.Stopped world := by
  intro a b
  exact Form.boxesAgree_sound _
    ((List.all_eq_true.mp ((List.all_eq_true.mp h) a (complete a))) b (complete b))

/-- A valid certificate binds the supplied table to the permanent table of this population. -/
def check (world : ℕ) (claimed : List (List Bool)) : Bool :=
  stoppedCheck U agents world && (claimed == table U agents world)

theorem check_stable (complete : ∀ a, a ∈ agents) {world : ℕ}
    {claimed : List (List Bool)} (h : check U agents world claimed = true)
    {later : ℕ} (hlater : world ≤ later) (a b : U.Agent) :
    U.play later a b = U.play world a b :=
  U.play_eq_of_stopped
    (stoppedCheck_sound U agents complete (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).1) hlater a b

theorem check_table {world : ℕ} {claimed : List (List Bool)}
    (h : check U agents world claimed = true) :
    claimed = table U agents world := by
  simpa only [beq_iff_eq] using (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).2

/-- The candidate never cooperates unilaterally in the certified table. -/
def safeCheck (world : ℕ) (candidate : U.Agent) : Bool :=
  agents.all fun b => !U.play world candidate b || U.play world b candidate

/-- Mutual cooperation with another agent; self-play alone does not satisfy this condition. -/
def externalCooperation [DecidableEq U.Agent] (world : ℕ) (candidate : U.Agent) : Bool :=
  agents.any fun b => decide (b ≠ candidate) &&
    U.play world candidate b && U.play world b candidate

/-- Certificate validity and desirability are different checks: an always-defecting candidate
can submit a valid certificate but does not pass this policy criterion. -/
def accepted [DecidableEq U.Agent] (world : ℕ) (claimed : List (List Bool))
    (candidate : U.Agent) : Bool :=
  check U agents world claimed && safeCheck U agents world candidate &&
    U.play world candidate candidate && externalCooperation U agents world candidate

/-- Accepted candidates cannot be exploited by any member of the supplied population in the
eventual chain outcomes. This does not quantify over agents absent from that population. -/
theorem accepted_safe [DecidableEq U.Agent] (complete : ∀ a, a ∈ agents)
    {world : ℕ} {claimed : List (List Bool)} {candidate : U.Agent}
    (h : accepted U agents world claimed candidate = true) (b : U.Agent)
    (hc : U.Cooperates candidate b) : U.Cooperates b candidate := by
  have parts := Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h
  have parts' := Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp parts.1
  have parts'' := Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp parts'.1
  have hs := stoppedCheck_sound U agents complete (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp parts''.1).1
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hc
  have forward : U.play world candidate b = true :=
    (U.play_eq_of_stopped hs (Nat.le_max_left world k) candidate b).symm.trans
      (hk _ (Nat.le_max_right world k))
  have backward := (List.all_eq_true.mp parts''.2) b (complete b)
  have hb : U.play world b candidate = true := by simpa [forward] using backward
  exact ⟨world, fun n hn => (U.play_eq_of_stopped hs hn b candidate).trans hb⟩

theorem accepted_self_cooperation [DecidableEq U.Agent] (complete : ∀ a, a ∈ agents)
    {world : ℕ} {claimed : List (List Bool)} {candidate : U.Agent}
    (h : accepted U agents world claimed candidate = true) : U.Cooperates candidate candidate := by
  have parts := Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h
  have parts' := Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp parts.1
  have hs := stoppedCheck_sound U agents complete
    (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp parts'.1).1).1
  exact ⟨world, fun n hn => (U.play_eq_of_stopped hs hn candidate candidate).trans parts'.2⟩

theorem accepted_external_cooperation [DecidableEq U.Agent] (complete : ∀ a, a ∈ agents)
    {world : ℕ} {claimed : List (List Bool)} {candidate : U.Agent}
    (h : accepted U agents world claimed candidate = true) :
    ∃ b, b ≠ candidate ∧ U.Cooperates candidate b ∧ U.Cooperates b candidate := by
  have parts := Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h
  have hs := stoppedCheck_sound U agents complete
    (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp parts.1).1).1).1
  obtain ⟨b, _, hb⟩ := List.any_eq_true.mp parts.2
  have hpair := Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp hb
  have hleft := Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp hpair.1
  refine ⟨b, of_decide_eq_true hleft.1, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact ⟨world, fun n hn => (U.play_eq_of_stopped hs hn candidate b).trans hleft.2⟩
  · exact ⟨world, fun n hn => (U.play_eq_of_stopped hs hn b candidate).trans hpair.2⟩

module

public import ProgramEquilibrium.Agents

/-!
# Reciprocity guards

The strict prefix `□ me` and the delayed prefix `□ (¬ □^k ⊥ → me)` each prevent
eventual exploitation, even after conjoining an arbitrary extra guard. These are
statements about any compatible modal universe, not only a finite test population.
They do not guarantee useful cooperation or safety at every early world.

The delayed prefix is related to Barasz et al.'s WaitFairBot family (Section 5),
whose formula also has an outer `¬ □^k ⊥` conjunct.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ProgramEquilibrium.Form

/-- Recognize the cooperation prefix that supplies the guard's safety guarantee. -/
def isGuardedSchema {α : Type} : Form (Target α) → Bool
  | .and (.box (.atom .me)) _ => true
  | _ => false

theorem isGuardedSchema_sound {α : Type} {schema : Form (Target α)}
    (h : schema.isGuardedSchema = true) :
    ∃ guard, schema = and (box (atom .me)) guard := by
  cases schema with
  | and left guard =>
    cases left with
    | box body =>
      cases body with
      | atom target =>
        cases target with
        | me => exact ⟨guard, rfl⟩
        | agent _ => simp [isGuardedSchema] at h
      | _ => simp [isGuardedSchema] at h
    | _ => simp [isGuardedSchema] at h
  | _ => simp [isGuardedSchema] at h

end ProgramEquilibrium.Form

namespace ProgramEquilibrium.Universe

open ProgramEquilibrium Form

variable {U : Universe} {f b : U.Agent} {guard : Form (Target U.Agent)}

/-- At any world where the guarded policy cooperates, its opponent cooperated with it at every
strictly earlier world. The additional guard has no bearing on this necessary condition. -/
theorem guarded_play_requires_counterparty_below
    (hf : U.schema f = and (box (atom .me)) guard) {n : ℕ}
    (h : U.play n f b = true) : ∀ m < n, U.play m b f = true := by
  rw [U.play_eq] at h
  simp only [rule, hf, map] at h
  have hbox := (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).1
  exact (eval_box (fun k p => U.play k p.1 p.2) n (atom (b, f))).1 hbox

/-- Eventual cooperation by the guarded policy requires its opponent to cooperate with it at
every world, not merely at sufficiently late worlds. -/
theorem guard_cooperation_requires_counterparty_all_worlds
    (hf : U.schema f = and (box (atom .me)) guard)
    (h : U.Cooperates f b) : ∀ m, U.play m b f = true := by
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := h
  intro m
  exact guarded_play_requires_counterparty_below hf
    (hK (max K (m + 1)) (Nat.le_max_left K (m + 1))) m (by omega)

/-- An opponent that eventually defects causes this guarded policy to eventually defect too.
This holds for any extra guard and does not rely on testing a finite list of opponents. -/
theorem guarded_unexploitable (hf : U.schema f = and (box (atom .me)) guard)
    (h : U.Defects b f) : U.Defects f b := by
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := h
  refine ⟨K + 1, fun n hn => Bool.eq_false_iff.2 ?_⟩
  intro hcoop
  have counterparty := guarded_play_requires_counterparty_below hf hcoop K (by omega)
  rw [hK K (Nat.le_refl K)] at counterparty
  contradiction

/-- Guarded cooperation and eventual counterparty defection cannot occur together. -/
theorem guarded_not_exploited (hf : U.schema f = and (box (atom .me)) guard) :
    ¬ (U.Cooperates f b ∧ U.Defects b f) := by
  rintro ⟨hcoop, hdefect⟩
  exact U.not_cooperates_and_defects f b ⟨hcoop, guarded_unexploitable hf hdefect⟩

/-- The executable schema check suffices for non-exploitation against every opponent in any
universe containing the checked agent, whether that universe is finite or infinite. -/
theorem checked_guard_not_exploited (h : (U.schema f).isGuardedSchema = true) :
    ¬ (U.Cooperates f b ∧ U.Defects b f) := by
  obtain ⟨guard, hguard⟩ := Form.isGuardedSchema_sound h
  exact guarded_not_exploited hguard

end ProgramEquilibrium.Universe

namespace ProgramEquilibrium.Form

/-- `k` boxes around falsity, true exactly below world `k`. -/
def cutoff {α : Type} : ℕ → Form α
  | 0 => bot
  | k + 1 => box (cutoff k)

@[simp] theorem map_cutoff {α β : Type} (f : α → β) (k : ℕ) :
    (cutoff k).map f = cutoff k := by
  induction k with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih => simp [cutoff, map, ih]

theorem eval_cutoff {α : Type} (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (k n : ℕ) :
    eval V n (cutoff k) = true ↔ n < k := by
  induction k generalizing n with
  | zero => simp [cutoff, eval]
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [cutoff, eval_box]
    constructor
    · intro h
      by_contra hn
      have hk : k < n := by omega
      have := (ih k).1 (h k hk)
      omega
    · intro hn m hm
      exact (ih m).2 (by omega)

end ProgramEquilibrium.Form

namespace ProgramEquilibrium.Universe

open Form

variable {U : Universe} {f b : U.Agent} {k : ℕ} {guard : Form (Target U.Agent)}

/-- Cooperation requires reciprocity at every earlier world above the cutoff. -/
theorem delayed_guard_requires_reciprocity
    (hf : U.schema f = and (box (imp (not (cutoff k)) (atom .me))) guard)
    {n m : ℕ} (h : U.play n f b = true) (hkm : k ≤ m) (hmn : m < n) :
    U.play m b f = true := by
  rw [U.play_eq] at h
  simp only [rule, hf, map, map_cutoff] at h
  have hbox := (Bool.and_eq_true_iff.mp h).1
  have hbody := (eval_box _ _ _).1 hbox m hmn
  have hcut : eval (fun j (p : U.Agent × U.Agent) => U.play j p.1 p.2)
      m (cutoff k) = false := by
    apply Bool.eq_false_iff.2
    intro htrue
    have := (eval_cutoff _ k m).1 htrue
    omega
  have hnot := (eval_not _ _ _).2 hcut
  exact (eval_imp _ _ _ _).1 hbody hnot

/-- A finite modal cutoff does not allow cooperation with an eventual defector. -/
theorem delayed_guard_unexploitable
    (hf : U.schema f = and (box (imp (not (cutoff k)) (atom .me))) guard)
    (h : U.Defects b f) : U.Defects f b := by
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := h
  refine ⟨max K k + 1, fun n hn => Bool.eq_false_iff.2 ?_⟩
  intro hcoop
  have other := delayed_guard_requires_reciprocity hf hcoop
    (m := max K k) (Nat.le_max_right K k) (by omega)
  rw [hK (max K k) (Nat.le_max_left K k)] at other
  contradiction

/-- The delayed guard prevents eventual exploitation in any compatible universe. -/
theorem delayed_guard_not_exploited
    (hf : U.schema f = and (box (imp (not (cutoff k)) (atom .me))) guard) :
    ¬ (U.Cooperates f b ∧ U.Defects b f) := by
  rintro ⟨hcoop, hdefect⟩
  exact U.not_cooperates_and_defects f b
    ⟨hcoop, delayed_guard_unexploitable hf hdefect⟩

end ProgramEquilibrium.Universe

module

public import ProgramEquilibrium.Guards

/-!
# The policy recovered by both samplers

The primary selection uses the supplied delayed-reciprocity control. The model-only
selections are Boolean rewrites of that control, as checked below. These theorems
concern modal semantics, not the neural models that proposed the formulas.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ProgramEquilibrium.Inkling

open ProgramEquilibrium Form

/-- Literal translation of the selected JSON constructor tree. -/
def control {Agent : Type} : Form (Target Agent) :=
  and (box (imp (not (box bot)) (atom .me))) top

/-- Literal constructor tree proposed by the base sampler. -/
def baseProposal {Agent : Type} : Form (Target Agent) :=
  and (box (imp (not (box bot)) (atom .me))) control

/-- Literal constructor tree proposed by the trained sampler. -/
def trainedProposal {Agent : Type} : Form (Target Agent) :=
  and (box (imp (not (box bot)) (atom .me)))
    (or (box (atom .me)) (not (box (atom .me))))

/-- The base sampler duplicated an existing conjunct rather than changing the rule. -/
theorem eval_base_eq_control {Agent : Type} (V : ℕ → Target Agent → Bool) (n : ℕ) :
    eval V n baseProposal = eval V n control := by
  simp [baseProposal, control, eval]

/-- The trained sampler's added guard is a Boolean tautology. -/
theorem eval_trained_eq_control {Agent : Type} (V : ℕ → Target Agent → Bool) (n : ℕ) :
    eval V n trainedProposal = eval V n control := by
  simp [trainedProposal, control, eval]

/-- The selected policy cannot eventually cooperate with an eventual defector. -/
theorem control_not_exploited (U : Universe) (f b : U.Agent)
    (hf : U.schema f = control) :
    ¬ (U.Cooperates f b ∧ U.Defects b f) := by
  exact Universe.delayed_guard_not_exploited (k := 1) (guard := top) hf

/-- Self-cooperation is not merely observed on the finite benchmark populations. -/
theorem control_self_cooperates (U : Universe) (f : U.Agent)
    (hf : U.schema f = control) : U.Cooperates f f := by
  refine ⟨0, fun n _ => ?_⟩
  induction n using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ n ih =>
    rw [U.play_eq]
    simp only [Universe.rule, hf, control, map, eval, Bool.and_true]
    apply List.all_eq_true.mpr
    intro m hm
    have hprior := ih m (List.mem_range.mp hm)
    simp [hprior]

end ProgramEquilibrium.Inkling

module

public import Mathlib.Order.Basic

/-!
# Modal formulas on the chain of worlds

`Form α` is the language of provability logic with atoms in `α`: the connectives and a box,
read "it is provable that". `eval V n φ` evaluates `φ` at world `n` of the chain `0, 1, 2, …`,
where world `n` sees exactly the worlds below it and `V m a` is the truth value of the atom `a`
at world `m`. Each world sees a finite strict linear order, and such frames validate the
provability logic GL (which also has branching frames).

`loeb` checks Löb's axiom `□(□φ → φ) → □φ` at every world for every valuation. A formula is
`modalized` when every atom sits under a box; `eval_congr_of_modalized` says that such a formula
only looks at worlds strictly below the one where it is evaluated, which is what lets an agent's
decision at world `n` be computed from the worlds before it.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ProgramEquilibrium

/-- Formulas of provability logic over atoms of type `α`. -/
inductive Form (α : Type) where
  | atom : α → Form α
  | top : Form α
  | bot : Form α
  | not : Form α → Form α
  | and : Form α → Form α → Form α
  | or : Form α → Form α → Form α
  | imp : Form α → Form α → Form α
  | box : Form α → Form α
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

namespace Form

variable {α : Type}

/-- Truth of `φ` at world `n` of the chain, where `□ψ` holds at `n` when `ψ` holds at every
world below `n`. -/
def eval (V : ℕ → α → Bool) : ℕ → Form α → Bool
  | n, atom a => V n a
  | _, top => true
  | _, bot => false
  | n, not φ => !eval V n φ
  | n, and φ ψ => eval V n φ && eval V n ψ
  | n, or φ ψ => eval V n φ || eval V n ψ
  | n, imp φ ψ => !eval V n φ || eval V n ψ
  | n, box φ => (List.range n).all fun m => eval V m φ

theorem eval_box (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (n : ℕ) (φ : Form α) :
    eval V n (box φ) = true ↔ ∀ m < n, eval V m φ = true := by
  simp [eval, List.all_eq_true, List.mem_range]

theorem eval_imp (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (n : ℕ) (φ ψ : Form α) :
    eval V n (imp φ ψ) = true ↔ (eval V n φ = true → eval V n ψ = true) := by
  cases h : eval V n φ <;> simp [eval, h]

theorem eval_not (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (n : ℕ) (φ : Form α) :
    eval V n (not φ) = true ↔ eval V n φ = false := by
  simp [eval]

/-- `□⊥` holds exactly at world `0`, the world that sees nothing. -/
theorem eval_box_bot (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (n : ℕ) : eval V n (box bot) = true ↔ n = 0 := by
  rw [eval_box]
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hn
    simpa [eval] using h 0 (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn)
  · rintro rfl m hm
    omega

/-- Löb's axiom `□(□φ → φ) → □φ` holds at every world of the chain, for every valuation. -/
theorem loeb (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (n : ℕ) (φ : Form α) :
    eval V n (imp (box (imp (box φ) φ)) (box φ)) = true := by
  rw [eval_imp, eval_box, eval_box]
  intro h m hm
  induction m using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ m ih =>
    have step := (eval_imp V m (box φ) φ).1 (h m hm)
    exact step ((eval_box V m φ).2 fun k hk => ih k hk (by omega))

/-- Every atom of `φ` occurs under a box. -/
def modalized : Form α → Bool
  | atom _ => false
  | top => true
  | bot => true
  | not φ => modalized φ
  | and φ ψ => modalized φ && modalized ψ
  | or φ ψ => modalized φ && modalized ψ
  | imp φ ψ => modalized φ && modalized ψ
  | box _ => true

/-- Rename the atoms of a formula. -/
def map {β : Type} (f : α → β) : Form α → Form β
  | atom a => atom (f a)
  | top => top
  | bot => bot
  | not φ => not (map f φ)
  | and φ ψ => and (map f φ) (map f ψ)
  | or φ ψ => or (map f φ) (map f ψ)
  | imp φ ψ => imp (map f φ) (map f ψ)
  | box φ => box (map f φ)

@[simp] theorem modalized_map {β : Type} (f : α → β) (φ : Form α) :
    (map f φ).modalized = φ.modalized := by
  induction φ <;> simp_all [map, modalized]

/-- The value at world `k` depends only on the valuation at worlds up to `k`. -/
theorem eval_congr_le {V W : ℕ → α → Bool} {k : ℕ} (h : ∀ m ≤ k, ∀ a, V m a = W m a)
    (φ : Form α) : eval V k φ = eval W k φ := by
  induction φ generalizing k with
  | atom a => exact h k (Nat.le_refl k) a
  | top | bot => rfl
  | not φ ih => simp [eval, ih h]
  | and φ ψ ihφ ihψ => simp [eval, ihφ h, ihψ h]
  | or φ ψ ihφ ihψ => simp [eval, ihφ h, ihψ h]
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ => simp [eval, ihφ h, ihψ h]
  | box φ ih =>
    have agree : ∀ m < k, eval V m φ = eval W m φ := fun m hm =>
      ih fun j hj a => h j (by omega) a
    apply Bool.eq_iff_iff.2
    rw [eval_box, eval_box]
    exact forall₂_congr fun m hm => by rw [agree m hm]

/-- A modalized formula at world `n` depends only on the valuation at worlds below `n`. -/
theorem eval_congr_of_modalized {V W : ℕ → α → Bool} {n : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ m < n, ∀ a, V m a = W m a) {φ : Form α} (hφ : modalized φ = true) :
    eval V n φ = eval W n φ := by
  induction φ with
  | atom a => simp [modalized] at hφ
  | top | bot => rfl
  | not φ ih =>
    simp only [modalized] at hφ
    simp [eval, ih hφ]
  | and φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    simp only [modalized, Bool.and_eq_true] at hφ
    simp [eval, ihφ hφ.1, ihψ hφ.2]
  | or φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    simp only [modalized, Bool.and_eq_true] at hφ
    simp [eval, ihφ hφ.1, ihψ hφ.2]
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    simp only [modalized, Bool.and_eq_true] at hφ
    simp [eval, ihφ hφ.1, ihψ hφ.2]
  | box φ =>
    apply Bool.eq_iff_iff.2
    rw [eval_box, eval_box]
    exact forall₂_congr fun m hm => by
      rw [eval_congr_le (fun j hj a => h j (by omega) a) φ]

/-- Under any valuation, a boxed formula changes value at most once, from true to false: either
its body holds at every world, or a world where it fails falsifies the box above it. -/
theorem box_stabilizes (V : ℕ → α → Bool) (φ : Form α) :
    ∃ K, ∀ n ≥ K, eval V n (box φ) = eval V K (box φ) := by
  by_cases h : ∀ m, eval V m φ = true
  · refine ⟨0, fun n _ => ?_⟩
    rw [(eval_box V n φ).2 fun m _ => h m, (eval_box V 0 φ).2 fun m _ => h m]
  · obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := Classical.not_forall.1 h
    have low : ∀ k > m, eval V k (box φ) = false := fun k hk =>
      Bool.eq_false_iff.2 fun hb => hm ((eval_box V k φ).1 hb m hk)
    exact ⟨m + 1, fun n hn => by rw [low n (by omega), low (m + 1) (by omega)]⟩

/-- Under any valuation, a modalized formula is eventually constant along the chain. -/
theorem stabilizes_of_modalized (V : ℕ → α → Bool) {φ : Form α} (hφ : modalized φ = true) :
    ∃ K, ∀ n ≥ K, eval V n φ = eval V K φ := by
  have pair : ∀ {φ ψ : Form α} (f : Bool → Bool → Bool),
      (∃ K, ∀ n ≥ K, eval V n φ = eval V K φ) → (∃ K, ∀ n ≥ K, eval V n ψ = eval V K ψ) →
      ∃ K, ∀ n ≥ K, f (eval V n φ) (eval V n ψ) = f (eval V K φ) (eval V K ψ) := by
    rintro φ ψ f ⟨K₁, h₁⟩ ⟨K₂, h₂⟩
    refine ⟨max K₁ K₂, fun n hn => ?_⟩
    rw [h₁ n (by omega), h₂ n (by omega), h₁ (max K₁ K₂) (by omega), h₂ (max K₁ K₂) (by omega)]
  induction φ with
  | atom a => simp [modalized] at hφ
  | top | bot => exact ⟨0, fun _ _ => rfl⟩
  | not φ ih =>
    simp only [modalized] at hφ
    obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := ih hφ
    exact ⟨K, fun n hn => by simp [eval, hK n hn]⟩
  | and φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    simp only [modalized, Bool.and_eq_true] at hφ
    exact pair (· && ·) (ihφ hφ.1) (ihψ hφ.2)
  | or φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    simp only [modalized, Bool.and_eq_true] at hφ
    exact pair (· || ·) (ihφ hφ.1) (ihψ hφ.2)
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
    simp only [modalized, Bool.and_eq_true] at hφ
    exact pair (fun x y => !x || y) (ihφ hφ.1) (ihψ hφ.2)
  | box φ => exact box_stabilizes V φ

/-! ### Löb's axiom on other frames

`holdsOn R V w φ` reads `φ` at world `w` of an arbitrary frame, where `□ψ` holds at `w` when `ψ`
holds at every `v` with `R v w` (`w` sees `v`). Löb's axiom holds on every transitive frame whose
relation is well founded, and `loeb_needs_transitivity` shows that transitivity cannot be dropped.
-/

/-- Truth on an arbitrary frame, where `R v w` means that `w` sees `v`. -/
def holdsOn {W : Type} (R : W → W → Prop) (V : W → α → Prop) : W → Form α → Prop
  | w, atom a => V w a
  | _, top => True
  | _, bot => False
  | w, not φ => ¬ holdsOn R V w φ
  | w, and φ ψ => holdsOn R V w φ ∧ holdsOn R V w ψ
  | w, or φ ψ => holdsOn R V w φ ∨ holdsOn R V w ψ
  | w, imp φ ψ => holdsOn R V w φ → holdsOn R V w ψ
  | w, box φ => ∀ v, R v w → holdsOn R V v φ

/-- Löb's axiom holds on every transitive, well-founded frame. -/
theorem loeb_of_wellFounded {W : Type} (R : W → W → Prop) (trans : ∀ u v w, R u v → R v w → R u w)
    (wf : WellFounded R) (V : W → α → Prop) (w : W) (φ : Form α) :
    holdsOn R V w (imp (box (imp (box φ) φ)) (box φ)) := by
  intro h v hv
  induction v using wf.induction with
  | _ v ih => exact h v hv fun u hu => ih u hu (trans u v w hu hv)

/-- Without transitivity Löb's axiom can fail: world `2` sees `1`, `1` sees `0`, but `2` does not
see `0`, and the atom is false at `0` and `1`. -/
theorem loeb_needs_transitivity :
    ¬ holdsOn (fun v w : Fin 3 => w.val = v.val + 1) (fun w (_ : Unit) => w.val = 2) 2
      (imp (box (imp (box (atom ())) (atom ()))) (box (atom ()))) := by
  intro h
  have step : ∀ v : Fin 3, (2 : Fin 3).val = v.val + 1 →
      (∀ u : Fin 3, v.val = u.val + 1 → u.val = 2) → v.val = 2 := by
    intro v hv hbox
    have hv' : v.val = 1 := by
      have h2 : (2 : Fin 3).val = 2 := rfl
      omega
    have hv1 : v = 1 := Fin.ext hv'
    subst hv1
    exact absurd (hbox 0 rfl) (by decide)
  have h1 : (1 : Fin 3).val = 2 := h step 1 rfl
  exact absurd h1 (by decide)

end Form

end ProgramEquilibrium

module

public import BoundedLob.Agents.Search
public import BoundedLob.Agents.Sources
public import BoundedLob.Checker.Calculus
public import BoundedLob.Theory.Robust
import Mathlib.Tactic.Set

/-!
# Different implementations cooperate

`System.robust` for the checker's system (`fair_cooperate`). Two agents whose sources, read in
the match, are `□_{t_A} α` and `□_{t_B} β` cooperate with each other at every large budget,
provided:

* the checker proves `α` and `β` from mutual cooperation `coop a b ∧ coop b a`;
* some budget `u(k)`, growing faster than `lg k`, stays below both `t_A` and `t_B` by `lg k`
  and any constant.

The conjunction is `¬(X → ¬Y)`, with the rules `Cert.conjLeft`, `Cert.conjRight` and
`Cert.conjIntro`. Instances: DUPOC with any two linear budgets `p·k + r` and `q·k + s` with
`p, q ≥ 1` (`dupoc_linear`), DUPOC against CIMCIC (`dupoc_cimcic`, Theorem 5.2 of Critch, Dennis
and Russell), and DUPOC against a DUPOC written with a redundant `⊤ →` (`dupoc_top`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BoundedLob

open Form Agent

/-- **Robust cooperation** in the checker's system. Two guarded sources that read, in the match,
as `□_{t_A} α` and `□_{t_B} β` cooperate at every large `k`, when the checker proves `α` and `β`
from mutual cooperation and some budget `u` growing faster than `lg k` stays below `t_A` and
`t_B` by `lg k` and any constant. -/
theorem fair_cooperate {a b α β : Form} {ta tb u : Bound}
    (ha : a.isPlaceholder = false) (hb : b.isPlaceholder = false) (hga : a.guarded = true)
    (hgb : b.guarded = true) (hfa : a.fill b a = box ta α) (hfb : b.fill a b = box tb β)
    (hα : calculus.Proves (calculus.above 0 (imp (Form.conj (coop a b) (coop b a)) α)))
    (hβ : calculus.Proves (calculus.above 0 (imp (Form.conj (coop a b) (coop b a)) β)))
    (hu : GrowsFasterThanLog (u.eval id))
    (gapA : ∀ c, ∃ K, ∀ k > K, u.eval id k + Nat.log 2 k + c ≤ ta.eval id k)
    (gapB : ∀ c, ∃ K, ∀ k > K, u.eval id k + Nat.log 2 k + c ≤ tb.eval id k) :
    ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k a b = true ∧ run k b a = true := by
  set X := coop a b
  set Y := coop b a
  have fairA := proves_of_check (a := 0) (φ := imp (box ta α) X) (.iffR .prog) (by
    simp [X, check, Sen.withForm, Sen.form, ha, hb, hga, hfa])
  have fairB := proves_of_check (a := 0) (φ := imp (box tb β) Y) (.iffR .prog) (by
    simp [Y, check, Sen.withForm, Sen.form, ha, hb, hgb, hfb])
  have hP := proves_of_check _ (check_conjIntro X Y)
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := calculus.robust hu gapA gapB hα hβ hP fairA fairB
  have hX := calculus.mp (proves_of_check _ (check_conjLeft X Y)) hK
  have hY := calculus.mp (proves_of_check _ (check_conjRight X Y)) hK
  refine ⟨max 0 K, fun k hk => ⟨(run_spec k a b).2 ?_, (run_spec k b a).2 ?_⟩⟩
  · exact calculus_sound hX k hk
  · exact calculus_sound hY k hk

/-- `X ∧ Y → (ψ → X)`, for an unused hypothesis `ψ`. -/
theorem proves_conj_addHyp (X Y ψ : Form) :
    calculus.Proves (calculus.above 0 (imp (Form.conj X Y) (imp ψ X))) :=
  proves_of_check _ (check_addHyp ψ (check_conjLeft X Y))

/-- A linear budget `p·k + r` with `p ≥ 1` is at least `k`. -/
theorem le_linear {p r : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) (k : ℕ) :
    k ≤ (Bound.add (.scale p .f) (.const r)).eval id k := by
  have := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left k hp
  simp only [Bound.eval, id]
  omega

/-- **Budgets may differ.** For every fixed `p, q ≥ 1` and `r, s`, DUPOC with budget `p·k + r`
and DUPOC with budget `q·k + s` cooperate with each other at every large `k`. -/
theorem dupoc_linear {p q r s : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) (hq : 0 < q) :
    ∃ K, ∀ k > K,
      run k (dupoc (.add (.scale p .f) (.const r))) (dupoc (.add (.scale q .f) (.const s))) =
          true ∧
        run k (dupoc (.add (.scale q .f) (.const s))) (dupoc (.add (.scale p .f) (.const r))) =
          true :=
  fair_cooperate (u := .div .f 2) (ha := rfl) (hb := rfl) (hga := rfl) (hgb := rfl)
    (hfa := rfl) (hfb := rfl) (proves_of_check _ (check_conjRight _ _))
    (proves_of_check _ (check_conjLeft _ _)) (growsFasterThanLog_id.div 2 (by decide))
    (gap_half (le_linear hp)) (gap_half (le_linear hq))

/-- **Theorem 5.2** of Critch, Dennis and Russell: DUPOC and CIMCIC cooperate at every large `k`.
CIMCIC's condition, "if I cooperate then you do", follows from mutual cooperation. -/
theorem dupoc_cimcic : ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k dupoc cimcic = true ∧ run k cimcic dupoc = true :=
  fair_cooperate (α := coop cimcic dupoc) (β := imp (coop cimcic dupoc) (coop dupoc cimcic))
    (u := .div .f 2) (ha := rfl) (hb := rfl) (hga := rfl) (hgb := rfl) (hfa := rfl) (hfb := rfl)
    (proves_of_check _ (check_conjRight _ _)) (proves_conj_addHyp _ _ _)
    (growsFasterThanLog_id.div 2 (by decide)) (gap_half fun _ => le_rfl)
    (gap_half fun _ => le_rfl)

/-- DUPOC and a DUPOC whose source reads "if true, then the opponent cooperates" cooperate at
every large `k`. -/
theorem dupoc_top : ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k dupoc dupocTop = true ∧ run k dupocTop dupoc = true :=
  fair_cooperate (α := coop dupocTop dupoc) (β := imp top (coop dupoc dupocTop))
    (u := .div .f 2) (ha := rfl) (hb := rfl) (hga := rfl) (hgb := rfl) (hfa := rfl) (hfb := rfl)
    (proves_of_check _ (check_conjRight _ _)) (proves_conj_addHyp _ _ _)
    (growsFasterThanLog_id.div 2 (by decide)) (gap_half fun _ => le_rfl)
    (gap_half fun _ => le_rfl)

end BoundedLob

module

public import BoundedLob.Agents.Search
public import BoundedLob.Agents.Sources
public import BoundedLob.Checker.Calculus
public import BoundedLob.Theory.Dimcid
import Mathlib.Tactic.Set

/-!
# Outcomes

Theorems about `run` itself, the program that searches for proofs. Two kinds of argument appear:

* **Bounded Löb**, through `calculus`: the abstract theorems `System.pblt` and
  `System.self_fulfilling` give a proof in the checker's system, `calculus_sound` makes it true,
  and `run_spec` makes it what the program does. These hold for every `k` beyond some threshold.
* **The worlds**: a sentence false at world `0` has no proof at all (`not_provable_of_world0`),
  so a search for it fails at every budget. These hold for every `k`.

For DUPOC against itself the threshold is explicit: the kernel builds the certificate the agent
tries first and checks it, and `dupoc_fast` shows that the search accepts it at every larger
budget.

The outcomes are those of Critch, Dennis and Russell's Theorems 3.4, 3.7 and 5.5, the
conjectured `(D, C)` of their Open Problem 3 and the outcome of their Open Problem 5 in this
system, `(D, D)` for their Open Problem 6, and a correction to their Example 5.3(a): DIMCID
defects against CooperateBot.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BoundedLob

open Form Agent

/-! ### DUPOC against itself -/

/-- **Theorem 3.7.** DUPOC cooperates with itself at every large budget, from the abstract
bounded Löb theorem. -/
theorem dupoc_self : ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k dupoc dupoc = true := by
  have hyp := proves_of_check (a := 0) (φ := imp (box .f (coop dupoc dupoc)) (coop dupoc dupoc))
    (.iffR .prog) (by decide)
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := calculus.pblt .f growsFasterThanLog_id hyp
  exact ⟨K, fun k hk => (run_spec k _ _).2 (calculus_sound hK k hk)⟩

/-- The certificate DUPOC builds against itself, of `∀ k > 17879, coop(DUPOC, DUPOC)`. -/
def selfProof : Candidate :=
  (Candidate.lob .f (coop dupoc dupoc) 0 (.iffR .prog)).get (by decide +kernel)

/-- `selfProof` is what the builder returns. -/
theorem selfProof_built : Candidate.lob .f (coop dupoc dupoc) 0 (.iffR .prog) = some selfProof :=
  (Option.some_get _).symm

/-- The guard of `selfProof`: the largest of the guards of its two monotonicity steps and its
inner necessitation (`K₁`, `K₂` and `a₆` in `Candidate.lob`), computed by the builder. It is
where this certificate becomes valid, not the smallest budget at which two DUPOCs cooperate. -/
def selfThreshold : ℕ := 17879

/-- The kernel computes the guard and size of `selfProof` and checks it. -/
theorem selfProof_spec : selfProof.guard = selfThreshold ∧ selfProof.cert.size = 2962 ∧
    check selfProof.cert (.all selfThreshold (coop dupoc dupoc)) = true := by
  decide +kernel

/-- At `k`, the instance of `selfProof` has `lg k + 2993` characters: the certificate (2962),
its instantiation at the guard (`lg 17879 + 3 = 17`), the formula `coop dupoc dupoc` (11) and
the numeral and markers of the sentence (`lg k + 3`). -/
theorem selfProof_len (k : ℕ) :
    len (.inst selfThreshold selfProof.cert) (.inst k (coop dupoc dupoc)) = Nat.log 2 k + 2993 := by
  simp only [len_inst, Cert.size_inst, selfProof_spec.2.1]
  have : Nat.log 2 selfThreshold = 14 := by decide
  rw [this]
  simp [Form.size, Form.text, dupoc, Bound.text]

/-- The proof fits in the budget from the guard on (`12` is a convenient base for the induction
`L + 2993 ≤ 2^L`). -/
private theorem selfProof_fits {k : ℕ} (hk : selfThreshold < k) : Nat.log 2 k + 2993 ≤ k := by
  have big : ∀ L ≥ 12, L + 2993 ≤ 2 ^ L := by
    intro L hL
    induction L, hL using Nat.le_induction with
    | base => decide
    | succ L _ ih => rw [Nat.pow_succ]; omega
  have hpow := Nat.pow_log_le_self 2 (show k ≠ 0 by omega)
  by_cases hL : Nat.log 2 k ≤ 12
  · simp only [selfThreshold] at hk
    omega
  · exact le_trans (big _ (by omega)) hpow

/-- Past the guard, the instance of `selfProof` checks. -/
theorem selfProof_check {k : ℕ} (hk : selfThreshold < k) :
    check (.inst selfThreshold selfProof.cert) (.inst k (coop dupoc dupoc)) = true := by
  simp [check, hk, selfProof_spec.2.2]

/-- Past the guard, the instance of `selfProof` is among DUPOC's candidates. -/
theorem selfProof_mem {k : ℕ} (hk : selfThreshold < k) :
    Cert.inst selfThreshold selfProof.cert ∈ candidates (.inst k (coop dupoc dupoc)) := by
  simp only [candidates, List.mem_filterMap]
  refine ⟨selfProof, ?_, by simp [selfProof_spec.1, hk]⟩
  have hb : Candidate.dupocBudget dupoc = some .f := rfl
  simp only [Candidate.forForm, Candidate.forCooperation, hb, beq_self_eq_true, ↓reduceIte,
    selfProof_built, Option.toList_some, List.cons_append, List.mem_cons, true_or]

/-- **The fast path.** For every `k > 17879`, DUPOC's search against itself is not refuted by the
worlds and accepts the certificate it builds; the complete search over strings is never
reached. -/
theorem dupoc_fast {k : ℕ} (hk : selfThreshold < k) :
    refuted worldDepth (coop dupoc dupoc) = false ∧
      byCandidate k (.inst k (coop dupoc dupoc)) = true := by
  have hp : Provable k (.inst k (coop dupoc dupoc)) :=
    ⟨_, selfProof_check hk, (selfProof_len k).trans_le (selfProof_fits hk)⟩
  refine ⟨?_, List.any_eq_true.2 ⟨_, selfProof_mem hk, affordable_iff.2 ⟨selfProof_check hk,
    (selfProof_len k).trans_le (selfProof_fits hk)⟩⟩⟩
  cases hr : refuted worldDepth (coop dupoc dupoc)
  · rfl
  · exact absurd hp (not_provable_of_refuted (σ := .inst k (coop dupoc dupoc)) hr k)

/-- **Theorem 3.7, with its threshold.** DUPOC cooperates with itself at every `k > 17879`. -/
theorem dupoc_self_of_lt {k : ℕ} (hk : selfThreshold < k) : run k dupoc dupoc = true := by
  obtain ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ := dupoc_fast hk
  have : run k dupoc dupoc = search k (.inst k (coop dupoc dupoc)) := rfl
  rw [this, search]
  simp [Sen.form, h₁, h₂]

/-! ### Self-fulfilling defection -/

/-- **Theorem 3.4.** CUPOD defects against itself at every large budget. -/
theorem cupod_self : ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k cupod cupod = false := by
  have hyp := proves_of_check (a := 0)
    (φ := imp (box .f (neg (coop cupod cupod))) (neg (coop cupod cupod)))
    (Cert.swap (coop cupod cupod) (box .f (neg (coop cupod cupod))) bot (.iffL .prog))
    (by decide)
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := calculus.pblt .f growsFasterThanLog_id hyp
  refine ⟨K, fun k hk => ?_⟩
  cases h : run k cupod cupod
  · rfl
  · exact absurd ((run_spec k _ _).1 h) (calculus_sound hK k hk)

/-- DIMCID's defection against `b`, proved in the checker's system. -/
theorem dimcid_proves {b : Form} (hb : b.isPlaceholder = false) :
    ∃ K, calculus.Proves (calculus.above K (neg (coop dimcid b))) := by
  set A := coop dimcid b
  set G := imp A (neg (coop b dimcid))
  have exfalso := proves_of_check (a := 0) (φ := imp (neg A) G)
    (Cert.impMono A bot (neg (coop b dimcid)) (Cert.efq (neg (coop b dimcid)))) (by
      simp [A, G, check, Cert.impMono, Cert.efq, Cert.trans, Sen.withForm, Sen.form])
  have code := proves_of_check (a := 0) (φ := imp (box .f G) (neg A))
    (Cert.swap A (box .f G) bot (.iffL .prog)) (by
      simp [A, G, check, Cert.swap, Cert.trans, Sen.withForm, Sen.form, hb, dimcid, guarded,
        fill, fillArg])
  exact calculus.self_fulfilling growsFasterThanLog_id exfalso code

/-- What `calculus` proves about DIMCID's defection, `run` does. -/
private theorem dimcid_run {b : Form} {K : ℕ}
    (h : calculus.Proves (calculus.above K (neg (coop dimcid b)))) :
    ∀ k > K, run k dimcid b = false := by
  intro k hk
  cases hr : run k dimcid b
  · rfl
  · exact absurd ((run_spec k _ _).1 hr) (calculus_sound h k hk)

/-- DIMCID defects against `b` at every large budget, for each source `b`; the threshold depends
on `b`. -/
theorem dimcid_defects {b : Form} (hb : b.isPlaceholder = false) :
    ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k dimcid b = false :=
  (dimcid_proves hb).imp fun _ => dimcid_run

/-- **Open Problem 6.** DUPOC against DIMCID: DUPOC defects at every budget, DIMCID at every
large budget. -/
theorem dupoc_dimcid :
    (∀ k, run k dupoc dimcid = false) ∧ ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k dimcid dupoc = false := by
  refine ⟨fun k => ?_, dimcid_defects rfl⟩
  cases h : run k dupoc dimcid
  · rfl
  · rw [run_iff_holds_fill rfl rfl rfl] at h
    refine absurd h (not_provable_of_world0 ?_)
    simp only [Sen.form, Form.within_none]
    decide

/-- **Correction to Example 5.3(a).** DIMCID defects against CooperateBot at every large budget,
where the paper answers `(C, C)`. -/
theorem dimcid_vs_cooperate :
    ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k dimcid cooperate = false ∧ run k cooperate dimcid = true :=
  (dimcid_defects rfl).imp fun _ h k hk => ⟨h k hk, rfl⟩

/-- **Theorem 5.5(a).** DIMCID defects against itself at every large budget. -/
theorem dimcid_self : ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k dimcid dimcid = false := dimcid_defects rfl

/-- **Theorem 5.5(b).** CUPOD against DIMCID ends in mutual defection at every large budget:
CUPOD finds the proof of DIMCID's defection. -/
theorem cupod_dimcid :
    ∃ K, ∀ k > K, run k cupod dimcid = false ∧ run k dimcid cupod = false := by
  obtain ⟨K₁, h₁⟩ := dimcid_proves (b := cupod) rfl
  obtain ⟨K₂, h₂⟩ := provable_of_proves h₁
  refine ⟨max K₁ K₂, fun k hk => ⟨?_, dimcid_run h₁ k (by omega)⟩⟩
  cases h : run k cupod dimcid
  · rfl
  · rw [run_iff_holds_fill rfl rfl rfl] at h
    exact absurd (h₂ k (by omega)) h

/-! ### The worlds -/

/-- **Open Problem 3**, in this system: DUPOC defects and CUPOD cooperates, at every budget. -/
theorem dupoc_cupod (k : ℕ) : run k dupoc cupod = false ∧ run k cupod dupoc = true := by
  constructor
  · cases h : run k dupoc cupod
    · rfl
    · rw [run_iff_holds_fill rfl rfl rfl] at h
      refine absurd h (not_provable_of_world0 ?_)
      simp only [Sen.form, Form.within_none]
      decide
  · rw [run_iff_holds_fill rfl rfl rfl]
    exact not_provable_of_world0 (by simp only [Sen.form, Form.within_none]; decide)

/-- **Open Problem 5**, in this system: CUPOD cooperates and CIMCIC defects, at every budget. -/
theorem cupod_cimcic (k : ℕ) : run k cupod cimcic = true ∧ run k cimcic cupod = false := by
  constructor
  · rw [run_iff_holds_fill rfl rfl rfl]
    exact not_provable_of_world0 (by simp only [Sen.form, Form.within_none]; decide)
  · cases h : run k cimcic cupod
    · rfl
    · rw [run_iff_holds_fill rfl rfl rfl] at h
      refine absurd h (not_provable_of_world0 ?_)
      simp only [Sen.form, Form.within_none]
      decide

end BoundedLob

module

public import BoundedLob.Agents.Candidates
public import BoundedLob.Checker.Parse
public import BoundedLob.Checker.Worlds

/-!
# Agents that search for proofs

`run n a b` plays the agent with source `a` against the agent with source `b` at the budget
parameter `k = n`: it reads `a` with `opp := b` and `me := a`, and decides each box `□_t σ` by
`search`, which looks for a proof of `σ` with at most `t` characters in three stages:

1. if `σ` fails at one of the worlds `0, …, worldDepth - 1` of the chain, there is no proof of
   any length;
2. otherwise it checks the candidates from `candidates`;
3. otherwise it checks every certificate string of at most `t - |σ|` characters.

The first two stages only make it faster. `search_spec`: `search t σ` is exactly "`σ` has a proof
of at most `t` characters", and `run_spec`: `run n a b` is exactly the truth of `coop a b`. The
third stage lists every string, so it is a guarantee and not a practical search. For DUPOC
against itself, `dupoc_fast` proves that the second stage decides; the tournament in `Play`
checks it for each search it plays.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BoundedLob

open Form

/-- How many worlds `search` tries, `0` to `5`. A heuristic: the complete search keeps the
answer exact when the worlds find nothing. -/
def worldDepth : ℕ := 6

/-- `c` is a proof of `σ` with at most `t` characters. -/
def affordable (t : ℕ) (σ : Sen) (c : Cert) : Bool := decide (len c σ ≤ t) && check c σ

/-- The complete search over strings. -/
def exhaustive (t : ℕ) (σ : Sen) : Bool :=
  (strings (t - σ.size)).any fun s =>
    match Cert.parse s with
    | some c => affordable t σ c
    | none => false

/-- Some candidate is a proof of `σ` with at most `t` characters. -/
def byCandidate (t : ℕ) (σ : Sen) : Bool := (candidates σ).any (affordable t σ)

/-- Bounded proof search: is there a proof of `σ` with at most `t` characters? -/
def search (t : ℕ) (σ : Sen) : Bool :=
  if refuted worldDepth σ.form then false
  else if byCandidate t σ then true
  else exhaustive t σ

/-- `affordable` as a proposition. -/
theorem affordable_iff {t : ℕ} {σ : Sen} {c : Cert} :
    affordable t σ c = true ↔ check c σ = true ∧ len c σ ≤ t := by
  simp [affordable, and_comm]

/-- The complete search finds a proof exactly when there is one. -/
theorem exhaustive_spec {t : ℕ} {σ : Sen} : exhaustive t σ = true ↔ Provable t σ := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨s, -, hs⟩ := List.any_eq_true.1 h
    split at hs
    · rename_i c _
      exact ⟨c, affordable_iff.1 hs⟩
    · simp at hs
  · rintro ⟨c, hc, hl⟩
    refine List.any_eq_true.2 ⟨c.text, mem_strings ?_ (fun _ h => Cert.text_subset c h), ?_⟩
    · have : c.text.length = c.size := rfl
      simp only [len] at hl
      omega
    · simp [Cert.parse_text, affordable_iff, hc, hl]

/-- **The search is exact**: `search t σ` holds exactly when `σ` has a proof of at most `t`
characters. -/
theorem search_spec {t : ℕ} {σ : Sen} : search t σ = true ↔ Provable t σ := by
  unfold search
  split
  · rename_i hr
    simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, false_iff]
    exact not_provable_of_refuted hr t
  · split
    · rename_i hh
      simp only [true_iff]
      obtain ⟨c, -, hc⟩ := List.any_eq_true.1 hh
      exact ⟨c, affordable_iff.1 hc⟩
    · exact exhaustive_spec

/-- Read a formula as an agent does, deciding each box by `search`. -/
def eval (n : ℕ) : Form → Option (Form × Form) → Bool
  | .bot, _ => false
  | .imp φ ψ, e => !eval n φ e || eval n ψ e
  | .iff φ ψ, e => eval n φ e == eval n ψ e
  | .box t φ, e => search (t.eval id n) (.inst n (φ.within e))
  | .coop a b, _ => !(a.isPlaceholder || b.isPlaceholder) && eval n a (some (b, a))
  | .opp, _ => false
  | .me, _ => false
  | .diag g p, e => !search (g.eval id n) (.inst n ((Form.diag g p).within e)) || eval n p e

/-- The agent with source `a` against the agent with source `b`, at `k = n`: `true` is
cooperation. -/
def run (n : ℕ) (a b : Form) : Bool := eval n (.coop a b) none

/-- `eval` computes the truth of a formula. -/
theorem eval_spec (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ (φ : Form) (e : Option (Form × Form)), eval n φ e = true ↔ holds n φ e
  | .bot, _ => by simp [eval, holds]
  | .imp φ ψ, e => by
    rw [eval, holds, ← eval_spec n φ e, ← eval_spec n ψ e]
    cases eval n φ e <;> simp
  | .iff φ ψ, e => by
    rw [eval, holds, ← eval_spec n φ e, ← eval_spec n ψ e]
    cases eval n φ e <;> cases eval n ψ e <;> simp
  | .box t φ, e => by rw [eval, holds, search_spec]
  | .coop a b, _ => by
    rw [eval, holds, ← eval_spec n a (some (b, a))]
    simp
  | .opp, _ => by simp [eval, holds]
  | .me, _ => by simp [eval, holds]
  | .diag g p, e => by
    rw [eval, holds, ← eval_spec n p e, ← search_spec]
    cases search (g.eval id n) (.inst n ((Form.diag g p).within e)) <;> simp

/-- **`run` plays exactly what the source says.** -/
theorem run_spec (n : ℕ) (a b : Form) : run n a b = true ↔ holds n (.coop a b) none :=
  eval_spec n _ none

/-- For a guarded source, `run` is the truth of the source with the two sources filled in. -/
theorem run_iff_holds_fill {n : ℕ} {a b : Form} (ha : a.isPlaceholder = false)
    (hb : b.isPlaceholder = false) (hg : a.guarded = true) :
    run n a b = true ↔ holds n (a.fill b a) none := by
  rw [run_spec, holds_coop ha hb hg]

end BoundedLob

module

public import BoundedLob.Checker.Rules
public import BoundedLob.Checker.Truth
public import BoundedLob.Theory.Lob

/-!
# The checker has Critch's properties

`calculus` is the proof system of `check` as a `System`: every field of the structure, which the
bounded Löb theorem takes as given, is here a theorem about the checker. Its proofs within `n`
characters are `Provable n`. The constants are `iffCost = 1`, `distCost = 0` (implication
distribution), `instCost = Cost.inst = 4` (quantifier distribution) and
`expansion = Cost.expansion = 2`. Inner necessitation is given here with the guard `2^|x|`,
which works for every bound; the certificate builders use the often smaller `Bound.fitGuard`.
Monotonicity uses the guard of `Bound.guard`.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BoundedLob

open Form

/-- The checker as a proof system with Critch's properties. -/
def calculus : System id where
  Sen := Sen
  Pred := Form
  imp := imp
  iff := iff
  box := box
  above := Sen.all
  ProvesIn := Provable
  mp := by
    rintro a b φ ψ ⟨_, c, hc, -⟩ ⟨_, d, hd, -⟩

    rintro a b φ ψ χ ⟨_, c, hc, -⟩ ⟨_, d, hd, -⟩

      simp [Cert.trans, check, Sen.withForm, Sen.form, hc, hd], le_rfl⟩

    rintro a b φ ψ χ ⟨_, c, hc, -⟩ ⟨_, d, hd, -⟩
    exact ⟨_, Cert.contract φ ψ χ (.raise a c) (.raise b d), by
      simp [Cert.contract, check, Sen.withForm, Sen.form, hc, hd], le_rfl⟩

    rintro a φ ψ χ ⟨_, c, hc, -⟩
    exact ⟨_, Cert.impMono φ ψ χ c, by
      simp [Cert.impMono, check, Sen.withForm, Sen.form, hc], le_rfl⟩

  iff_forward := by
    rintro n a φ ψ ⟨c, hc, hl⟩
    refine ⟨.iffL c, by simp [check, Sen.withForm, Sen.form, hc], ?_⟩
    simp only [len_all, Form.size_imp, Form.size_iff, Cert.size_iffL] at hl ⊢

    rintro n a φ ψ ⟨c, hc, -⟩

    rintro N a φ ⟨c, hc, hl⟩

/-- What `calculus` proves about every `k > a` is true for every `k > a`. -/
theorem calculus_sound {a : ℕ} {φ : Form} (h : calculus.Proves (calculus.above a φ)) :
    ∀ k > a, holds k φ none := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := h
  exact Provable.sound (t := t) (σ := .all a φ) ht

/-- A checked certificate for `∀ k > a, φ` makes `calculus` prove it. -/
theorem proves_of_check {a : ℕ} {φ : Form} (c : Cert) (h : check c (.all a φ) = true) :
    calculus.Proves (calculus.above a φ) := ⟨_, c, h, le_rfl⟩

/-- A uniform proof gives an affordable proof at every large instance: instantiating it costs
the numeral for `k` and the two three-character wrappers of `inst`. -/
theorem provable_of_proves {K : ℕ} {φ : Form} (h : calculus.Proves (calculus.above K φ)) :
    ∃ K', ∀ k > K', Provable k (.inst k φ) := by
  obtain ⟨_, c, hc, -⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨Ke, hKe⟩ :=
    growsFasterThanLog_id.eventually_le_div (φ.size + Nat.log 2 K + c.size + 6) 1 (by decide)
  refine ⟨max K Ke, fun k hk => ⟨.inst K c, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · simp only [check, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq]
    exact ⟨by omega, hc⟩
  · have := hKe k (by omega)
    simp only [len_inst, Cert.size_inst, id, Nat.div_one] at this ⊢
    omega

module

public import BoundedLob.Checker.Check

/-!
# What the sentences say, and soundness

`holds n φ e` is the truth of `φ` at `k = n`. A box is true when the checker accepts some
certificate within its budget, so truth refers to the checker and never the other way round.
`coop a b` is true when the source `a`, read against `b`, is true; reading a source fills its
placeholders (`e = some (b, a)`), and since every placeholder of a guarded source sits under a
box, reading never needs the truth of another `coop` with a placeholder.

`holds` is defined for every formula, not only guarded sources. A bare placeholder, or a `coop`
outside a box with a placeholder argument, is false; such formulas never occur in the agents'
sources, and the checker's rule for sources (`prog`) only accepts guarded ones.

`sound`: every sentence with a checked certificate is true.

Three readings of a formula appear in turn. `holds` is the intended one, with a box read as
bounded provability. `worlds` (in `Worlds`) forgets the budgets: a sentence false at some world
has no proof, but one true at the worlds an agent tests may still have none. `eval` (in
`Agents/Search`) computes `holds` by proof search (`eval_spec`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BoundedLob

open Form

/-- Truth at `k = n`, while reading the match `e` (`none` for a plain sentence). -/
def holds (n : ℕ) : Form → Option (Form × Form) → Prop
  | .bot, _ => False
  | .imp φ ψ, e => holds n φ e → holds n ψ e
  | .iff φ ψ, e => (holds n φ e ↔ holds n ψ e)
  | .box t φ, e => Provable (t.eval id n) (.inst n (φ.within e))
  | .coop a b, _ => (a.isPlaceholder || b.isPlaceholder) = false ∧ holds n a (some (b, a))
  | .opp, _ => False
  | .me, _ => False
  | .diag g p, e => Provable (g.eval id n) (.inst n ((Form.diag g p).within e)) → holds n p e

/-- A true sentence: a guarded universal is true at every `k` past its guard. -/
def Sen.holds : Sen → Prop
  | .all a φ => ∀ k > a, BoundedLob.holds k φ none
  | .inst n φ => BoundedLob.holds n φ none

/-- Reading a guarded source in a match is the same as reading its filled text. -/
theorem holds_fill {o m : Form} (ho : o.isPlaceholder = false) (hm : m.isPlaceholder = false)
    (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ (a : Form), a.guarded = true → ∀ e, holds n (a.fill o m) e ↔ holds n a (some (o, m))
  | .bot, _, _ => Iff.rfl
  | .imp φ ψ, h, e => by
    simp only [guarded, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
    simp only [fill, holds, holds_fill ho hm n φ h.1 e, holds_fill ho hm n ψ h.2 e]
  | .iff φ ψ, h, e => by
    simp only [guarded, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
    simp only [fill, holds, holds_fill ho hm n φ h.1 e, holds_fill ho hm n ψ h.2 e]
  | .box t φ, _, e => by
    simp only [fill, holds]
    rw [Form.within_fill ho hm]
    rfl
  | .coop a b, h, e => by
    simp only [guarded, Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.not_eq_true'] at h
    simp only [fill, holds, Form.fillArg_self h.1, Form.fillArg_self h.2]
  | .opp, h, _ => by simp [guarded] at h
  | .me, h, _ => by simp [guarded] at h
  | .diag g p, h, e => by
    simp only [guarded] at h
    have hw : (Form.diag g (p.fill o m)).within e = Form.diag g (p.fill o m) :=
      Form.within_fill ho hm (Form.diag g p) e
    simp only [fill, holds]
    rw [hw, holds_fill ho hm n p h e]
    rfl

/-! ### Soundness -/

namespace Sen

/-- A formula true at every `k` makes every sentence about it true. -/
theorem holds_of_valid {σ : Sen} (hv : ∀ n, BoundedLob.holds n σ.form none) : σ.holds := by
  cases σ <;> simp_all [Sen.holds, Sen.form]

/-- Modus ponens for true sentences under the same guard or instance. -/
theorem holds_mp {σ : Sen} {φ : Form} (h₁ : (σ.withForm (imp φ σ.form)).holds)
    (h₂ : (σ.withForm φ).holds) :
    σ.holds := by
  cases σ with
  | all a ψ => exact fun k hk => h₁ k hk (h₂ k hk)
  | inst n ψ => exact h₁ h₂

/-- A pointwise implication between the formulas carries a true sentence over. -/
theorem holds_of_withForm {σ : Sen} {φ : Form} (hσ : ∀ n, BoundedLob.holds n φ none →
    BoundedLob.holds n σ.form none) (h : (σ.withForm φ).holds) : σ.holds := by
  cases σ with
  | all a ψ => exact fun k hk => hσ k (h k hk)
  | inst n ψ => exact hσ n h

end Sen

/-- Implication distribution at one instance. -/
theorem provable_dist {n x y : ℕ} {φ ψ : Form} (h₁ : Provable x (.inst n (imp φ ψ)))
    (h₂ : Provable y (.inst n φ)) : Provable (x + y) (.inst n ψ) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hcl⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨d, hd, hdl⟩ := h₂
  refine ⟨.mp φ c d, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [check, Sen.withForm, Sen.form, hc, hd]
  · simp only [len_inst, Form.size_imp, Cert.size_mp] at hcl hdl ⊢
    omega

/-- Inner necessitation at one instance, once the text of `x` fits in `x(n)` or in `lg n`.
Boxing a proof of `φ` costs the text of `x` and two characters, the box of the formula and the
`nec` of the certificate, and the hypothesis pays for them out of a second copy of `x(n)`. -/
theorem provable_four {n : ℕ} {x : Bound} {φ : Form}
    (hn : x.size + 2 ≤ x.eval id n ∨ x.size ≤ Nat.log 2 n)
    (h : Provable (x.eval id n) (.inst n φ)) :
    Provable (2 * x.eval id n) (.inst n (box x φ)) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hcl⟩ := h
  refine ⟨.nec c, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [check, hc, hcl]
  · have hφ := φ.size_pos
    have hc' := c.size_pos
    simp only [len_inst, Form.size_box, Cert.size_nec] at hcl ⊢
    omega

/-- **Soundness.** A sentence with a checked certificate is true. -/
theorem sound : ∀ (c : Cert) (σ : Sen), check c σ = true → σ.holds
  | .axK, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i φ ψ φ' hf
      simp only [beq_iff_eq] at h
      subst h
      exact Sen.holds_of_valid fun n => by rw [hf]; exact fun a _ => a
    · simp at h
  | .axS, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i φ ψ χ φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ χ₁ hf
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨h₁, h₂⟩, h₃⟩, h₄⟩ := h
      subst h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄
      exact Sen.holds_of_valid fun n => by
        rw [hf]; exact fun a b c => a c (b c)
    · simp at h
  | .axDN, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i φ φ' hf
      simp only [beq_iff_eq] at h
      subst h
      exact Sen.holds_of_valid fun n => by
        rw [hf]; exact fun a => Classical.byContradiction a
    · simp at h
  | .iffL c, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i φ ψ hf
      exact Sen.holds_of_withForm (φ := iff φ ψ) (fun n hv => by rw [hf]; exact hv.1) (sound c _ h)
    · simp at h
  | .iffR c, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i ψ φ hf
      exact Sen.holds_of_withForm (φ := iff φ ψ) (fun n hv => by rw [hf]; exact hv.2) (sound c _ h)
    · simp at h
  | .iffI c d, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i φ ψ hf
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h
      have h₁ := sound c _ h.1
      have h₂ := sound d _ h.2
      cases σ with
      | all a χ =>
        simp only [Sen.form] at hf
        subst hf
        exact fun k hk => ⟨h₁ k hk, h₂ k hk⟩
      | inst n χ =>
        simp only [Sen.form] at hf
        subst hf
        exact ⟨h₁, h₂⟩
    · simp at h
  | .mp φ c d, σ, h => by
    simp only [check, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
    exact Sen.holds_mp (sound c _ h.1) (sound d _ h.2)
  | .raise a c, σ, h => by
    cases σ with
    | all b φ =>
      simp only [check, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      exact fun k hk => sound c _ h.2 k (by omega)
    | inst _ _ => simp [check] at h
  | .inst a c, σ, h => by
    cases σ with
    | inst n φ =>
      simp only [check, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      exact sound c _ h.2 n h.1
    | all _ _ => simp [check] at h
  | .qd c, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i a M φ
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      intro k hk
      refine ⟨.inst a c, ?_, ?_⟩
      · simp [check, hk, h.2]
      · simp only [len_inst, len_all, Cert.size_inst, Bound.eval, Form.within_none, Cost.inst]
          at h ⊢
        omega
    · simp at h
  | .nec c, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i n t φ
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      exact ⟨c, h.2, h.1⟩
    · simp at h
  | .dist, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i x φ ψ y φ₁ z ψ₁ hf
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨h₁, h₂⟩, h₃⟩ := h
      subst h₁ h₂ h₃
      exact Sen.holds_of_valid fun n => by
        rw [hf]
        intro hx hy
        have := provable_dist hx hy
        simp only [holds, Form.within_none, Bound.eval, Nat.add_zero]
        exact this
    · simp at h
  | .four, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i a x φ y x₁ φ₁
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨h₁, h₂⟩, h₃⟩, h₄⟩ := h
      subst h₁ h₂ h₃
      intro k hk hx
      have := provable_four (Bound.fits_spec h₄ hk) hx
      simp only [holds, Form.within_none, Bound.eval, Cost.expansion]
      exact this
    · rename_i n x φ y x₁ φ₁
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨h₁, h₂⟩, h₃⟩, h₄⟩ := h
      subst h₁ h₂ h₃
      intro hx
      have := provable_four (Or.inl h₄) hx
      simp only [holds, Form.within_none, Bound.eval, Cost.expansion]
      exact this
    · simp at h
  | .mono, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i a x φ y φ₁
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ := h
      subst h₁
      split at h₂
      · rename_i K hK
        simp only [decide_eq_true_eq] at h₂
        intro k hk hx
        exact hx.mono (Bound.le_of_guard hK k (by omega))
      · simp at h₂
    · rename_i n x φ y φ₁
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ := h
      subst h₁
      exact fun hx => hx.mono h₂
    · simp at h
  | .diag, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i g p g₁ g₂ p₁ p₂ hf
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨h₁, h₂⟩, h₃⟩, h₄⟩ := h
      subst h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄
      exact Sen.holds_of_valid fun n => by
        rw [hf]
        exact Iff.rfl
    · simp at h
  | .prog, σ, h => by
    simp only [check] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i a b φ hf
      simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.not_eq_true', beq_iff_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨ha, hb⟩, hg⟩, hφ⟩ := h
      subst hφ
      exact Sen.holds_of_valid fun n => by
        rw [hf]
        simp only [holds, ha, hb, Bool.or_self, true_and]
        exact (holds_fill hb ha n a hg none).symm
    · simp at h

/-- What has a proof of some length is true. -/
theorem Provable.sound {t : ℕ} {σ : Sen} (h : Provable t σ) : σ.holds :=
  let ⟨c, hc, _⟩ := h
  BoundedLob.sound c σ hc

/-- A match is true exactly when the filled source is. -/
theorem holds_coop {n : ℕ} {a b : Form} (ha : a.isPlaceholder = false)
    (hb : b.isPlaceholder = false) (hg : a.guarded = true) :
    holds n (coop a b) none ↔ holds n (a.fill b a) none := by
  simp only [holds, ha, hb, Bool.or_self, true_and]
  exact (holds_fill hb ha n a hg none).symm

end BoundedLob

module

public import BoundedLob.Theory.Dupoc

/-!
# DUPOC against DIMCID

Open Problem 6 of Critch, Dennis and Russell (arXiv:2208.07006) asks for the outcome of DUPOC(k)
against DIMCID(k). DIMCID ("defect if my cooperation implies defection") defects exactly when it
finds a proof, of at most `k` characters, of its guard

  `G(k)`: if DIMCID(k) cooperates with DUPOC(k), then DUPOC(k) defects against DIMCID(k).

The answer is mutual defection for every large `k`, in any sound system with these properties
that proves the agents' code and the propositional fact `¬A → (A → B)`. The bounded Löb theorem
is applied to DIMCID's own defection `d(k)`, for a budget `f(k)` that may be anything growing
faster than `lg k` (the agents use `f(k) = k`):

* `d(k) → G(k)` is ex falso: "DIMCID cooperates" is false once DIMCID defects, and anything
  follows from it. The system has one proof of it, of some length `N`, for every positive `k`.
* Distributing the box, a proof of `d(k)` within `⌊f(k)/2⌋` characters gives a proof of `G(k)`
  within `⌊f(k)/2⌋ + C + 2N + lg k + c`, which is at most `f(k)` once `k` is large
  (`System.box_imp_of_gap`). DIMCID's code turns any such proof into `d(k)`.
* So the system proves `∀ k > k₁, □_{⌊f(k)/2⌋} d(k) → d(k)`, and `pblt` with that budget proves
  `d(k)` for every large `k` (`System.self_fulfilling`).
* DUPOC cooperates only on a checked proof that DIMCID cooperates (`Checker.not_exploited`), and
  DIMCID defects, so DUPOC defects as well (`dupoc_vs_dimcid`).

Critch, Dennis and Russell prove `outcome(CUPOD(k), DIMCID(k)) = (D, D)` (their Theorem 5.5(b))
with the bounded Löb theorem applied to the whole outcome. Applying it to DIMCID's move alone
avoids needing any short proof of DUPOC's failed search; DUPOC's move then follows from
soundness.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BoundedLob

namespace System

variable {f : ℕ → ℕ} (S : System f)

/-- **Self-fulfilling statements.** If `f` grows faster than `lg k` and the system proves `d → G`
and `□_f G → d` for every positive `k`, it proves `d` beyond some `k₂`. For DIMCID, `d` is its
defection and `G` its guard. -/
theorem self_fulfilling (hf : GrowsFasterThanLog f) {d G : S.Pred}
    (exfalso : S.Proves (S.above 0 (S.imp d G)))
    (code : S.Proves (S.above 0 (S.imp (S.box .f G) d))) :
    ∃ k₂, S.Proves (S.above k₂ d) := by
  -- Half the budget leaves room for the overhead of turning a proof of `d` into one of `G`.
  have gap : ∀ c, ∃ K, ∀ k > K,
      (Bound.div .f 2).eval f k + Nat.log 2 k + c ≤ Bound.f.eval f k := by
    intro c
    obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := hf.eventually_le_div c 2 (by omega)
    refine ⟨K, fun k hk => ?_⟩
    have := hK k hk
    simp only [Bound.eval]
    omega
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := S.box_imp_of_gap gap exfalso code
  exact S.pblt (.div .f 2) (hf.div 2 (by omega)) hK

end System

/-- **Open Problem 6.** DUPOC(k) against DIMCID(k) ends in mutual defection for every large `k`.

`S` is a system with Critch's properties and budget symbol `f(k) = k`, in which `defects` says
"DIMCID(k) defects against DUPOC(k)" and `guard` is DIMCID's guard. The hypotheses are what the
setting of Critch, Dennis and Russell provides: `exfalso` (a program has one output), `code`
(DIMCID defects whenever its guard has a proof of at most `k` characters), soundness of `S` for
the sentences `∀ k > k₂, defects(k)`, and DUPOC as an executable search over a sound checker. -/
theorem dupoc_vs_dimcid {G : Game} {P : Checker G} (sound : P.Sound)
    {cands : ℕ → G.Source → G.Source → List P.Proof} {dupoc : ℕ → G.Source}
    (hd : P.IsDupoc cands dupoc) (dimcid : ℕ → G.Source) (S : System id) (defects guard : S.Pred)
    (exfalso : S.Proves (S.above 0 (S.imp defects guard)))
    (code : S.Proves (S.above 0 (S.imp (S.box .f guard) defects)))
    (true_of : ∀ k₂, S.Proves (S.above k₂ defects) →
      ∀ k > k₂, G.run (dimcid k) (dupoc k) = false) :
    ∃ k₂, ∀ k > k₂, G.run (dupoc k) (dimcid k) = false ∧ G.run (dimcid k) (dupoc k) = false := by
  obtain ⟨k₂, h⟩ := S.self_fulfilling growsFasterThanLog_id exfalso code
  refine ⟨k₂, fun k hk => ⟨?_, true_of k₂ h k hk⟩⟩
  cases hrun : G.run (dupoc k) (dimcid k)
  · rfl
  · have := Checker.not_exploited sound hd hrun
    rw [true_of k₂ h k hk] at this
    exact absurd this Bool.false_ne_true

end BoundedLob
